import json
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import scipy.stats as stats
from typing import Dict, List, Tuple, Optional, Any, Union
from dataclasses import dataclass, asdict
from pathlib import Path
from datetime import datetime
import logging
import argparse
from collections import defaultdict, Counter

from sklearn.metrics import cohen_kappa_score, confusion_matrix
import krippendorff
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns


@dataclass
class AnnotationData:
    &quot;&quot;&quot;Structured representation of annotation data.&quot;&quot;&quot;
    annotator_id: str
    file_path: str
    relevance_score: int  # 1-5 scale
    confidence_score: int  # 1-5 scale
    reasoning: str
    annotation_timestamp: str
    task_batch: str
    repository: str


@dataclass
class ReliabilityAnalysis:
    &quot;&quot;&quot;Comprehensive reliability analysis results.&quot;&quot;&quot;
    cohens_kappa_binary: float
    cohens_kappa_weighted: float
    krippendorffs_alpha: float
    agreement_percentage: float
    interpretation: str
    quality_gate_passed: bool
    statistical_significance: Dict[str, Any]
    confidence_intervals: Dict[str, Tuple[float, float]]
    bias_analysis: Dict[str, Any]
    annotator_consistency: Dict[str, float]


class InterRaterReliabilityCalculator:
    &quot;&quot;&quot;
    Calculate comprehensive inter-rater reliability statistics for annotation quality validation.
    
    Implements academic-grade statistical validation with multiple reliability measures
    and comprehensive bias detection as required by ICSE standards.
    &quot;&quot;&quot;
    
    def __init__(self, min_kappa_threshold: float = 0.70, 
                 confidence_level: float = 0.95,
                 output_dir: Optional[Path] = None):
        &quot;&quot;&quot;Initialize reliability calculator with academic standards.&quot;&quot;&quot;
        self.min_kappa_threshold = min_kappa_threshold
        self.confidence_level = confidence_level
        self.output_dir = Path(output_dir) if output_dir else Path.cwd()
        
        # Setup logging
        self.setup_logging()
        
        # Statistical constants
        self.kappa_interpretation_thresholds = {
            0.81: &quot;almost_perfect&quot;,
            0.61: &quot;substantial&quot;, 
            0.41: &quot;moderate&quot;,
            0.21: &quot;fair&quot;,
            0.01: &quot;slight&quot;,
            -1.0: &quot;poor&quot;
        }
        
    def setup_logging(self) -&gt; None:
        &quot;&quot;&quot;Setup logging for reliability analysis audit trail.&quot;&quot;&quot;
        log_file = self.output_dir / &#x27;reliability_analysis.log&#x27;
        self.output_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        
        logging.basicConfig(
            level=logging.INFO,
            format=&#x27;%(asctime)s - %(name)s - %(levelname)s - %(message)s&#x27;,
            handlers=[
                logging.FileHandler(log_file),
                logging.StreamHandler()
            ]
        )
        self.logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
        
    def load_annotations(self, annotation_file: Path) -&gt; List[AnnotationData]:
        &quot;&quot;&quot;Load and validate annotation data from JSON file.&quot;&quot;&quot;
        self.logger.info(f&quot;Loading annotations from {annotation_file}&quot;)
        
        with open(annotation_file, &#x27;r&#x27;) as f:
            data = json.load(f)
            
        annotations = []
        for item in data.get(&#x27;annotations&#x27;, []):
            try:
                annotation = AnnotationData(
                    annotator_id=item[&#x27;annotator_id&#x27;],
                    file_path=item[&#x27;file_path&#x27;],
                    relevance_score=item[&#x27;relevance_score&#x27;],
                    confidence_score=item[&#x27;confidence_score&#x27;],
                    reasoning=item[&#x27;reasoning&#x27;],
                    annotation_timestamp=item[&#x27;annotation_timestamp&#x27;],
                    task_batch=item.get(&#x27;task_batch&#x27;, &#x27;default&#x27;),
                    repository=item.get(&#x27;repository&#x27;, &#x27;unknown&#x27;)
                )
                annotations.append(annotation)
            except KeyError as e:
                self.logger.error(f&quot;Missing field in annotation data: {e}&quot;)
                continue
                
        self.logger.info(f&quot;Loaded {len(annotations)} annotations&quot;)
        return annotations
        
    def organize_annotations_by_item(self, annotations: List[AnnotationData]) -&gt; Dict[str, Dict[str, AnnotationData]]:
        &quot;&quot;&quot;Organize annotations by item (file) for reliability calculation.&quot;&quot;&quot;
        organized = defaultdict(dict)
        
        for annotation in annotations:
            item_key = f&quot;{annotation.repository}::{annotation.file_path}&quot;
            organized[item_key][annotation.annotator_id] = annotation
            
        # Filter to items with multiple annotations
        multi_annotated = {
            item: annotators for item, annotators in organized.items()
            if len(annotators) &gt;= 2
        }
        
        self.logger.info(f&quot;Found {len(multi_annotated)} items with multiple annotations&quot;)
        return multi_annotated
        
    def calculate_cohens_kappa(self, annotations_dict: Dict[str, Dict[str, AnnotationData]]) -&gt; Dict[str, float]:
        &quot;&quot;&quot;Calculate Cohen&#x27;s kappa for all annotator pairs.&quot;&quot;&quot;
        annotators = set()
        for item_annotations in annotations_dict.values():
            annotators.update(item_annotations.keys())
        annotators = list(annotators)
        
        if len(annotators) &lt; 2:
            self.logger.error(&quot;Need at least 2 annotators for kappa calculation&quot;)
            return {}
            
        kappa_results = {}
        
        # Calculate kappa for all pairs
        for i in range(len(annotators)):
            for j in range(i + 1, len(annotators)):
                annotator_a, annotator_b = annotators[i], annotators[j]
                pair_key = f&quot;{annotator_a}_vs_{annotator_b}&quot;
                
                # Extract paired ratings
                ratings_a, ratings_b = [], []
                for item, item_annotations in annotations_dict.items():
                    if annotator_a in item_annotations and annotator_b in item_annotations:
                        ratings_a.append(item_annotations[annotator_a].relevance_score)
                        ratings_b.append(item_annotations[annotator_b].relevance_score)
                
                if len(ratings_a) &lt; 5:  # Minimum sample size
                    self.logger.warning(f&quot;Insufficient paired annotations for {pair_key}: {len(ratings_a)}&quot;)
                    continue
                    
                # Binary kappa (relevant vs not relevant, threshold at 3)
                binary_a = [1 if score &gt;= 3 else 0 for score in ratings_a]
                binary_b = [1 if score &gt;= 3 else 0 for score in ratings_b]
                
                kappa_binary = cohen_kappa_score(binary_a, binary_b)
                
                # Weighted kappa for ordinal scale
                kappa_weighted = cohen_kappa_score(ratings_a, ratings_b, weights=&#x27;linear&#x27;)
                
                kappa_results[f&quot;{pair_key}_binary&quot;] = kappa_binary
                kappa_results[f&quot;{pair_key}_weighted&quot;] = kappa_weighted
                
                self.logger.info(f&quot;Cohen&#x27;s κ for {pair_key}: binary={kappa_binary:.3f}, weighted={kappa_weighted:.3f}&quot;)
                
        return kappa_results
        
    def calculate_krippendorffs_alpha(self, annotations_dict: Dict[str, Dict[str, AnnotationData]]) -&gt; float:
        &quot;&quot;&quot;Calculate Krippendorff&#x27;s alpha for multiple annotators.&quot;&quot;&quot;
        
        # Prepare data matrix: annotators x items
        annotators = set()
        items = list(annotations_dict.keys())
        
        for item_annotations in annotations_dict.values():
            annotators.update(item_annotations.keys())
        annotators = sorted(list(annotators))
        
        # Create reliability data matrix
        reliability_data = []
        for annotator in annotators:
            annotator_ratings = []
            for item in items:
                if annotator in annotations_dict[item]:
                    rating = annotations_dict[item][annotator].relevance_score
                else:
                    rating = np.nan  # Missing value
                annotator_ratings.append(rating)
            reliability_data.append(annotator_ratings)
            
        # Calculate Krippendorff&#x27;s alpha
        try:
            alpha = krippendorff.alpha(reliability_data, level_of_measurement=&#x27;ordinal&#x27;)
            self.logger.info(f&quot;Krippendorff&#x27;s α: {alpha:.3f}&quot;)
            return alpha
        except Exception as e:
            self.logger.error(f&quot;Failed to calculate Krippendorff&#x27;s alpha: {e}&quot;)
            return 0.0
            
    def calculate_agreement_percentage(self, annotations_dict: Dict[str, Dict[str, AnnotationData]], 
                                     tolerance: int = 1) -&gt; float:
        &quot;&quot;&quot;Calculate percentage agreement within tolerance.&quot;&quot;&quot;
        total_comparisons = 0
        agreements = 0
        
        for item, item_annotations in annotations_dict.items():
            if len(item_annotations) &lt; 2:
                continue
                
            # Get all ratings for this item
            ratings = [ann.relevance_score for ann in item_annotations.values()]
            
            # Count pairwise agreements within tolerance
            for i in range(len(ratings)):
                for j in range(i + 1, len(ratings)):
                    total_comparisons += 1
                    if abs(ratings[i] - ratings[j]) &lt;= tolerance:
                        agreements += 1
                        
        if total_comparisons == 0:
            return 0.0
            
        agreement_percentage = (agreements / total_comparisons) * 100
        self.logger.info(f&quot;Agreement percentage (tolerance={tolerance}): {agreement_percentage:.1f}%&quot;)
        return agreement_percentage
        
    def interpret_kappa(self, kappa: float) -&gt; str:
        &quot;&quot;&quot;Interpret kappa value according to Landis &amp; Koch (1977).&quot;&quot;&quot;
        for threshold, interpretation in self.kappa_interpretation_thresholds.items():
            if kappa &gt;= threshold:
                return interpretation
        return &quot;poor&quot;
        
    def calculate_confidence_intervals(self, annotations_dict: Dict[str, Dict[str, AnnotationData]],
                                     kappa_values: Dict[str, float]) -&gt; Dict[str, Tuple[float, float]]:
        &quot;&quot;&quot;Calculate confidence intervals for kappa values.&quot;&quot;&quot;
        confidence_intervals = {}
        
        # Simplified CI calculation - in production would use bootstrap
        for kappa_name, kappa_value in kappa_values.items():
            if &#x27;binary&#x27; in kappa_name:
                # Approximate standard error for binary kappa
                n_items = len([item for item in annotations_dict.keys()
                             if len(annotations_dict[item]) &gt;= 2])
                se = np.sqrt((kappa_value * (1 - kappa_value)) / n_items) if n_items &gt; 0 else 0.1
                
                # 95% confidence interval
                z_score = 1.96  # 95% CI
                ci_lower = max(-1.0, kappa_value - z_score * se)
                ci_upper = min(1.0, kappa_value + z_score * se)
                
                confidence_intervals[kappa_name] = (ci_lower, ci_upper)
                
        return confidence_intervals
        
    def detect_systematic_bias(self, annotations: List[AnnotationData]) -&gt; Dict[str, Any]:
        &quot;&quot;&quot;Detect systematic biases in annotation patterns.&quot;&quot;&quot;
        bias_analysis = {
            &#x27;annotator_bias&#x27;: {},
            &#x27;file_type_bias&#x27;: {},
            &#x27;repository_bias&#x27;: {},
            &#x27;temporal_bias&#x27;: {},
            &#x27;confidence_alignment_bias&#x27;: {}
        }
        
        # Annotator-specific bias
        annotator_stats = defaultdict(list)
        for annotation in annotations:
            annotator_stats[annotation.annotator_id].append(annotation.relevance_score)
            
        for annotator_id, scores in annotator_stats.items():
            bias_analysis[&#x27;annotator_bias&#x27;][annotator_id] = {
                &#x27;mean_score&#x27;: np.mean(scores),
                &#x27;std_score&#x27;: np.std(scores),
                &#x27;score_distribution&#x27;: dict(Counter(scores))
            }
            
        # File type bias
        file_type_stats = defaultdict(list)
        for annotation in annotations:
            file_ext = Path(annotation.file_path).suffix.lower()
            file_type_stats[file_ext or &#x27;no_extension&#x27;].append(annotation.relevance_score)
            
        for file_type, scores in file_type_stats.items():
            if len(scores) &gt;= 5:  # Minimum sample size
                bias_analysis[&#x27;file_type_bias&#x27;][file_type] = {
                    &#x27;mean_score&#x27;: np.mean(scores),
                    &#x27;count&#x27;: len(scores)
                }
                
        # Confidence-score alignment bias
        confidence_relevance_pairs = [(ann.confidence_score, ann.relevance_score) for ann in annotations]
        if confidence_relevance_pairs:
            confidence_scores, relevance_scores = zip(*confidence_relevance_pairs)
            correlation = np.corrcoef(confidence_scores, relevance_scores)[0, 1]
            bias_analysis[&#x27;confidence_alignment_bias&#x27;] = {
                &#x27;correlation&#x27;: correlation,
                &#x27;alignment_quality&#x27;: &#x27;good&#x27; if correlation &gt; 0.5 else &#x27;poor&#x27;
            }
            
        return bias_analysis
        
    def calculate_annotator_consistency(self, annotations_dict: Dict[str, Dict[str, AnnotationData]]) -&gt; Dict[str, float]:
        &quot;&quot;&quot;Calculate individual annotator consistency metrics.&quot;&quot;&quot;
        annotator_consistency = {}
        
        # Get annotator-specific data
        annotator_data = defaultdict(list)
        for item, item_annotations in annotations_dict.items():
            for annotator_id, annotation in item_annotations.items():
                annotator_data[annotator_id].append({
                    &#x27;relevance&#x27;: annotation.relevance_score,
                    &#x27;confidence&#x27;: annotation.confidence_score,
                    &#x27;reasoning_length&#x27;: len(annotation.reasoning)
                })
                
        for annotator_id, data in annotator_data.items():
            if len(data) &lt; 5:  # Minimum sample size
                continue
                
            relevance_scores = [d[&#x27;relevance&#x27;] for d in data]
            confidence_scores = [d[&#x27;confidence&#x27;] for d in data]
            reasoning_lengths = [d[&#x27;reasoning_length&#x27;] for d in data]
            
            # Consistency metrics
            consistency_score = 1.0 - (np.std(relevance_scores) / 5.0)  # Normalized by scale
            confidence_alignment = np.corrcoef(relevance_scores, confidence_scores)[0, 1]
            reasoning_consistency = 1.0 - (np.std(reasoning_lengths) / np.mean(reasoning_lengths))
            
            # Composite consistency score
            composite_consistency = np.mean([
                consistency_score, 
                (confidence_alignment + 1) / 2,  # Normalize from [-1,1] to [0,1]
                max(0, reasoning_consistency)
            ])
            
            annotator_consistency[annotator_id] = composite_consistency
            
        return annotator_consistency
        
    def perform_statistical_significance_tests(self, kappa_values: Dict[str, float],
                                             n_items: int) -&gt; Dict[str, Any]:
        &quot;&quot;&quot;Perform statistical significance tests for reliability measures.&quot;&quot;&quot;
        significance_tests = {}
        
        for kappa_name, kappa_value in kappa_values.items():
            if &#x27;binary&#x27; in kappa_name:
                # Test against null hypothesis (κ = 0)
                se = np.sqrt((kappa_value * (1 - kappa_value)) / n_items) if n_items &gt; 0 else 0.1
                z_statistic = kappa_value / se if se &gt; 0 else 0
                p_value = 2 * (1 - stats.norm.cdf(abs(z_statistic)))
                
                significance_tests[kappa_name] = {
                    &#x27;z_statistic&#x27;: z_statistic,
                    &#x27;p_value&#x27;: p_value,
                    &#x27;significant_at_05&#x27;: p_value &lt; 0.05,
                    &#x27;effect_size&#x27;: self.interpret_kappa(kappa_value)
                }
                
        return significance_tests
        
    def generate_reliability_report(self, annotations: List[AnnotationData]) -&gt; ReliabilityAnalysis:
        &quot;&quot;&quot;Generate comprehensive reliability analysis report.&quot;&quot;&quot;
        self.logger.info(&quot;Generating comprehensive reliability analysis&quot;)
        
        # Organize annotations
        annotations_dict = self.organize_annotations_by_item(annotations)
        n_items = len(annotations_dict)
        
        if n_items &lt; 10:
            self.logger.warning(f&quot;Low number of multiply-annotated items: {n_items}&quot;)
            
        # Calculate reliability measures
        kappa_values = self.calculate_cohens_kappa(annotations_dict)
        krippendorffs_alpha = self.calculate_krippendorffs_alpha(annotations_dict)
        agreement_percentage = self.calculate_agreement_percentage(annotations_dict)
        
        # Get primary kappa values (average of binary kappa scores)
        binary_kappas = [v for k, v in kappa_values.items() if &#x27;binary&#x27; in k]
        weighted_kappas = [v for k, v in kappa_values.items() if &#x27;weighted&#x27; in k]
        
        avg_binary_kappa = np.mean(binary_kappas) if binary_kappas else 0.0
        avg_weighted_kappa = np.mean(weighted_kappas) if weighted_kappas else 0.0
        
        # Interpretation and quality gate
        interpretation = self.interpret_kappa(avg_binary_kappa)
        quality_gate_passed = avg_binary_kappa &gt;= self.min_kappa_threshold
        
        # Statistical validation
        confidence_intervals = self.calculate_confidence_intervals(annotations_dict, kappa_values)
        significance_tests = self.perform_statistical_significance_tests(kappa_values, n_items)
        
        # Bias analysis
        bias_analysis = self.detect_systematic_bias(annotations)
        
        # Annotator consistency
        annotator_consistency = self.calculate_annotator_consistency(annotations_dict)
        
        # Create comprehensive analysis
        analysis = ReliabilityAnalysis(
            cohens_kappa_binary=avg_binary_kappa,
            cohens_kappa_weighted=avg_weighted_kappa,
            krippendorffs_alpha=krippendorffs_alpha,
            agreement_percentage=agreement_percentage,
            interpretation=interpretation,
            quality_gate_passed=quality_gate_passed,
            statistical_significance=significance_tests,
            confidence_intervals=confidence_intervals,
            bias_analysis=bias_analysis,
            annotator_consistency=annotator_consistency
        )
        
        return analysis
        
    def create_visualization_report(self, analysis: ReliabilityAnalysis,
                                  annotations: List[AnnotationData]) -&gt; Path:
        &quot;&quot;&quot;Create comprehensive visualization report.&quot;&quot;&quot;
        fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 3, figsize=(18, 12))
        fig.suptitle(&#x27;Inter-Rater Reliability Analysis Report&#x27;, fontsize=16, fontweight=&#x27;bold&#x27;)
        
        # 1. Kappa values comparison
        ax1 = axes[0, 0]
        kappa_types = [&#x27;Binary κ&#x27;, &#x27;Weighted κ&#x27;, &quot;Krippendorff&#x27;s α&quot;]
        kappa_values = [
            analysis.cohens_kappa_binary,
            analysis.cohens_kappa_weighted, 
            analysis.krippendorffs_alpha
        ]
        
        bars = ax1.bar(kappa_types, kappa_values, 
                      color=[&#x27;#2E86AB&#x27;, &#x27;#A23B72&#x27;, &#x27;#F18F01&#x27;])
        ax1.axhline(y=self.min_kappa_threshold, color=&#x27;red&#x27;, linestyle=&#x27;--&#x27;, 
                   label=f&#x27;Threshold ({self.min_kappa_threshold})&#x27;)
        ax1.set_ylabel(&#x27;Reliability Coefficient&#x27;)
        ax1.set_title(&#x27;Reliability Measures&#x27;)
        ax1.legend()

        # Add value labels on bars
        for bar, value in zip(bars, kappa_values):

        # 2. Score distribution by annotator
        ax2 = axes[0, 1]
        annotator_scores = defaultdict(list)
        for ann in annotations:
            annotator_scores[ann.annotator_id].append(ann.relevance_score)
            
        for i, (annotator, scores) in enumerate(annotator_scores.items()):

        ax2.set_xlabel(&#x27;Relevance Score&#x27;)
        ax2.set_ylabel(&#x27;Density&#x27;)
        ax2.set_title(&#x27;Score Distribution by Annotator&#x27;)
        ax2.legend()
        
        # 3. Confidence vs Relevance alignment
        ax3 = axes[0, 2]
        confidence_scores = [ann.confidence_score for ann in annotations]
        relevance_scores = [ann.relevance_score for ann in annotations]
        ax3.scatter(confidence_scores, relevance_scores, alpha=0.6)
        ax3.set_xlabel(&#x27;Confidence Score&#x27;)
        ax3.set_ylabel(&#x27;Relevance Score&#x27;)
        ax3.set_title(&#x27;Confidence-Relevance Alignment&#x27;)
        
        # Add correlation line
        z = np.polyfit(confidence_scores, relevance_scores, 1)
        p = np.poly1d(z)
        ax3.plot(confidence_scores, p(confidence_scores), &quot;r--&quot;, alpha=0.8)
        correlation = np.corrcoef(confidence_scores, relevance_scores)[0, 1]
        ax3.text(0.05, 0.95, f&#x27;r = {correlation:.3f}&#x27;, transform=ax3.transAxes,
                fontweight=&#x27;bold&#x27;, bbox=dict(boxstyle=&#x27;round&#x27;, facecolor=&#x27;white&#x27;, alpha=0.8))
        
        # 4. Annotator consistency scores
        ax4 = axes[1, 0]
        if analysis.annotator_consistency:
            annotators = list(analysis.annotator_consistency.keys())
            consistency_scores = list(analysis.annotator_consistency.values())

    def load_pr_signals(self, pr_signals_file: Path) -&gt; List[Dict[str, Any]]:
        &quot;&quot;&quot;Load PR-based relevance signals for task generation.&quot;&quot;&quot;
        self.logger.info(f&quot;Loading PR signals from {pr_signals_file}&quot;)
        
        with open(pr_signals_file, &#x27;r&#x27;) as f:
            data = json.load(f)
            
        signals = data.get(&#x27;relevance_signals&#x27;, [])
        self.logger.info(f&quot;Loaded {len(signals)} PR relevance signals&quot;)
        return signals
        
    def select_scenario_for_repository(self, repo_context: Dict[str, Any]) -&gt; Dict[str, Any]:
        &quot;&quot;&quot;Select appropriate scenario based on repository characteristics.&quot;&quot;&quot;
        primary_language = repo_context.get(&#x27;language_primary&#x27;, &#x27;&#x27;).lower()
        repo_size = repo_context.get(&#x27;file_count&#x27;, 0)
        
        # Filter scenarios by language compatibility
        applicable_scenarios = {
            name: template for name, template in self.scenario_templates.items()
            if primary_language in template[&#x27;applicable_languages&#x27;]
        }
        
        if not applicable_scenarios:
            # Fallback to language-agnostic scenarios
            applicable_scenarios = {
                name: template for name, template in self.scenario_templates.items()
                if &#x27;typescript&#x27; in template[&#x27;applicable_languages&#x27;]  # Most general
            }
            
        # Prefer scenarios based on repository size/complexity
        if repo_size &gt; 5000:  # Large repository
            preferred = [&#x27;microservice_integration&#x27;, &#x27;api_crud_operations&#x27;]
        elif repo_size &gt; 1000:  # Medium repository  
            preferred = [&#x27;web_app_auth&#x27;, &#x27;data_visualization&#x27;, &#x27;search_functionality&#x27;]
        else:  # Small repository
            preferred = [&#x27;web_app_auth&#x27;, &#x27;api_crud_operations&#x27;]
            
        # Select scenario with preference
        for pref in preferred:
            if pref in applicable_scenarios:
                return applicable_scenarios[pref]
                
        # Random selection if no preferred match
        return random.choice(list(applicable_scenarios.values()))
        
    def determine_file_difficulty(self, pr_signal: Dict[str, Any]) -&gt; str:
        &quot;&quot;&quot;Determine annotation difficulty based on PR signal characteristics.&quot;&quot;&quot;
        relevance_score = pr_signal.get(&#x27;relevance_score&#x27;, 0.0)
        semantic_role = pr_signal.get(&#x27;semantic_role&#x27;, &#x27;&#x27;)
        change_density = pr_signal.get(&#x27;change_density&#x27;, 0.0)
        dependency_impact = pr_signal.get(&#x27;dependency_impact&#x27;, 0.0)
        
        # Complexity scoring
        complexity_score = 0.0
        
        # Semantic role complexity
        role_complexity = {
            &#x27;core_logic&#x27;: 0.8,
            &#x27;configuration&#x27;: 0.4,
            &#x27;test&#x27;: 0.3,
            &#x27;build_deployment&#x27;: 0.5,
            &#x27;documentation&#x27;: 0.2,
            &#x27;assets&#x27;: 0.1
        }
        complexity_score += role_complexity.get(semantic_role, 0.5)
        
        # Change characteristics
        complexity_score += min(change_density * 0.5, 0.3)
        complexity_score += min(dependency_impact * 0.4, 0.3)
        complexity_score += min(relevance_score * 0.3, 0.2)
        
        # Classify based on composite score
        if complexity_score &gt;= 0.7:
            return &#x27;complex&#x27;
        elif complexity_score &gt;= 0.4:
            return &#x27;medium&#x27;
        else:
            return &#x27;simple&#x27;

    def identify_context_files(self, target_file: str, pr_signals: List[Dict[str, Any]]) -&gt; List[str]:
        &quot;&quot;&quot;Identify related context files for annotation task.&quot;&quot;&quot;
        target_dir = str(Path(target_file).parent)
        target_name = Path(target_file).stem
        
        context_files = []
        
        # Find files in same directory
        same_dir_files = [
            signal[&#x27;file_path&#x27;] for signal in pr_signals
            if str(Path(signal[&#x27;file_path&#x27;]).parent) == target_dir
            and signal[&#x27;file_path&#x27;] != target_file
        ]
        context_files.extend(same_dir_files[:3])  # Max 3 same-directory files
        
        # Find related files by name patterns
        related_files = [
            signal[&#x27;file_path&#x27;] for signal in pr_signals
            if target_name.lower() in Path(signal[&#x27;file_path&#x27;]).stem.lower()
            and signal[&#x27;file_path&#x27;] != target_file
            and signal[&#x27;file_path&#x27;] not in context_files
        ]
        context_files.extend(related_files[:2])  # Max 2 name-related files
        
        # Find high-relevance files as additional context
        high_relevance_files = [
            signal[&#x27;file_path&#x27;] for signal in pr_signals
            if signal.get(&#x27;relevance_score&#x27;, 0) &gt;= 0.7
            and signal[&#x27;file_path&#x27;] != target_file
            and signal[&#x27;file_path&#x27;] not in context_files
        ]
        context_files.extend(high_relevance_files[:2])  # Max 2 high-relevance files
        
        return context_files
        
    def calculate_annotation_time(self, difficulty: str, context_file_count: int) -&gt; int:
        &quot;&quot;&quot;Calculate estimated annotation time based on task characteristics.&quot;&quot;&quot;
        base_min, base_max = self.task_time_estimates[difficulty]
        base_time = random.randint(base_min, base_max)
        
        # Add time for context files
        context_time = context_file_count * random.randint(1, 3)
        
        return base_time + context_time
        
    def generate_task_from_signal(self, pr_signal: Dict[str, Any], 
                                scenario: Dict[str, Any],
                                pr_signals: List[Dict[str, Any]],
                                task_batch_id: str,
                                repository: str) -&gt; AnnotationTask:
        &quot;&quot;&quot;Generate a complete annotation task from PR signal.&quot;&quot;&quot;
        
        file_path = pr_signal[&#x27;file_path&#x27;]
        difficulty = self.determine_file_difficulty(pr_signal)
        context_files = self.identify_context_files(file_path, pr_signals)
        
        # Generate unique task ID
        task_id = hashlib.sha256(
            f&quot;{task_batch_id}_{file_path}_{pr_signal.get(&#x27;pr_context&#x27;, {}).get(&#x27;pr_number&#x27;, 0)}&quot;
            .encode()
        ).hexdigest()[:12]
        
        # Create task
        task = AnnotationTask(
            task_id=task_id,
            task_batch=task_batch_id,
            repository=repository,
            file_path=file_path,
            task_type=scenario[&#x27;theme&#x27;].lower().replace(&#x27; &#x27;, &#x27;_&#x27;),
            scenario_description=scenario[&#x27;description&#x27;],
            specific_requirements=scenario[&#x27;requirements&#x27;],
            file_preview=self.generate_file_preview(file_path, pr_signal.get(&#x27;pr_context&#x27;, {})),
            context_files=context_files,
            difficulty_level=difficulty,
            expected_annotation_time_minutes=self.calculate_annotation_time(difficulty, len(context_files)),
            pr_signal_score=pr_signal.get(&#x27;relevance_score&#x27;, 0.0),
            pr_context=pr_signal.get(&#x27;pr_context&#x27;, {}),
            task_metadata={
                &#x27;generation_timestamp&#x27;: datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
                &#x27;generator_version&#x27;: &#x27;1.0.0&#x27;,
                &#x27;methodology_version&#x27;: &#x27;ground_truth_v1.0&#x27;,
                &#x27;seed_used&#x27;: self.seed,
                &#x27;difficulty_factors&#x27;: {
                    &#x27;semantic_role&#x27;: pr_signal.get(&#x27;semantic_role&#x27;),
                    &#x27;change_density&#x27;: pr_signal.get(&#x27;change_density&#x27;),
                    &#x27;dependency_impact&#x27;: pr_signal.get(&#x27;dependency_impact&#x27;)
                }
            }
        )
        
        return task
        
    def balance_difficulty_distribution(self, tasks: List[AnnotationTask]) -&gt; List[AnnotationTask]:
        &quot;&quot;&quot;Balance task difficulty distribution according to target weights.&quot;&quot;&quot;
        
        # Group by difficulty
        by_difficulty = defaultdict(list)
        for task in tasks:
            by_difficulty[task.difficulty_level].append(task)
            
        # Calculate target counts
        total_tasks = len(tasks)
        target_counts = {
            difficulty: int(total_tasks * weight)
            for difficulty, weight in self.difficulty_weights.items()
        }
        
        # Balance by sampling
        balanced_tasks = []
        for difficulty, target_count in target_counts.items():
            available = by_difficulty[difficulty]
            if len(available) &gt;= target_count:
                # Random sample without replacement
                sampled = random.sample(available, target_count)
            else:
                # Use all available
                sampled = available
                
            balanced_tasks.extend(sampled)
            
        # If we need more tasks, add from remaining pool
        remaining_tasks = [
            task for task in tasks if task not in balanced_tasks
        ]
        
        additional_needed = total_tasks - len(balanced_tasks)
        if additional_needed &gt; 0 and remaining_tasks:
            additional = random.sample(
                remaining_tasks, 
                min(additional_needed, len(remaining_tasks))
            )
            balanced_tasks.extend(additional)
            
        # Shuffle for random presentation order
        random.shuffle(balanced_tasks)
        
        return balanced_tasks
        
    def generate_batch_from_repository(self, pr_signals_file: Path,
                                     repo_context: Dict[str, Any],
                                     max_tasks_per_batch: int = 15) -&gt; TaskBatch:
        &quot;&quot;&quot;Generate a complete task batch for a repository.&quot;&quot;&quot;
        
        # Load PR signals
        pr_signals = self.load_pr_signals(pr_signals_file)
        
        if not pr_signals:
            raise ValueError(f&quot;No PR signals found in {pr_signals_file}&quot;)
            
        # Select scenario
        scenario = self.select_scenario_for_repository(repo_context)
        
        # Generate batch ID
        repo_name = repo_context.get(&#x27;name&#x27;, &#x27;unknown_repo&#x27;)
        batch_id = f&quot;{repo_name}_{scenario[&#x27;theme&#x27;].lower().replace(&#x27; &#x27;, &#x27;_&#x27;)}_{datetime.now().strftime(&#x27;%Y%m%d&#x27;)}&quot;
        
        # Filter signals for task generation (focus on higher relevance)
        suitable_signals = [
            signal for signal in pr_signals
            if signal.get(&#x27;relevance_score&#x27;, 0.0) &gt;= 0.2  # Minimum relevance threshold
        ]
        
        # Limit to max tasks per batch
        if len(suitable_signals) &gt; max_tasks_per_batch:
            # Stratified sampling by relevance score
            suitable_signals.sort(key=lambda x: x.get(&#x27;relevance_score&#x27;, 0.0), reverse=True)
            suitable_signals = suitable_signals[:max_tasks_per_batch]
            
        # Generate tasks
        tasks = []
        for signal in suitable_signals:
            task = self.generate_task_from_signal(
                signal, scenario, pr_signals, batch_id, repo_name
            )
            tasks.append(task)
            
        # Balance difficulty distribution
        tasks = self.balance_difficulty_distribution(tasks)
        
        # Calculate batch statistics
        difficulty_distribution = Counter(task.difficulty_level for task in tasks)
        total_time = sum(task.expected_annotation_time_minutes for task in tasks)
        
        # Create batch
        batch = TaskBatch(
            batch_id=batch_id,
            repository=repo_name,
            scenario_theme=scenario[&#x27;theme&#x27;],
            task_count=len(tasks),
            difficulty_distribution=dict(difficulty_distribution),
            estimated_total_time_minutes=total_time,
            tasks=tasks,
            generation_metadata={
                &#x27;timestamp&#x27;: datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
                &#x27;generator_version&#x27;: &#x27;1.0.0&#x27;,
                &#x27;methodology_version&#x27;: &#x27;ground_truth_v1.0&#x27;,
                &#x27;seed&#x27;: self.seed,
                &#x27;pr_signals_file&#x27;: str(pr_signals_file),
                &#x27;scenario_selected&#x27;: scenario[&#x27;theme&#x27;],
                &#x27;target_difficulty_weights&#x27;: self.difficulty_weights,
                &#x27;actual_difficulty_distribution&#x27;: dict(difficulty_distribution)
            }
        )
        
        return batch
        
    def save_task_batch(self, batch: TaskBatch, output_filename: str) -&gt; Path:
        &quot;&quot;&quot;Save task batch with comprehensive metadata.&quot;&quot;&quot;
        
        # Prepare serializable batch data
        batch_data = {
            &#x27;batch_metadata&#x27;: {
                &#x27;batch_id&#x27;: batch.batch_id,
                &#x27;repository&#x27;: batch.repository,
                &#x27;scenario_theme&#x27;: batch.scenario_theme,
                &#x27;task_count&#x27;: batch.task_count,
                &#x27;difficulty_distribution&#x27;: batch.difficulty_distribution,
                &#x27;estimated_total_time_minutes&#x27;: batch.estimated_total_time_minutes,
                &#x27;generation_metadata&#x27;: batch.generation_metadata
            },
            &#x27;annotation_instructions&#x27;: {
                &#x27;relevance_scale_definition&#x27;: {
                    &#x27;5&#x27;: &#x27;Critical - File is essential for task completion&#x27;,
                    &#x27;4&#x27;: &#x27;High - File likely requires modification or deep understanding&#x27;, 
                    &#x27;3&#x27;: &#x27;Medium - File provides important context or may need minor changes&#x27;,
                    &#x27;2&#x27;: &#x27;Low - File provides some context but unlikely to need changes&#x27;,
                    &#x27;1&#x27;: &#x27;Minimal - File is largely irrelevant to the task&#x27;
                },
                &#x27;confidence_scale_definition&#x27;: {
                    &#x27;5&#x27;: &#x27;Very confident in relevance assessment&#x27;,
                    &#x27;4&#x27;: &#x27;Confident with minor uncertainty&#x27;,
                    &#x27;3&#x27;: &#x27;Moderately confident&#x27;,
                    &#x27;2&#x27;: &#x27;Low confidence, significant uncertainty&#x27;,
                    &#x27;1&#x27;: &#x27;Very low confidence, mostly guessing&#x27;
                },
                &#x27;annotation_guidelines&#x27;: [
                    &#x27;Read the scenario description and requirements carefully&#x27;,
                    &#x27;Review the file preview and context files&#x27;,
                    &#x27;Consider how the file would be involved in implementing the scenario&#x27;,
                    &#x27;Rate relevance based on likelihood of modification or importance for understanding&#x27;,
                    &#x27;Rate confidence based on how certain you are about the relevance assessment&#x27;,
                    &#x27;Provide clear reasoning for your relevance rating&#x27;
                ]
            },
            &#x27;tasks&#x27;: [asdict(task) for task in batch.tasks]
        }
        
        # Save to JSON
        output_path = self.output_dir / output_filename
        with open(output_path, &#x27;w&#x27;) as f:
            json.dump(batch_data, f, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)
            
        self.logger.info(f&quot;Task batch saved to {output_path}&quot;)
        return output_path
        
    def validate_batch_quality(self, batch: TaskBatch) -&gt; Dict[str, Any]:
        &quot;&quot;&quot;Validate batch quality against academic standards.&quot;&quot;&quot;
        
        quality_report = {
            &#x27;task_count_adequate&#x27;: batch.task_count &gt;= 10,
            &#x27;difficulty_balanced&#x27;: all(
                count &gt;= 2 for count in batch.difficulty_distribution.values()
            ),
            &#x27;time_estimate_reasonable&#x27;: (
                30 &lt;= batch.estimated_total_time_minutes &lt;= 180  # 30min - 3hrs
            ),
            &#x27;context_files_provided&#x27;: all(
                len(task.context_files) &gt;= 1 for task in batch.tasks
            ),
            &#x27;preview_content_generated&#x27;: all(
                len(task.file_preview) &gt;= 50 for task in batch.tasks
            ),
            &#x27;pr_signals_linked&#x27;: all(
                task.pr_signal_score &gt; 0.0 for task in batch.tasks
            )
        }
        
        quality_report[&#x27;overall_quality_score&#x27;] = sum(quality_report.values()) / len(quality_report)
        
        return quality_report


def main():
    &quot;&quot;&quot;Main execution function for annotation task generation.&quot;&quot;&quot;
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        description=&#x27;Generate annotation tasks for ground-truth dataset creation&#x27;
    )
    parser.add_argument(&#x27;--pr-signals-file&#x27;, required=True, type=Path,

    args = parser.parse_args()
    
    # Initialize generator

        # Validate batch quality

        # Save batch
        output_filename = f&quot;annotation_tasks_{batch.repository}_{datetime.now().strftime(&#x27;%Y%m%d&#x27;)}.json&quot;
        batch_path = generator.save_task_batch(batch, output_filename)
        
        # Print summary
        print(&quot;\n&quot; + &quot;=&quot;*60)

        print(f&quot;⏱️  Estimated time: {batch.estimated_total_time_minutes} minutes&quot;)
        print(f&quot;📈 Difficulty distribution: {batch.difficulty_distribution}&quot;)
        print(f&quot;✅ Quality score: {quality_report[&#x27;overall_quality_score&#x27;]:.2f}&quot;)
        print(f&quot;📁 Tasks saved to: {batch_path}&quot;)
        print(&quot;=&quot;*60)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
&quot;&quot;&quot;
Update LaTeX paper with generated tables and figures.

Patches LaTeX documents by:
- Replacing placeholder values with actual results
- Updating table references with generated content  
- Updating figure paths and captions
- Preserving document structure and formatting
&quot;&quot;&quot;

import argparse
import json
import logging
import re
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Any

# Configure logging
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO)
logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


class LaTeXPatcher:
    &quot;&quot;&quot;Update LaTeX documents with evaluation results.&quot;&quot;&quot;
    
    def __init__(self):
        self.placeholder_pattern = r&#x27;\\placeholder\{([^}]+)\}&#x27;
        self.table_pattern = r&#x27;\\input\{([^}]+_table[^}]*)\}&#x27;
        self.figure_pattern = r&#x27;\\includegraphics(?:\[[^\]]*\])?\{([^}]+)\}&#x27;
        
    def load_tex_file(self, tex_file: Path) -&gt; str:
        &quot;&quot;&quot;Load LaTeX file content.&quot;&quot;&quot;
        with open(tex_file, &#x27;r&#x27;, encoding=&#x27;utf-8&#x27;) as f:
            return f.read()
            
    def load_tables(self, tables_file: Path) -&gt; str:
        &quot;&quot;&quot;Load generated LaTeX tables.&quot;&quot;&quot;
        with open(tables_file, &#x27;r&#x27;, encoding=&#x27;utf-8&#x27;) as f:
            return f.read()
            
    def update_placeholders(self, content: str, results: Dict[str, Any]) -&gt; str:
        &quot;&quot;&quot;Update placeholder values with actual results.&quot;&quot;&quot;
        
        def replace_placeholder(match):
            placeholder = match.group(1)
            
            # Define placeholder mappings
            replacements = {
                &#x27;MAIN_IMPROVEMENT&#x27;: self._format_improvement(results),
                &#x27;TARGET_IMPROVEMENT&#x27;: &#x27;13.0&#x27;,
                &#x27;CONFIDENCE_LEVEL&#x27;: &#x27;95&#x27;,
                &#x27;BOOTSTRAP_ITERATIONS&#x27;: &#x27;10000&#x27;,
                &#x27;EVALUATION_SEEDS&#x27;: &#x27;100&#x27;,
                &#x27;TOKEN_BUDGETS&#x27;: &#x27;50k, 120k, 200k&#x27;,
                &#x27;SYSTEMS_EVALUATED&#x27;: self._format_systems(results),
                &#x27;SIGNIFICANCE_THRESHOLD&#x27;: &#x27;0.05&#x27;
            }
            
            return replacements.get(placeholder, f&#x27;\\texttt{{{placeholder}}}&#x27;)
            
        return re.sub(self.placeholder_pattern, replace_placeholder, content)
        
    def update_table_references(self, content: str, tables_content: str) -&gt; str:
        &quot;&quot;&quot;Update table input references with generated tables.&quot;&quot;&quot;
        
        # Extract individual tables from tables content
        tables = self._extract_tables(tables_content)
        
        def replace_table_input(match):
            table_file = match.group(1)
            
            # Map table files to generated content
            if &#x27;main_results&#x27; in table_file:
                return tables.get(&#x27;main_results&#x27;, match.group(0))
            elif &#x27;category&#x27; in table_file:
                return tables.get(&#x27;category_breakdown&#x27;, match.group(0))
            elif &#x27;negative&#x27; in table_file:
                return tables.get(&#x27;negative_controls&#x27;, match.group(0))
            elif &#x27;baselines&#x27; in table_file:
                return tables.get(&#x27;ir_baselines&#x27;, match.group(0))
            else:
                return match.group(0)
                
        return re.sub(self.table_pattern, replace_table_input, content)
        
    def update_figure_references(self, content: str, figures_dir: Path) -&gt; str:
        &quot;&quot;&quot;Update figure references with generated figures.&quot;&quot;&quot;
        
        def replace_figure_path(match):
            figure_file = match.group(1)
            
            # Map figure names to generated files
            figure_mappings = {
                &#x27;performance_comparison&#x27;: &#x27;performance_comparison.pdf&#x27;,
                &#x27;confidence_intervals&#x27;: &#x27;confidence_intervals.pdf&#x27;, 
                &#x27;category_breakdown&#x27;: &#x27;category_breakdown.pdf&#x27;,
                &#x27;effect_sizes&#x27;: &#x27;effect_sizes.pdf&#x27;
            }
            
            # Check if this is a figure we generated
            for key, generated_file in figure_mappings.items():
                if key in figure_file:
                    new_path = figures_dir / generated_file
                    if new_path.exists():
                        return str(new_path)
                        
            return figure_file
            
        return re.sub(self.figure_pattern, 
                     lambda m: f&#x27;\\includegraphics{{{replace_figure_path(m)}}}&#x27;, 
                     content)
        
    def _extract_tables(self, tables_content: str) -&gt; Dict[str, str]:
        &quot;&quot;&quot;Extract individual tables from consolidated content.&quot;&quot;&quot;
        tables = {}
        
        # Split by table boundaries
        table_sections = re.split(r&#x27;(?=\\begin\{table\})&#x27;, tables_content)
        
        for section in table_sections:
            if not section.strip():
                continue
                
            # Identify table type from label or caption
            if &#x27;main_results&#x27; in section or &#x27;Main Results&#x27; in section:
                tables[&#x27;main_results&#x27;] = section.strip()
            elif &#x27;category&#x27; in section or &#x27;Category&#x27; in section:
                tables[&#x27;category_breakdown&#x27;] = section.strip()
            elif &#x27;negative&#x27; in section or &#x27;Negative&#x27; in section:
                tables[&#x27;negative_controls&#x27;] = section.strip()
            elif &#x27;baselines&#x27; in section or &#x27;Baselines&#x27; in section:
                tables[&#x27;ir_baselines&#x27;] = section.strip()
                
        return tables
        
    def _format_improvement(self, results: Dict[str, Any]) -&gt; str:
        &quot;&quot;&quot;Format main improvement percentage.&quot;&quot;&quot;
        # Extract from results if available
        if &#x27;system_analyses&#x27; in results:
            for system, analysis in results[&#x27;system_analyses&#x27;].items():
                if system != &#x27;baseline&#x27; and &#x27;overall_improvement_pct&#x27; in analysis:
                    improvement = analysis[&#x27;overall_improvement_pct&#x27;]
                    return f&quot;{improvement:+.1f}\\%&quot;
                    
        return &quot;+XX.X\\%&quot;  # Placeholder if not available
        
    def _format_systems(self, results: Dict[str, Any]) -&gt; str:
        &quot;&quot;&quot;Format list of evaluated systems.&quot;&quot;&quot;
        if &#x27;system_analyses&#x27; in results:
            systems = list(results[&#x27;system_analyses&#x27;].keys())
            return &quot;, &quot;.join(s.upper() for s in systems if s != &#x27;baseline&#x27;)
            
        return &quot;V1, V2, V3, V4, V5&quot;
        
    def patch_document(
        self,
        tex_file: Path,
        tables_file: Path,
        figures_dir: Path,
        results: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None
    ) -&gt; str:
        &quot;&quot;&quot;Patch LaTeX document with generated content.&quot;&quot;&quot;
        
        # Load content
        content = self.load_tex_file(tex_file)
        tables_content = self.load_tables(tables_file)
        
        logger.info(f&quot;Patching LaTeX document: {tex_file}&quot;)
        
        # Apply updates
        if results:
            content = self.update_placeholders(content, results)
            
        content = self.update_table_references(content, tables_content)
        content = self.update_figure_references(content, figures_dir)
        
        return content
        
    def save_patched_document(
        self,
        original_tex: Path,
        patched_content: str,
        output_tex: Optional[Path] = None
    ):
        &quot;&quot;&quot;Save patched document.&quot;&quot;&quot;
        
        if output_tex is None:
            output_tex = original_tex
            
        # Create backup of original
        if output_tex == original_tex:
            backup_file = original_tex.with_suffix(&#x27;.tex.backup&#x27;)
            original_tex.rename(backup_file)
            logger.info(f&quot;Created backup: {backup_file}&quot;)
            
        # Save patched content
        with open(output_tex, &#x27;w&#x27;, encoding=&#x27;utf-8&#x27;) as f:
            f.write(patched_content)
            
        logger.info(f&quot;Saved patched document: {output_tex}&quot;)


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        description=&quot;Update LaTeX paper with generated tables and figures&quot;,
        formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter,
        epilog=&quot;&quot;&quot;
Example:
  python patch_tex.py --tex paper/fastpath.tex --tables paper/tables.tex --figdir paper/figures --results artifacts/analysis.json
        &quot;&quot;&quot;
    )

#!/usr/bin/env python3
&quot;&quot;&quot;
Generate publication figures from evaluation artifacts.

Creates publication-ready figures including:
- Performance comparison plots
- Confidence interval visualization
- Category breakdown charts
- Effect size forest plots
&quot;&quot;&quot;

import argparse
import json
import logging
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Any, Tuple
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
from matplotlib.patches import Rectangle
import warnings

# Configure plotting
plt.style.use(&#x27;seaborn-v0_8&#x27;)
sns.set_palette(&quot;husl&quot;)
warnings.filterwarnings(&quot;ignore&quot;, category=UserWarning)

# Configure logging
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO)
logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


class PublicationFigureGenerator:
    &quot;&quot;&quot;Generate publication-quality figures from evaluation data.&quot;&quot;&quot;
    
    def __init__(self):
        self.figure_size = (10, 6)
        self.dpi = 300
        self.font_size = 12
        
        # Configure matplotlib for publication
        plt.rcParams.update({
            &#x27;font.size&#x27;: self.font_size,
            &#x27;axes.titlesize&#x27;: self.font_size,
            &#x27;axes.labelsize&#x27;: self.font_size,
            &#x27;xtick.labelsize&#x27;: self.font_size - 1,
            &#x27;ytick.labelsize&#x27;: self.font_size - 1,
            &#x27;legend.fontsize&#x27;: self.font_size - 1,
            &#x27;figure.titlesize&#x27;: self.font_size + 2,
            &#x27;font.family&#x27;: &#x27;serif&#x27;,
            &#x27;font.serif&#x27;: [&#x27;Times New Roman&#x27;],
            &#x27;text.usetex&#x27;: False  # Disable for compatibility
        })
        
    def load_artifacts(self, artifacts_dir: Path) -&gt; Dict[str, Any]:
        &quot;&quot;&quot;Load all artifacts from directory.&quot;&quot;&quot;
        artifacts = {}
        
        # Load CI results
        ci_file = artifacts_dir / &#x27;ci.json&#x27;
        if ci_file.exists():
            with open(ci_file, &#x27;r&#x27;) as f:
                artifacts[&#x27;ci&#x27;] = json.load(f)
                
        # Load analysis results
        analysis_file = artifacts_dir / &#x27;analysis.json&#x27;
        if analysis_file.exists():
            with open(analysis_file, &#x27;r&#x27;) as f:
                artifacts[&#x27;analysis&#x27;] = json.load(f)
                
        # Load collected results
        collected_file = artifacts_dir / &#x27;collected.json&#x27;
        if collected_file.exists():
            with open(collected_file, &#x27;r&#x27;) as f:
                artifacts[&#x27;collected&#x27;] = json.load(f)
                
        logger.info(f&quot;Loaded {len(artifacts)} artifact types&quot;)
        return artifacts
        
    def generate_performance_comparison(self, artifacts: Dict, output_dir: Path):
        &quot;&quot;&quot;Generate performance comparison figure.&quot;&quot;&quot;
        
        if &#x27;collected&#x27; not in artifacts:
            logger.warning(&quot;No collected results available for performance comparison&quot;)
            return
            
        results = artifacts[&#x27;collected&#x27;][&#x27;results&#x27;]
        
        # Group results by system and budget
        systems = sorted(set(r[&#x27;system&#x27;] for r in results))
        budgets = sorted(set(r[&#x27;budget&#x27;] for r in results))
        
        # Calculate mean QA/100k tokens for each system-budget combination
        performance_data = {}
        for system in systems:
            performance_data[system] = {}
            for budget in budgets:
                system_budget_results = [
                    r for r in results 
                    if r[&#x27;system&#x27;] == system and r[&#x27;budget&#x27;] == budget
                ]
                if system_budget_results:
                    qa_scores = [r[&#x27;qa_score&#x27;] for r in system_budget_results]
                    tokens = [r[&#x27;tokens_used&#x27;] for r in system_budget_results]
                    qa_per_100k = (sum(qa_scores) / sum(tokens)) * 100000
                    performance_data[system][budget] = qa_per_100k
                    
        # Create figure
        fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=self.figure_size)
        
        # Plot bars for each system
        bar_width = 0.15
        budget_positions = np.arange(len(budgets))
        
        colors = sns.color_palette(&quot;husl&quot;, len(systems))
        
        for i, system in enumerate(systems):
            system_values = [performance_data[system].get(budget, 0) for budget in budgets]
            positions = budget_positions + i * bar_width
            
            bars = ax.bar(positions, system_values, bar_width, 
                         label=system.upper(), color=colors[i], alpha=0.8)
            
            # Add value labels on bars
            for bar, value in zip(bars, system_values):
                if value &gt; 0:
                    ax.text(bar.get_x() + bar.get_width()/2, bar.get_height() + 5,
                           f&#x27;{value:.0f}&#x27;, ha=&#x27;center&#x27;, va=&#x27;bottom&#x27;, fontsize=10)
        
        # Formatting
        ax.set_xlabel(&#x27;Token Budget&#x27;)
        ax.set_ylabel(&#x27;QA Answers per 100k Tokens&#x27;)
        ax.set_title(&#x27;FastPath Performance Comparison&#x27;)
        ax.set_xticks(budget_positions + bar_width * (len(systems) - 1) / 2)
        ax.set_xticklabels([f&#x27;{b//1000}k&#x27; for b in budgets])
        ax.legend(bbox_to_anchor=(1.05, 1), loc=&#x27;upper left&#x27;)
        ax.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
        
        plt.tight_layout()
        
        output_file = output_dir / &#x27;performance_comparison.pdf&#x27;
        plt.savefig(output_file, dpi=self.dpi, bbox_inches=&#x27;tight&#x27;)
        plt.close()
        
        logger.info(f&quot;Generated performance comparison: {output_file}&quot;)
        
    def generate_confidence_intervals(self, artifacts: Dict, output_dir: Path):
        &quot;&quot;&quot;Generate confidence intervals visualization.&quot;&quot;&quot;
        
        if &#x27;ci&#x27; not in artifacts:
            logger.warning(&quot;No CI results available&quot;)
            return
            
        ci_results = artifacts[&#x27;ci&#x27;][&#x27;results&#x27;]
        
        # Prepare data for plotting
        systems = []
        improvements = []
        ci_lowers = []
        ci_uppers = []
        significant = []
        
        for result in ci_results:
            systems.append(result[&#x27;experimental_system&#x27;].upper())
            improvements.append(result[&#x27;observed_difference_pct&#x27;])
            ci_lowers.append(result[&#x27;ci_lower&#x27;])
            ci_uppers.append(result[&#x27;ci_upper&#x27;])
            significant.append(result[&#x27;significant_fdr&#x27;])
            
        # Create figure
        fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=self.figure_size)
        
        y_positions = np.arange(len(systems))
        
        # Plot confidence intervals
        for i, (system, imp, lower, upper, sig) in enumerate(
            zip(systems, improvements, ci_lowers, ci_uppers, significant)
        ):
            # Error bar
            color = &#x27;red&#x27; if sig else &#x27;blue&#x27;
            ax.errorbar(imp, i, xerr=[[imp - lower], [upper - imp]], 
                       fmt=&#x27;o&#x27;, color=color, capsize=5, capthick=2)
            
            # Add significance marker
            marker = &#x27;*&#x27; if sig else &#x27;&#x27;
            ax.text(imp + 1, i, marker, fontsize=16, ha=&#x27;left&#x27;, va=&#x27;center&#x27;, color=&#x27;red&#x27;)
            
        # Add vertical line at 0 (no improvement)
        ax.axvline(x=0, color=&#x27;black&#x27;, linestyle=&#x27;--&#x27;, alpha=0.7)
        
        # Add target improvement line
        target = 13.0  # From TODO.md
        ax.axvline(x=target, color=&#x27;green&#x27;, linestyle=&#x27;:&#x27;, alpha=0.7, 
                  label=f&#x27;Target ({target}%)&#x27;)
        
        # Formatting
        ax.set_yticks(y_positions)
        ax.set_yticklabels(systems)
        ax.set_xlabel(&#x27;Improvement (% QA/100k tokens)&#x27;)
        ax.set_title(&#x27;FastPath Improvements with 95% Confidence Intervals&#x27;)
        ax.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
        ax.legend()
        
        # Add note about significance
        ax.text(0.02, 0.98, &#x27;* Significant at FDR-corrected α = 0.05&#x27;, 
               transform=ax.transAxes, va=&#x27;top&#x27;, fontsize=10)
        
        plt.tight_layout()
        
        output_file = output_dir / &#x27;confidence_intervals.pdf&#x27;
        plt.savefig(output_file, dpi=self.dpi, bbox_inches=&#x27;tight&#x27;)
        plt.close()
        
        logger.info(f&quot;Generated confidence intervals: {output_file}&quot;)

    def generate_effect_size_forest_plot(self, artifacts: Dict, output_dir: Path):

#!/usr/bin/env python3
&quot;&quot;&quot;
Comprehensive Real-World Benchmarking System for FastPath vs Baseline PackRepo

This system provides rigorous empirical validation of FastPath performance claims
with statistical significance testing, real repository validation, and comprehensive
performance analysis across multiple dimensions.

Key Features:
- Real-world repository testing with different sizes/languages
- Statistical rigor with confidence intervals and significance testing
- Comprehensive performance metrics (latency, memory, token efficiency)
- Quality assessment and retention analysis
- Automated visualization and reporting
- Production-ready benchmark suite
&quot;&quot;&quot;

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

@dataclass
class RepositorySpec:
    &quot;&quot;&quot;Specification for a test repository.&quot;&quot;&quot;
    name: str
    url: str
    language: str
    category: str  # small, medium, large
    expected_files: int
    expected_loc: int
    clone_depth: Optional[int] = 1  # Shallow clone by default
    description: str = &quot;&quot;


@dataclass 
class BenchmarkMetrics:
    &quot;&quot;&quot;Comprehensive performance metrics for a single benchmark run.&quot;&quot;&quot;
    run_id: int
    system_name: str  # fastpath, baseline, extended
    repo_name: str
    token_budget: int
    
    # Performance metrics
    execution_time_ms: float
    memory_peak_mb: float
    memory_current_mb: float

    # Output quality metrics
    total_tokens_used: int
    total_files_selected: int
    readme_retained: bool
    doc_files_count: int
    code_files_count: int
    
    # Token efficiency (key metric)
    tokens_per_second: float
    timestamp: str
    qa_score: Optional[float] = None  # Simulated QA accuracy
    token_efficiency: Optional[float] = None  # QA score per 100k tokens
    
    # Metadata
    success: bool = True
    error_message: Optional[str] = None


@dataclass
class StatisticalAnalysis:
