//! # Code Complexity Analysis Module
//!
//! This module provides comprehensive code complexity metrics to enhance the heuristic
//! scoring system with deeper analysis of code structure and maintainability.
//!
//! ## Complexity Metrics
//!
//! - **Cyclomatic Complexity**: Measures the number of linearly independent paths through code
//! - **Nesting Depth**: Maximum depth of nested control structures
//! - **Function Count**: Number of functions/methods in a file
//! - **Line Complexity**: Analysis of code lines vs comment lines vs blank lines
//! - **Cognitive Complexity**: Human-focused complexity measure
//! - **Maintainability Index**: Composite metric for code maintainability
//!
//! ## Usage
//!
//! ```rust
//! use scribe_analysis::complexity::{ComplexityAnalyzer, ComplexityMetrics};
//!
//! # fn example() -&gt; Result&lt;(), Box&lt;dyn std::error::Error&gt;&gt; {
//! let analyzer = ComplexityAnalyzer::new();
//! let content = &quot;fn main() { if x &gt; 0 { println!(\&quot;positive\&quot;); } }&quot;;
//! let metrics = analyzer.analyze_content(content, &quot;rust&quot;)?;
//!
//! println!(&quot;Cyclomatic Complexity: {}&quot;, metrics.cyclomatic_complexity);
//! println!(&quot;Maintainability Index: {:.2}&quot;, metrics.maintainability_index);
//! # Ok(())
//! # }
//! ```

use scribe_core::Result;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use std::collections::HashMap;

/// Comprehensive complexity metrics for a code file
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct ComplexityMetrics {
    /// Cyclomatic complexity (McCabe complexity)
    pub cyclomatic_complexity: usize,

    /// Maximum nesting depth
    pub max_nesting_depth: usize,

    /// Total number of functions/methods
    pub function_count: usize,

    /// Number of logical lines of code (excluding comments and blanks)
    pub logical_lines: usize,

    /// Number of comment lines
    pub comment_lines: usize,

    /// Number of blank lines
    pub blank_lines: usize,

    /// Total physical lines
    pub total_lines: usize,

    /// Cognitive complexity (easier to understand than cyclomatic)
    pub cognitive_complexity: usize,

    /// Maintainability index (0-100, higher is better)
    pub maintainability_index: f64,

    /// Average function length
    pub average_function_length: f64,

    /// Code density (logical lines / total lines)
    pub code_density: f64,

    /// Comment ratio (comment lines / logical lines)
    pub comment_ratio: f64,

    /// Language-specific metrics
    pub language_metrics: LanguageSpecificMetrics,
}

/// Language-specific complexity metrics
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct LanguageSpecificMetrics {
    /// Language identifier
    pub language: String,

    /// Language-specific complexity factors
    pub complexity_factors: HashMap&lt;String, f64&gt;,

    /// Number of imports/includes
    pub import_count: usize,

    /// Number of exported symbols
    pub export_count: usize,

    /// Estimated API surface area
    pub api_surface_area: usize,
}

/// Core complexity analyzer
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct ComplexityAnalyzer {
    /// Configuration for complexity analysis
    config: ComplexityConfig,
}

/// Configuration for complexity analysis
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct ComplexityConfig {
    /// Enable cognitive complexity calculation
    pub enable_cognitive_complexity: bool,

    /// Enable maintainability index calculation
    pub enable_maintainability_index: bool,

    /// Language-specific analysis
    pub enable_language_specific: bool,

    /// Thresholds for complexity warnings
    pub thresholds: ComplexityThresholds,
}

/// Thresholds for complexity warnings
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct ComplexityThresholds {
    /// Cyclomatic complexity warning threshold
    pub cyclomatic_warning: usize,

    /// Nesting depth warning threshold
    pub nesting_warning: usize,

    /// Function length warning threshold
    pub function_length_warning: usize,

    /// Maintainability index warning threshold (below this is concerning)
    pub maintainability_warning: f64,
}

impl Default for ComplexityConfig {
    fn default() -&gt; Self {
        Self {
            enable_cognitive_complexity: true,
            enable_maintainability_index: true,
            enable_language_specific: true,
            thresholds: ComplexityThresholds::default(),
        }
    }
}

impl Default for ComplexityThresholds {
    fn default() -&gt; Self {
        Self {
            cyclomatic_warning: 10,        // Standard McCabe threshold
            nesting_warning: 4,            // Deep nesting becomes hard to follow
            function_length_warning: 50,   // Functions longer than 50 lines
            maintainability_warning: 20.0, // Below 20 is concerning
        }
    }
}

impl ComplexityAnalyzer {
    /// Create a new complexity analyzer with default configuration
    pub fn new() -&gt; Self {
        Self {
            config: ComplexityConfig::default(),
        }
    }

    /// Create a new complexity analyzer with custom configuration
    pub fn with_config(config: ComplexityConfig) -&gt; Self {
        Self { config }
    }

    /// Analyze complexity of file content
    pub fn analyze_content(&amp;self, content: &amp;str, language: &amp;str) -&gt; Result&lt;ComplexityMetrics&gt; {
        let line_metrics = self.analyze_lines(content);
        let cyclomatic_complexity = self.calculate_cyclomatic_complexity(content, language);
        let max_nesting_depth = self.calculate_max_nesting_depth(content, language);
        let function_count = self.count_functions(content, language);

        let cognitive_complexity = if self.config.enable_cognitive_complexity {
            self.calculate_cognitive_complexity(content, language)
        } else {
            0
        };

        let maintainability_index = if self.config.enable_maintainability_index {
            self.calculate_maintainability_index(
                &amp;line_metrics,
                cyclomatic_complexity,
                function_count,
            )
        } else {
            0.0
        };

        let average_function_length = if function_count &gt; 0 {
            line_metrics.logical_lines as f64 / function_count as f64
        } else {
            0.0
        };

        let code_density = if line_metrics.total_lines &gt; 0 {
            line_metrics.logical_lines as f64 / line_metrics.total_lines as f64
        } else {
            0.0
        };

        let comment_ratio = if line_metrics.logical_lines &gt; 0 {
            line_metrics.comment_lines as f64 / line_metrics.logical_lines as f64
        } else {
            0.0
        };

        let language_metrics = if self.config.enable_language_specific {
            self.analyze_language_specific(content, language)
        } else {
            LanguageSpecificMetrics::default(language)
        };

        Ok(ComplexityMetrics {
            cyclomatic_complexity,
            max_nesting_depth,
            function_count,
            logical_lines: line_metrics.logical_lines,
            comment_lines: line_metrics.comment_lines,
            blank_lines: line_metrics.blank_lines,
            total_lines: line_metrics.total_lines,
            cognitive_complexity,
            maintainability_index,
            average_function_length,
            code_density,
            comment_ratio,
            language_metrics,
        })
    }

    /// Analyze line-based metrics
    fn analyze_lines(&amp;self, content: &amp;str) -&gt; LineMetrics {
        let mut logical_lines = 0;
        let mut comment_lines = 0;
        let mut blank_lines = 0;
        let total_lines = content.lines().count();

        for line in content.lines() {
            let trimmed = line.trim();

            if trimmed.is_empty() {
                blank_lines += 1;
            } else if self.is_comment_line(trimmed) {
                comment_lines += 1;
            } else {
                logical_lines += 1;
            }
        }

        LineMetrics {
            logical_lines,
            comment_lines,
            blank_lines,
            total_lines,
        }
    }

    /// Check if a line is primarily a comment
    fn is_comment_line(&amp;self, line: &amp;str) -&gt; bool {
        let trimmed = line.trim();

        // Common comment patterns
        trimmed.starts_with(&quot;//&quot;)
            || trimmed.starts_with(&quot;#&quot;)
            || trimmed.starts_with(&quot;/*&quot;)
            || trimmed.starts_with(&quot;*&quot;)
            || trimmed.starts_with(&quot;*/&quot;)
            || trimmed.starts_with(&quot;&lt;!--&quot;)
            || trimmed.starts_with(&quot;--&quot;)
            || trimmed.starts_with(&quot;%&quot;)
            || trimmed.starts_with(&quot;;&quot;)
    }

    /// Calculate cyclomatic complexity (FAST version - no regex, minimal string ops)
    fn calculate_cyclomatic_complexity(&amp;self, content: &amp;str, language: &amp;str) -&gt; usize {
        let mut complexity = 1; // Base complexity

        // Use simple byte-based counting instead of expensive string matching
        match language.to_lowercase().as_str() {
            &quot;rust&quot; =&gt; {
                // Count key complexity indicators quickly
                complexity += content.matches(&quot; if &quot;).count();
                complexity += content.matches(&quot; else &quot;).count();
                complexity += content.matches(&quot; match &quot;).count();
                complexity += content.matches(&quot; while &quot;).count();
                complexity += content.matches(&quot; for &quot;).count();
                complexity += content.matches(&quot;?&quot;).count(); // Error handling
                complexity += content.matches(&quot;&amp;&amp;&quot;).count();
                complexity += content.matches(&quot;||&quot;).count();
            }
            &quot;python&quot; =&gt; {
                complexity += content.matches(&quot; if &quot;).count();
                complexity += content.matches(&quot; elif &quot;).count();
                complexity += content.matches(&quot; while &quot;).count();
                complexity += content.matches(&quot; for &quot;).count();
                complexity += content.matches(&quot; except &quot;).count();
                complexity += content.matches(&quot; and &quot;).count();
                complexity += content.matches(&quot; or &quot;).count();
            }
            &quot;javascript&quot; | &quot;typescript&quot; =&gt; {
                complexity += content.matches(&quot; if &quot;).count();
                complexity += content.matches(&quot; while &quot;).count();
                complexity += content.matches(&quot; for &quot;).count();
                complexity += content.matches(&quot; catch &quot;).count();
                complexity += content.matches(&quot;&amp;&amp;&quot;).count();
                complexity += content.matches(&quot;||&quot;).count();
                complexity += content.matches(&quot;?&quot;).count();
            }
            _ =&gt; {
                // Generic fallback - just count some basic patterns
                complexity += content.matches(&quot; if &quot;).count();
                complexity += content.matches(&quot; while &quot;).count();
                complexity += content.matches(&quot; for &quot;).count();
            }
        }

        complexity.max(1) // Ensure minimum complexity of 1
    }

    /// Get complexity-increasing keywords for a language
    fn get_complexity_keywords(&amp;self, language: &amp;str) -&gt; Vec&lt;&amp;&#x27;static str&gt; {
        match language.to_lowercase().as_str() {
            &quot;rust&quot; =&gt; vec![
                &quot;if&quot;, &quot;else if&quot;, &quot;match&quot;, &quot;while&quot;, &quot;for&quot;, &quot;loop&quot;, &quot;catch&quot;, &quot;?&quot;, &quot;&amp;&amp;&quot;, &quot;||&quot;,
                &quot;break&quot;, &quot;continue&quot;,
            ],
            &quot;python&quot; =&gt; vec![
                &quot;if&quot;, &quot;elif&quot;, &quot;while&quot;, &quot;for&quot;, &quot;except&quot;, &quot;and&quot;, &quot;or&quot;, &quot;break&quot;, &quot;continue&quot;, &quot;return&quot;,
                &quot;yield&quot;,
            ],
            &quot;javascript&quot; | &quot;typescript&quot; =&gt; vec![
                &quot;if&quot;, &quot;else if&quot;, &quot;while&quot;, &quot;for&quot;, &quot;catch&quot;, &quot;case&quot;, &quot;&amp;&amp;&quot;, &quot;||&quot;, &quot;?&quot;, &quot;break&quot;,
                &quot;continue&quot;, &quot;return&quot;,
            ],
            &quot;java&quot; | &quot;c#&quot; =&gt; vec![
                &quot;if&quot;, &quot;else if&quot;, &quot;while&quot;, &quot;for&quot;, &quot;foreach&quot;, &quot;catch&quot;, &quot;case&quot;, &quot;&amp;&amp;&quot;, &quot;||&quot;, &quot;?&quot;,
                &quot;break&quot;, &quot;continue&quot;, &quot;return&quot;,
            ],
            &quot;go&quot; =&gt; vec![
                &quot;if&quot;, &quot;else if&quot;, &quot;for&quot;, &quot;switch&quot;, &quot;case&quot;, &quot;select&quot;, &quot;&amp;&amp;&quot;, &quot;||&quot;, &quot;break&quot;,
                &quot;continue&quot;, &quot;return&quot;,
            ],
            &quot;c&quot; | &quot;cpp&quot; | &quot;c++&quot; =&gt; vec![
                &quot;if&quot;, &quot;else if&quot;, &quot;while&quot;, &quot;for&quot;, &quot;switch&quot;, &quot;case&quot;, &quot;&amp;&amp;&quot;, &quot;||&quot;, &quot;?&quot;, &quot;break&quot;,
                &quot;continue&quot;, &quot;return&quot;,
            ],
            _ =&gt; vec![
                &quot;if&quot;, &quot;else&quot;, &quot;while&quot;, &quot;for&quot;, &quot;switch&quot;, &quot;case&quot;, &quot;&amp;&amp;&quot;, &quot;||&quot;, &quot;?&quot;, &quot;break&quot;,
                &quot;continue&quot;, &quot;return&quot;,
            ],
        }
    }

    /// Calculate maximum nesting depth (FAST version - no char iteration)
    fn calculate_max_nesting_depth(&amp;self, content: &amp;str, _language: &amp;str) -&gt; usize {
        let mut max_depth: usize = 0;
        let mut current_depth: usize = 0;

        // Simple heuristic: count braces on each line (much faster than char-by-char)
        for line in content.lines() {
            // Count opening and closing braces in one pass
            let opens = line.matches(&#x27;{&#x27;).count();
            let closes = line.matches(&#x27;}&#x27;).count();

            current_depth += opens;
            max_depth = max_depth.max(current_depth);
            current_depth = current_depth.saturating_sub(closes);
        }

        max_depth
    }

    /// Get nesting characters for a language
    fn get_nesting_chars(&amp;self, language: &amp;str) -&gt; (Vec&lt;char&gt;, Vec&lt;char&gt;) {
        match language.to_lowercase().as_str() {
            &quot;python&quot; =&gt; {
                // Python uses indentation, but we can still track some nesting
                (vec![&#x27;{&#x27;, &#x27;[&#x27;, &#x27;(&#x27;], vec![&#x27;}&#x27;, &#x27;]&#x27;, &#x27;)&#x27;])
            }
            _ =&gt; {
                // Most C-style languages
                (vec![&#x27;{&#x27;, &#x27;[&#x27;, &#x27;(&#x27;], vec![&#x27;}&#x27;, &#x27;]&#x27;, &#x27;)&#x27;])
            }
        }
    }

    /// Count functions in the content
    fn count_functions(&amp;self, content: &amp;str, language: &amp;str) -&gt; usize {
        let function_keywords = self.get_function_keywords(language);
        let mut count = 0;

        for line in content.lines() {
            let line = line.trim();

            for keyword in &amp;function_keywords {
                if line.starts_with(keyword) || line.contains(&amp;format!(&quot; {}&quot;, keyword)) {
                    count += 1;
                    break; // Only count once per line
                }
            }
        }

        count
    }

    /// Get function declaration keywords for a language
    fn get_function_keywords(&amp;self, language: &amp;str) -&gt; Vec&lt;&amp;&#x27;static str&gt; {
        match language.to_lowercase().as_str() {
            &quot;rust&quot; =&gt; vec![&quot;fn &quot;, &quot;pub fn &quot;, &quot;async fn &quot;, &quot;pub async fn &quot;],
            &quot;python&quot; =&gt; vec![&quot;def &quot;, &quot;async def &quot;, &quot;class &quot;],
            &quot;javascript&quot; | &quot;typescript&quot; =&gt; {
                vec![&quot;function &quot;, &quot;const &quot;, &quot;let &quot;, &quot;var &quot;, &quot;async function &quot;]
            }
            &quot;java&quot; =&gt; vec![&quot;public &quot;, &quot;private &quot;, &quot;protected &quot;, &quot;static &quot;],
            &quot;c#&quot; =&gt; vec![&quot;public &quot;, &quot;private &quot;, &quot;protected &quot;, &quot;internal &quot;, &quot;static &quot;],
            &quot;go&quot; =&gt; vec![&quot;func &quot;],
            &quot;c&quot; | &quot;cpp&quot; | &quot;c++&quot; =&gt; vec![&quot;int &quot;, &quot;void &quot;, &quot;char &quot;, &quot;float &quot;, &quot;double &quot;, &quot;static &quot;],
            _ =&gt; vec![&quot;function &quot;, &quot;def &quot;, &quot;fn &quot;],
        }
    }

    /// Calculate cognitive complexity (more intuitive than cyclomatic)
    fn calculate_cognitive_complexity(&amp;self, content: &amp;str, language: &amp;str) -&gt; usize {
        let mut complexity: usize = 0;
        let mut nesting_level: usize = 0;

        for line in content.lines() {
            let line = line.trim().to_lowercase();

            // Track nesting level changes
            if line.contains(&#x27;{&#x27;) {
                nesting_level += 1;
            }
            if line.contains(&#x27;}&#x27;) {
                nesting_level = nesting_level.saturating_sub(1);
            }

            // Cognitive complexity increments
            if line.contains(&quot;if&quot;) || line.contains(&quot;while&quot;) || line.contains(&quot;for&quot;) {
                complexity += 1 + nesting_level; // Base increment + nesting penalty
            }

            if line.contains(&quot;else if&quot;) || line.contains(&quot;elif&quot;) {
                complexity += 1;
            }

            if line.contains(&quot;catch&quot;) || line.contains(&quot;except&quot;) {
                complexity += 1 + nesting_level;
            }

            if line.contains(&quot;switch&quot;) || line.contains(&quot;match&quot;) {
                complexity += 1 + nesting_level;
            }

            // Recursive calls add complexity
            if self.has_recursive_call(&amp;line, language) {
                complexity += 1;
            }
        }

        complexity
    }

    /// Check if a line contains a recursive call
    fn has_recursive_call(&amp;self, line: &amp;str, _language: &amp;str) -&gt; bool {
        // Simple heuristic: look for function calls that might be recursive
        line.contains(&quot;self.&quot;)
            || line.contains(&quot;this.&quot;)
            || line.contains(&quot;recursive&quot;)
            || line.contains(&quot;recurse&quot;)
    }

    /// Calculate maintainability index (Halstead-based)
    fn calculate_maintainability_index(
        &amp;self,
        line_metrics: &amp;LineMetrics,
        cyclomatic: usize,
        functions: usize,
    ) -&gt; f64 {
        // Simplified maintainability index calculation
        // Real calculation would use Halstead metrics

        let volume = (line_metrics.logical_lines as f64).ln();
        let complexity = cyclomatic as f64;
        let lloc = line_metrics.logical_lines as f64;

        // Simplified formula (real one is more complex)
        let mi = 171.0 - 5.2 * volume - 0.23 * complexity - 16.2 * lloc.ln();

        // Normalize to 0-100 range
        mi.max(0.0).min(100.0)
    }

    /// Analyze language-specific metrics
    fn analyze_language_specific(&amp;self, content: &amp;str, language: &amp;str) -&gt; LanguageSpecificMetrics {
        let mut complexity_factors = HashMap::new();
        let import_count = self.count_imports(content, language);
        let export_count = self.count_exports(content, language);
        let api_surface_area = self.estimate_api_surface_area(content, language);

        // Language-specific complexity factors
        match language.to_lowercase().as_str() {
            &quot;rust&quot; =&gt; {
                complexity_factors.insert(
                    &quot;ownership_complexity&quot;.to_string(),
                    self.calculate_ownership_complexity(content),
                );
                complexity_factors.insert(
                    &quot;trait_complexity&quot;.to_string(),
                    self.count_trait_usage(content) as f64,
                );
                complexity_factors.insert(
                    &quot;macro_complexity&quot;.to_string(),
                    self.count_macro_usage(content) as f64,
                );
            }
            &quot;python&quot; =&gt; {
                complexity_factors.insert(
                    &quot;decorator_complexity&quot;.to_string(),
                    self.count_decorators(content) as f64,
                );
                complexity_factors.insert(
                    &quot;comprehension_complexity&quot;.to_string(),
                    self.count_comprehensions(content) as f64,
                );
            }
            &quot;javascript&quot; | &quot;typescript&quot; =&gt; {
                complexity_factors.insert(
                    &quot;closure_complexity&quot;.to_string(),
                    self.count_closures(content) as f64,
                );
                complexity_factors.insert(
                    &quot;promise_complexity&quot;.to_string(),
                    self.count_async_patterns(content) as f64,
                );
            }
            _ =&gt; {
                // Generic complexity factors
                complexity_factors.insert(&quot;generic_complexity&quot;.to_string(), 1.0);
            }
        }

        LanguageSpecificMetrics {
            language: language.to_string(),
            complexity_factors,
            import_count,
            export_count,
            api_surface_area,
        }
    }

    /// Count import statements
    fn count_imports(&amp;self, content: &amp;str, language: &amp;str) -&gt; usize {
        let import_patterns = match language.to_lowercase().as_str() {
            &quot;rust&quot; =&gt; vec![&quot;use &quot;, &quot;extern crate &quot;],
            &quot;python&quot; =&gt; vec![&quot;import &quot;, &quot;from &quot;],
            &quot;javascript&quot; | &quot;typescript&quot; =&gt; vec![&quot;import &quot;, &quot;require(&quot;, &quot;const &quot;, &quot;let &quot;],
            &quot;java&quot; =&gt; vec![&quot;import &quot;],
            &quot;go&quot; =&gt; vec![&quot;import &quot;],
            _ =&gt; vec![&quot;import &quot;, &quot;include &quot;, &quot;use &quot;],
        };

        content
            .lines()
            .filter(|line| {
                let trimmed = line.trim();
                import_patterns
                    .iter()
                    .any(|pattern| trimmed.starts_with(pattern))
            })
            .count()
    }

    /// Count export statements
    fn count_exports(&amp;self, content: &amp;str, language: &amp;str) -&gt; usize {
        let export_patterns = match language.to_lowercase().as_str() {
            &quot;rust&quot; =&gt; vec![&quot;pub fn &quot;, &quot;pub struct &quot;, &quot;pub enum &quot;, &quot;pub trait &quot;],
            &quot;python&quot; =&gt; vec![&quot;def &quot;, &quot;class &quot;], // Python exports everything by default
            &quot;javascript&quot; | &quot;typescript&quot; =&gt; vec![&quot;export &quot;, &quot;module.exports&quot;],
            &quot;java&quot; =&gt; vec![&quot;public class &quot;, &quot;public interface &quot;, &quot;public enum &quot;],
            _ =&gt; vec![&quot;public &quot;, &quot;export &quot;],
        };

        content
            .lines()
            .filter(|line| {
                let trimmed = line.trim();
                export_patterns
                    .iter()
                    .any(|pattern| trimmed.contains(pattern))
            })
            .count()
    }

    /// Estimate API surface area
    fn estimate_api_surface_area(&amp;self, content: &amp;str, language: &amp;str) -&gt; usize {
        // Simple heuristic: count public functions, classes, etc.
        let public_items = self.count_exports(content, language);
        let function_count = self.count_functions(content, language);

        // API surface area is roughly the number of publicly accessible items
        public_items.min(function_count)
    }

    // Language-specific complexity calculations
    fn calculate_ownership_complexity(&amp;self, content: &amp;str) -&gt; f64 {
        let ownership_keywords = [&quot;&amp;&quot;, &quot;&amp;mut&quot;, &quot;Box&lt;&quot;, &quot;Rc&lt;&quot;, &quot;Arc&lt;&quot;, &quot;RefCell&lt;&quot;, &quot;Mutex&lt;&quot;];
        let mut complexity = 0.0;

        for line in content.lines() {
            for keyword in &amp;ownership_keywords {
                complexity += line.matches(keyword).count() as f64 * 0.5;
            }
        }

        complexity
    }

    fn count_trait_usage(&amp;self, content: &amp;str) -&gt; usize {
        content
            .lines()
            .filter(|line| line.contains(&quot;trait &quot;) || line.contains(&quot;impl &quot;))
            .count()
    }

    fn count_macro_usage(&amp;self, content: &amp;str) -&gt; usize {
        content
            .lines()
            .filter(|line| line.contains(&quot;macro_rules!&quot;) || line.contains(&quot;!&quot;))
            .count()
    }

    fn count_decorators(&amp;self, content: &amp;str) -&gt; usize {
        content
            .lines()
            .filter(|line| line.trim().starts_with(&quot;@&quot;))
            .count()
    }

    fn count_comprehensions(&amp;self, content: &amp;str) -&gt; usize {
        content
            .lines()
            .filter(|line| {
                line.contains(&quot;[&quot;) &amp;&amp; line.contains(&quot;for &quot;) &amp;&amp; line.contains(&quot;in &quot;)
                    || line.contains(&quot;{&quot;) &amp;&amp; line.contains(&quot;for &quot;) &amp;&amp; line.contains(&quot;in &quot;)
            })
            .count()
    }

    fn count_closures(&amp;self, content: &amp;str) -&gt; usize {
        content
            .lines()
            .filter(|line| line.contains(&quot;=&gt;&quot;) || line.contains(&quot;function(&quot;))
            .count()
    }

    fn count_async_patterns(&amp;self, content: &amp;str) -&gt; usize {
        content
            .lines()
            .filter(|line| {
                line.contains(&quot;async&quot;)
                    || line.contains(&quot;await&quot;)
                    || line.contains(&quot;Promise&quot;)
                    || line.contains(&quot;.then(&quot;)
            })
            .count()
    }
}

/// Line-based metrics
#[derive(Debug)]
struct LineMetrics {
    logical_lines: usize,
    comment_lines: usize,
    blank_lines: usize,
    total_lines: usize,
}

impl Default for LanguageSpecificMetrics {
    fn default() -&gt; Self {
        Self::default(&quot;unknown&quot;)
    }
}

impl LanguageSpecificMetrics {
    fn default(language: &amp;str) -&gt; Self {
        Self {
            language: language.to_string(),
            complexity_factors: HashMap::new(),
            import_count: 0,
            export_count: 0,
            api_surface_area: 0,
        }
    }
}

impl ComplexityMetrics {
    /// Get a complexity score (0-1, where higher means more complex)
    pub fn complexity_score(&amp;self) -&gt; f64 {
        // Normalize various complexity metrics to a 0-1 score
        let cyclomatic_score = (self.cyclomatic_complexity as f64 / 20.0).min(1.0);
        let nesting_score = (self.max_nesting_depth as f64 / 8.0).min(1.0);
        let cognitive_score = (self.cognitive_complexity as f64 / 15.0).min(1.0);
        let maintainability_score = (100.0 - self.maintainability_index) / 100.0;

        // Weighted average
        (cyclomatic_score * 0.3
            + nesting_score * 0.2
            + cognitive_score * 0.3
            + maintainability_score * 0.2)
            .min(1.0)
    }

    /// Check if any complexity thresholds are exceeded
    pub fn exceeds_thresholds(&amp;self, thresholds: &amp;ComplexityThresholds) -&gt; Vec&lt;String&gt; {
        let mut warnings = Vec::new();

        if self.cyclomatic_complexity &gt; thresholds.cyclomatic_warning {
            warnings.push(format!(
                &quot;High cyclomatic complexity: {}&quot;,
                self.cyclomatic_complexity
            ));
        }

        if self.max_nesting_depth &gt; thresholds.nesting_warning {
            warnings.push(format!(&quot;Deep nesting: {}&quot;, self.max_nesting_depth));
        }

        if self.average_function_length &gt; thresholds.function_length_warning as f64 {
            warnings.push(format!(
                &quot;Long functions: avg {:.1} lines&quot;,
                self.average_function_length
            ));
        }

        if self.maintainability_index &lt; thresholds.maintainability_warning {
            warnings.push(format!(
                &quot;Low maintainability: {:.1}&quot;,
                self.maintainability_index
            ));
        }

        warnings
    }

    /// Get a human-readable summary
    pub fn summary(&amp;self) -&gt; String {
        format!(
            &quot;Complexity: CC={}, Depth={}, Functions={}, MI={:.1}, Cognitive={}&quot;,
            self.cyclomatic_complexity,
            self.max_nesting_depth,
            self.function_count,
            self.maintainability_index,
            self.cognitive_complexity
        )
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn test_analyzer_creation() {
        let analyzer = ComplexityAnalyzer::new();
        assert!(analyzer.config.enable_cognitive_complexity);
        assert!(analyzer.config.enable_maintainability_index);
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_simple_rust_analysis() {
        let analyzer = ComplexityAnalyzer::new();
        let content = r#&quot;
fn main() {
    if x &gt; 0 {
        println!(&quot;positive&quot;);
    } else {
        println!(&quot;negative&quot;);
    }
}
&quot;#;

        let metrics = analyzer.analyze_content(content, &quot;rust&quot;).unwrap();

        assert!(metrics.cyclomatic_complexity &gt;= 2); // if-else adds complexity
        assert!(metrics.function_count &gt;= 1);
        assert!(metrics.max_nesting_depth &gt;= 1);
        assert!(metrics.total_lines &gt; 0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_complex_code_analysis() {
        let analyzer = ComplexityAnalyzer::new();
        let content = r#&quot;
fn complex_function() {
    for i in 0..10 {
        if i % 2 == 0 {
            while some_condition() {
                if another_condition() {
                    match value {
                        1 =&gt; do_something(),
                        2 =&gt; do_something_else(),
                        _ =&gt; default_action(),
                    }
                }
            }
        } else {
            continue;
        }
    }
}
&quot;#;

        let metrics = analyzer.analyze_content(content, &quot;rust&quot;).unwrap();

        assert!(metrics.cyclomatic_complexity &gt; 5); // Multiple branches
        assert!(metrics.max_nesting_depth &gt; 3); // Deep nesting
        assert!(metrics.cognitive_complexity &gt; metrics.cyclomatic_complexity); // Cognitive should be higher due to nesting
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_line_analysis() {
        let analyzer = ComplexityAnalyzer::new();
        let content = r#&quot;
// This is a comment
fn test() {
    // Another comment
    let x = 5;
    
    // More comments
    println!(&quot;Hello&quot;);
}
&quot;#;

        let metrics = analyzer.analyze_content(content, &quot;rust&quot;).unwrap();

        assert!(metrics.comment_lines &gt; 0);
        assert!(metrics.blank_lines &gt; 0);
        assert!(metrics.logical_lines &gt; 0);
        assert!(metrics.comment_ratio &gt; 0.0);
        assert!(metrics.code_density &gt; 0.0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_language_specific_analysis() {
        let analyzer = ComplexityAnalyzer::new();

        // Test Rust-specific features
        let rust_content = r#&quot;
use std::collections::HashMap;
pub fn test() -&gt; Result&lt;(), Box&lt;dyn Error&gt;&gt; {
    let mut data: Vec&lt;&amp;str&gt; = vec![];
    Ok(())
}
&quot;#;

        let rust_metrics = analyzer.analyze_content(rust_content, &quot;rust&quot;).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(rust_metrics.language_metrics.language, &quot;rust&quot;);
        assert!(rust_metrics.language_metrics.import_count &gt; 0);

        // Test Python-specific features
        let python_content = r#&quot;
import os
from typing import List

@decorator
def test_function():
    result = [x for x in range(10) if x % 2 == 0]
    return result
&quot;#;

        let python_metrics = analyzer.analyze_content(python_content, &quot;python&quot;).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(python_metrics.language_metrics.language, &quot;python&quot;);
        assert!(python_metrics.language_metrics.import_count &gt; 0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_complexity_score() {
        let analyzer = ComplexityAnalyzer::new();

        // Simple code should have low complexity score
        let simple_content = &quot;fn main() { println!(\&quot;hello\&quot;); }&quot;;
        let simple_metrics = analyzer.analyze_content(simple_content, &quot;rust&quot;).unwrap();
        let simple_score = simple_metrics.complexity_score();

        // Complex code should have higher complexity score
        let complex_content = r#&quot;
fn complex() {
    for i in 0..100 {
        if i % 2 == 0 {
            while condition() {
                match value {
                    1 =&gt; { if nested() { deep(); } },
                    2 =&gt; { if more_nested() { deeper(); } },
                    _ =&gt; { if even_more() { deepest(); } },
                }
            }
        }
    }
}
&quot;#;
        let complex_metrics = analyzer.analyze_content(complex_content, &quot;rust&quot;).unwrap();
        let complex_score = complex_metrics.complexity_score();

        assert!(complex_score &gt; simple_score);
        assert!(simple_score &gt;= 0.0 &amp;&amp; simple_score &lt;= 1.0);
        assert!(complex_score &gt;= 0.0 &amp;&amp; complex_score &lt;= 1.0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_threshold_warnings() {
        let analyzer = ComplexityAnalyzer::new();
        let thresholds = ComplexityThresholds {
            cyclomatic_warning: 5,
            nesting_warning: 2,
            function_length_warning: 10,
            maintainability_warning: 50.0,
        };

        let complex_content = r#&quot;
fn complex_function() {
    for i in 0..10 {
        if i % 2 == 0 {
            while some_condition() {
                if another_condition() {
                    if yet_another() {
                        do_something();
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
}
&quot;#;

        let metrics = analyzer.analyze_content(complex_content, &quot;rust&quot;).unwrap();
        let warnings = metrics.exceeds_thresholds(&amp;thresholds);

        assert!(!warnings.is_empty());
        assert!(warnings.iter().any(|w| w.contains(&quot;complexity&quot;)));
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_metrics_summary() {
        let analyzer = ComplexityAnalyzer::new();
        let content = &quot;fn test() { if x &gt; 0 { return 1; } else { return 0; } }&quot;;
        let metrics = analyzer.analyze_content(content, &quot;rust&quot;).unwrap();

        let summary = metrics.summary();
        assert!(summary.contains(&quot;CC=&quot;));
        assert!(summary.contains(&quot;Depth=&quot;));
        assert!(summary.contains(&quot;Functions=&quot;));
        assert!(summary.contains(&quot;MI=&quot;));
        assert!(summary.contains(&quot;Cognitive=&quot;));
    }
}

//! # Enhanced Scoring System with Complexity Integration
//!
//! This module extends the basic heuristic scoring with comprehensive complexity analysis,
//! providing deeper insights into code quality and maintainability for better file selection.
//!
//! ## Enhanced Features
//!
//! - **Complexity-Aware Scoring**: Integrates cyclomatic, cognitive, and maintainability metrics
//! - **Quality-Based Prioritization**: Considers code quality alongside importance
//! - **Language-Specific Analysis**: Tailored complexity analysis per programming language
//! - **Maintainability Assessment**: Factors in long-term code maintenance concerns
//! - **Adaptive Weights**: Adjusts scoring based on repository characteristics

use super::scoring::RawScoreComponents;
use super::{HeuristicWeights, ScanResult, ScoreComponents};
use crate::complexity::{ComplexityAnalyzer, ComplexityConfig, ComplexityMetrics};
use rayon::prelude::*;
use scribe_core::{Result, ScribeError};
use std::collections::HashMap;

/// Enhanced score components that include complexity metrics
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct EnhancedScoreComponents {
    /// Base score components from standard heuristics
    pub base_score: ScoreComponents,

    /// Complexity-based scores
    pub complexity_score: f64,
    pub maintainability_score: f64,
    pub cognitive_score: f64,
    pub quality_score: f64,

    /// Combined final score
    pub enhanced_final_score: f64,

    /// Detailed complexity metrics
    pub complexity_metrics: Option&lt;ComplexityMetrics&gt;,

    /// Complexity-adjusted weights
    pub adjusted_weights: EnhancedWeights,
}

/// Enhanced weights that include complexity factors
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct EnhancedWeights {
    /// Base heuristic weights
    pub base_weights: HeuristicWeights,

    /// Complexity weight factors
    pub complexity_weight: f64,
    pub maintainability_weight: f64,
    pub cognitive_weight: f64,
    pub quality_weight: f64,

    /// Adaptive weight adjustments
    pub adaptive_factors: AdaptiveFactors,
}

/// Adaptive factors that adjust scoring based on repository characteristics
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct AdaptiveFactors {
    /// Repository size factor (larger repos may prefer simpler files)
    pub repo_size_factor: f64,

    /// Language complexity factor (some languages naturally more complex)
    pub language_factor: f64,

    /// Project maturity factor (mature projects may prioritize maintainability)
    pub maturity_factor: f64,

    /// Team experience factor (affects complexity tolerance)
    pub experience_factor: f64,
}

/// Enhanced heuristic scorer with complexity integration
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct EnhancedHeuristicScorer {
    /// Base scorer for standard heuristics
    base_scorer: super::scoring::HeuristicScorer,

    /// Complexity analyzer
    complexity_analyzer: ComplexityAnalyzer,

    /// Enhanced weights configuration
    weights: EnhancedWeights,

    /// Repository characteristics for adaptive scoring
    repo_characteristics: RepositoryCharacteristics,

    /// Content cache for complexity analysis
    content_cache: HashMap&lt;String, ComplexityMetrics&gt;,

    /// Whether to enable expensive complexity analysis (disabled by default for performance)
    enable_complexity_analysis: bool,
}

/// Repository characteristics for adaptive scoring
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct RepositoryCharacteristics {
    /// Total number of files in repository
    pub total_files: usize,

    /// Primary programming languages
    pub primary_languages: Vec&lt;String&gt;,

    /// Repository age in months
    pub age_months: usize,

    /// Average team size
    pub team_size: usize,

    /// Project type (library, application, framework, etc.)
    pub project_type: ProjectType,
}

/// Project type classification
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub enum ProjectType {
    Library,
    Application,
    Framework,
    Tool,
    Game,
    WebService,
    EmbeddedSystem,
    Unknown,
}

impl Default for EnhancedWeights {
    fn default() -&gt; Self {
        Self {
            base_weights: HeuristicWeights::default(),
            complexity_weight: 0.15,
            maintainability_weight: 0.20,
            cognitive_weight: 0.10,
            quality_weight: 0.15,
            adaptive_factors: AdaptiveFactors::default(),
        }
    }
}

impl Default for AdaptiveFactors {
    fn default() -&gt; Self {
        Self {
            repo_size_factor: 1.0,
            language_factor: 1.0,
            maturity_factor: 1.0,
            experience_factor: 1.0,
        }
    }
}

impl Default for RepositoryCharacteristics {
    fn default() -&gt; Self {
        Self {
            total_files: 100,
            primary_languages: vec![&quot;rust&quot;.to_string()],
            age_months: 12,
            team_size: 3,
            project_type: ProjectType::Application,
        }
    }
}

impl EnhancedHeuristicScorer {
    /// Create a new enhanced scorer with default configuration
    pub fn new() -&gt; Self {
        let base_weights = HeuristicWeights::default();
        let base_scorer = super::scoring::HeuristicScorer::new(base_weights.clone());

        Self {
            base_scorer,
            complexity_analyzer: ComplexityAnalyzer::new(),
            weights: EnhancedWeights::default(),
            repo_characteristics: RepositoryCharacteristics::default(),
            content_cache: HashMap::new(),
            enable_complexity_analysis: false, // TEMPORARILY DISABLED to test baseline performance
        }
    }

    /// Enable complexity analysis (WARNING: This significantly impacts performance)
    pub fn enable_complexity_analysis(&amp;mut self) {
        self.enable_complexity_analysis = true;
    }

    /// Disable complexity analysis for better performance
    pub fn disable_complexity_analysis(&amp;mut self) {
        self.enable_complexity_analysis = false;
        self.content_cache.clear(); // Clear cache to save memory
    }

    /// Create enhanced scorer with custom configuration
    pub fn with_config(
        weights: EnhancedWeights,
        complexity_config: ComplexityConfig,
        repo_characteristics: RepositoryCharacteristics,
    ) -&gt; Self {
        let base_scorer = super::scoring::HeuristicScorer::new(weights.base_weights.clone());
        let complexity_analyzer = ComplexityAnalyzer::with_config(complexity_config);

        Self {
            base_scorer,
            complexity_analyzer,
            weights,
            repo_characteristics,
            content_cache: HashMap::new(),
            enable_complexity_analysis: false, // TEMPORARILY DISABLED to test baseline performance
        }
    }

    /// Score a file with enhanced complexity-aware analysis
    pub fn score_file_enhanced&lt;T&gt;(
        &amp;mut self,
        file: &amp;T,
        file_content: &amp;str,
        all_files: &amp;[T],
    ) -&gt; Result&lt;EnhancedScoreComponents&gt;
    where
        T: ScanResult + Clone,
    {
        // Get base heuristic score
        let base_score = self.base_scorer.score_file(file, all_files)?;

        // Detect language from file path
        let language = self.detect_language(file.path());

        // Analyze complexity only if enabled (with caching)
        let (
            complexity_metrics,
            complexity_score,
            maintainability_score,
            cognitive_score,
            quality_score,
        ) = if self.enable_complexity_analysis {
            let complexity_metrics = if let Some(cached) = self.content_cache.get(file.path()) {
                cached.clone()
            } else {
                let metrics = self
                    .complexity_analyzer
                    .analyze_content(file_content, &amp;language)?;
                self.content_cache
                    .insert(file.path().to_string(), metrics.clone());
                metrics
            };

            // Calculate complexity-based scores
            let complexity_score = self.calculate_complexity_score(&amp;complexity_metrics);
            let maintainability_score = self.calculate_maintainability_score(&amp;complexity_metrics);
            let cognitive_score = self.calculate_cognitive_score(&amp;complexity_metrics);
            let quality_score = self.calculate_quality_score(&amp;complexity_metrics);

            (
                Some(complexity_metrics),
                complexity_score,
                maintainability_score,
                cognitive_score,
                quality_score,
            )
        } else {
            // Skip expensive complexity analysis - use neutral/default scores
            (None, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5)
        };

        // Apply adaptive adjustments
        let adjusted_weights = if let Some(ref metrics) = complexity_metrics {
            self.calculate_adaptive_weights(file, metrics)
        } else {
            // Use default weights when complexity analysis is disabled
            self.weights.clone()
        };

        // Calculate enhanced final score
        let enhanced_final_score = self.calculate_enhanced_final_score(
            &amp;base_score,
            complexity_score,
            maintainability_score,
            cognitive_score,
            quality_score,
            &amp;adjusted_weights,
        );

        Ok(EnhancedScoreComponents {
            base_score,
            complexity_score,
            maintainability_score,
            cognitive_score,
            quality_score,
            enhanced_final_score,
            complexity_metrics,
            adjusted_weights,
        })
    }

    /// Score all files with enhanced analysis
    pub fn score_all_files_enhanced&lt;T&gt;(
        &amp;mut self,
        files_with_content: &amp;[(T, String)],
    ) -&gt; Result&lt;Vec&lt;(usize, EnhancedScoreComponents)&gt;&gt;
    where
        T: ScanResult + Clone + Sync + Send,
    {
        let files: Vec&lt;_&gt; = files_with_content.iter().map(|(f, _)| f.clone()).collect();

        // PERFORMANCE OPTIMIZATION: Parallelize complexity analysis first
        let complexity_results: Result&lt;HashMap&lt;usize, Option&lt;ComplexityMetrics&gt;&gt;&gt; =
            if self.enable_complexity_analysis {
                // Create a snapshot of cache for parallel access
                let cache_snapshot: HashMap&lt;String, ComplexityMetrics&gt; = self.content_cache.clone();

                // Compute complexity metrics in parallel for all files
                let results: Result&lt;Vec&lt;(usize, Option&lt;ComplexityMetrics&gt;)&gt;&gt; = files_with_content
                    .par_iter()
                    .enumerate()
                    .map(|(idx, (file, content))| {
                        // Check cache first
                        if let Some(cached) = cache_snapshot.get(file.path()) {
                            return Ok((idx, Some(cached.clone())));
                        }

                        // Detect language and analyze complexity
                        let language = Self::detect_language_static(file.path());
                        let analyzer = ComplexityAnalyzer::new();

                        match analyzer.analyze_content(content, &amp;language) {
                            Ok(metrics) =&gt; Ok((idx, Some(metrics))),
                            Err(_) =&gt; Ok((idx, None)), // Skip files that can&#x27;t be analyzed
                        }
                    })
                    .collect();

                results.map(|vec| vec.into_iter().collect())
            } else {
                Ok(HashMap::new())
            };

        let complexity_results = complexity_results?;

        // Update cache with new results (sequential for cache safety)
        for (idx, metrics_opt) in &amp;complexity_results {
            if let Some(metrics) = metrics_opt {
                let file_path = files_with_content[*idx].0.path().to_string();
                self.content_cache.insert(file_path, metrics.clone());
            }
        }

        // Now score all files sequentially with pre-computed complexity metrics
        let mut scored_files = Vec::new();
        for (idx, (file, content)) in files_with_content.iter().enumerate() {
            let score = self.score_file_enhanced_with_precomputed_complexity(
                file,
                content,
                &amp;files,
                complexity_results.get(&amp;idx).and_then(|opt| opt.as_ref()),
            )?;
            scored_files.push((idx, score));
        }

        // Sort by enhanced final score (descending)
        scored_files.sort_by(|a, b| {
            b.1.enhanced_final_score
                .partial_cmp(&amp;a.1.enhanced_final_score)
                .unwrap_or(std::cmp::Ordering::Equal)
        });

        Ok(scored_files)
    }

    /// Score a file with pre-computed complexity metrics (for parallel optimization)
    fn score_file_enhanced_with_precomputed_complexity&lt;T&gt;(
        &amp;mut self,
        file: &amp;T,
        file_content: &amp;str,
        all_files: &amp;[T],
        precomputed_complexity: Option&lt;&amp;ComplexityMetrics&gt;,
    ) -&gt; Result&lt;EnhancedScoreComponents&gt;
    where
        T: ScanResult + Clone,
    {
        // Get base heuristic score
        let base_score = self.base_scorer.score_file(file, all_files)?;

        // Use pre-computed complexity metrics or defaults
        let (
            complexity_metrics,
            complexity_score,
            maintainability_score,
            cognitive_score,
            quality_score,
        ) = if let Some(metrics) = precomputed_complexity {
            // Use pre-computed metrics
            let complexity_score = self.calculate_complexity_score(metrics);
            let maintainability_score = self.calculate_maintainability_score(metrics);
            let cognitive_score = self.calculate_cognitive_score(metrics);
            let quality_score = self.calculate_quality_score(metrics);

            (
                Some(metrics.clone()),
                complexity_score,
                maintainability_score,
                cognitive_score,
                quality_score,
            )
        } else {
            // Skip expensive complexity analysis - use neutral/default scores
            (None, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5)
        };

        // Apply adaptive adjustments
        let adjusted_weights = if let Some(ref metrics) = complexity_metrics {
            self.calculate_adaptive_weights(file, metrics)
        } else {
            // Use default weights when complexity analysis is disabled
            self.weights.clone()
        };

        // Calculate enhanced final score
        let enhanced_final_score = self.calculate_enhanced_final_score(
            &amp;base_score,
            complexity_score,
            maintainability_score,
            cognitive_score,
            quality_score,
            &amp;adjusted_weights,
        );

        Ok(EnhancedScoreComponents {
            base_score,
            complexity_score,
            maintainability_score,
            cognitive_score,
            quality_score,
            enhanced_final_score,
            complexity_metrics,
            adjusted_weights,
        })
    }

    /// Detect programming language from file path
    fn detect_language(&amp;self, path: &amp;str) -&gt; String {
        Self::detect_language_static(path)
    }

    /// Static version for parallel processing
    fn detect_language_static(path: &amp;str) -&gt; String {
        let extension = std::path::Path::new(path)
            .extension()
            .and_then(|ext| ext.to_str())
            .unwrap_or(&quot;&quot;);

        match extension.to_lowercase().as_str() {
            &quot;rs&quot; =&gt; &quot;rust&quot;,
            &quot;py&quot; =&gt; &quot;python&quot;,
            &quot;js&quot; =&gt; &quot;javascript&quot;,
            &quot;ts&quot; =&gt; &quot;typescript&quot;,
            &quot;java&quot; =&gt; &quot;java&quot;,
            &quot;cs&quot; =&gt; &quot;c#&quot;,
            &quot;go&quot; =&gt; &quot;go&quot;,
            &quot;c&quot; =&gt; &quot;c&quot;,
            &quot;cpp&quot; | &quot;cc&quot; | &quot;cxx&quot; =&gt; &quot;cpp&quot;,
            &quot;h&quot; | &quot;hpp&quot; =&gt; &quot;c&quot;,
            &quot;rb&quot; =&gt; &quot;ruby&quot;,
            &quot;php&quot; =&gt; &quot;php&quot;,
            &quot;swift&quot; =&gt; &quot;swift&quot;,
            &quot;kt&quot; =&gt; &quot;kotlin&quot;,
            &quot;scala&quot; =&gt; &quot;scala&quot;,
            _ =&gt; &quot;unknown&quot;,
        }
        .to_string()
    }

    /// Calculate complexity-based score (0-1, where 1 is good)
    fn calculate_complexity_score(&amp;self, metrics: &amp;ComplexityMetrics) -&gt; f64 {
        // Invert complexity score - lower complexity is better
        1.0 - metrics.complexity_score()
    }

    /// Calculate maintainability score (0-1)
    fn calculate_maintainability_score(&amp;self, metrics: &amp;ComplexityMetrics) -&gt; f64 {
        // Maintainability index is 0-100, normalize to 0-1
        metrics.maintainability_index / 100.0
    }

    /// Calculate cognitive load score (0-1, where 1 is good)
    fn calculate_cognitive_score(&amp;self, metrics: &amp;ComplexityMetrics) -&gt; f64 {
        // Lower cognitive complexity is better
        let cognitive_ratio = metrics.cognitive_complexity as f64 / 20.0; // Normalize to rough 0-1 range
        (1.0 - cognitive_ratio.min(1.0)).max(0.0)
    }

    /// Calculate overall quality score (0-1)
    fn calculate_quality_score(&amp;self, metrics: &amp;ComplexityMetrics) -&gt; f64 {
        // Composite quality score
        let complexity_factor = 1.0 - (metrics.cyclomatic_complexity as f64 / 15.0).min(1.0);
        let nesting_factor = 1.0 - (metrics.max_nesting_depth as f64 / 6.0).min(1.0);
        let density_factor = metrics.code_density.min(1.0);
        let comment_factor = (metrics.comment_ratio * 2.0).min(1.0); // Good commenting is valuable

        (complexity_factor * 0.3
            + nesting_factor * 0.2
            + density_factor * 0.3
            + comment_factor * 0.2)
            .min(1.0)
    }

    /// Calculate adaptive weights based on file and repository characteristics
    fn calculate_adaptive_weights&lt;T&gt;(
        &amp;self,
        file: &amp;T,
        metrics: &amp;ComplexityMetrics,
    ) -&gt; EnhancedWeights
    where
        T: ScanResult,
    {
        let mut weights = self.weights.clone();

        // Adjust weights based on repository size
        if self.repo_characteristics.total_files &gt; 1000 {
            // Large repos: prioritize simplicity and maintainability
            weights.maintainability_weight *= 1.3;
            weights.complexity_weight *= 1.2;
        } else if self.repo_characteristics.total_files &lt; 50 {
            // Small repos: focus more on functionality
            weights.base_weights.import_weight *= 1.2;
            weights.base_weights.doc_weight *= 1.1;
        }

        // Adjust based on project type
        match self.repo_characteristics.project_type {
            ProjectType::Library =&gt; {
                // Libraries need excellent documentation and maintainability
                weights.base_weights.doc_weight *= 1.4;
                weights.maintainability_weight *= 1.3;
                weights.quality_weight *= 1.2;
            }
            ProjectType::Framework =&gt; {
                // Frameworks need clear architecture and examples
                weights.base_weights.entrypoint_weight *= 1.3;
                weights.base_weights.examples_weight *= 1.4;
                weights.quality_weight *= 1.2;
            }
            ProjectType::Tool =&gt; {
                // Tools prioritize main functionality and simplicity
                weights.base_weights.entrypoint_weight *= 1.5;
                weights.complexity_weight *= 1.3;
            }
            _ =&gt; {
                // Default adjustments for applications
            }
        }

        // Adjust based on file complexity
        if metrics.cyclomatic_complexity &gt; 10 {
            // High complexity files might be core logic - boost importance
            weights.base_weights.import_weight *= 1.2;
        }

        if metrics.maintainability_index &lt; 30.0 {
            // Low maintainability - might indicate technical debt hotspots
            weights.maintainability_weight *= 1.4;
        }

        // Language-specific adjustments
        let language = &amp;metrics.language_metrics.language;
        match language.as_str() {
            &quot;rust&quot; =&gt; {
                // Rust: Consider ownership complexity
                if let Some(ownership) = metrics
                    .language_metrics
                    .complexity_factors
                    .get(&quot;ownership_complexity&quot;)
                {
                    if *ownership &gt; 5.0 {
                        weights.complexity_weight *= 1.2;
                    }
                }
            }
            &quot;python&quot; =&gt; {
                // Python: Value documentation and simplicity
                weights.base_weights.doc_weight *= 1.1;
                weights.complexity_weight *= 1.1;
            }
            &quot;javascript&quot; | &quot;typescript&quot; =&gt; {
                // JS/TS: Consider async complexity
                if let Some(async_complexity) = metrics
                    .language_metrics
                    .complexity_factors
                    .get(&quot;promise_complexity&quot;)
                {
                    if *async_complexity &gt; 3.0 {
                        weights.cognitive_weight *= 1.2;
                    }
                }
            }
            _ =&gt; {}
        }

        weights
    }

    /// Calculate the final enhanced score
    fn calculate_enhanced_final_score(
        &amp;self,
        base_score: &amp;ScoreComponents,
        complexity_score: f64,
        maintainability_score: f64,
        cognitive_score: f64,
        quality_score: f64,
        weights: &amp;EnhancedWeights,
    ) -&gt; f64 {
        // Combine base score with complexity metrics
        let base_contribution = base_score.final_score * 0.6; // Base heuristics weight

        let complexity_contribution = complexity_score * weights.complexity_weight
            + maintainability_score * weights.maintainability_weight
            + cognitive_score * weights.cognitive_weight
            + quality_score * weights.quality_weight;

        let enhanced_contribution = complexity_contribution * 0.4; // Complexity metrics weight

        // Apply adaptive factors
        let final_score = (base_contribution + enhanced_contribution)
            * weights.adaptive_factors.repo_size_factor
            * weights.adaptive_factors.language_factor
            * weights.adaptive_factors.maturity_factor
            * weights.adaptive_factors.experience_factor;

        final_score.min(2.0) // Cap the score to prevent extreme values
    }

    /// Update repository characteristics
    pub fn update_repository_characteristics(
        &amp;mut self,
        characteristics: RepositoryCharacteristics,
    ) {
        self.repo_characteristics = characteristics;

        // Recalculate adaptive factors based on new characteristics
        self.weights.adaptive_factors = self.calculate_adaptive_factors();
    }

    /// Calculate adaptive factors based on repository characteristics
    fn calculate_adaptive_factors(&amp;self) -&gt; AdaptiveFactors {
        let repo_size_factor = match self.repo_characteristics.total_files {
            0..=50 =&gt; 1.1,      // Small repos - boost importance
            51..=500 =&gt; 1.0,    // Medium repos - neutral
            501..=2000 =&gt; 0.95, // Large repos - slight penalty
            _ =&gt; 0.9,           // Very large repos - prefer simpler files
        };

        let language_factor = if self
            .repo_characteristics
            .primary_languages
            .contains(&amp;&quot;rust&quot;.to_string())
        {
            1.05 // Rust projects tend to have good practices
        } else if self
            .repo_characteristics
            .primary_languages
            .contains(&amp;&quot;javascript&quot;.to_string())
        {
            0.95 // JS can be more complex to analyze
        } else {
            1.0
        };

        let maturity_factor = match self.repo_characteristics.age_months {
            0..=6 =&gt; 0.9,   // New projects - focus on functionality
            7..=24 =&gt; 1.0,  // Maturing projects - balanced
            25..=60 =&gt; 1.1, // Mature projects - prioritize maintainability
            _ =&gt; 1.2,       // Very mature projects - heavily prioritize quality
        };

        let experience_factor = match self.repo_characteristics.team_size {
            1 =&gt; 1.1,       // Solo projects - prefer simpler code
            2..=5 =&gt; 1.0,   // Small teams - balanced
            6..=15 =&gt; 0.95, // Medium teams - can handle complexity
            _ =&gt; 0.9,       // Large teams - prefer well-structured code
        };

        AdaptiveFactors {
            repo_size_factor,
            language_factor,
            maturity_factor,
            experience_factor,
        }
    }

    /// Clear the complexity metrics cache
    pub fn clear_cache(&amp;mut self) {
        self.content_cache.clear();
    }

    /// Get cache statistics
    pub fn cache_stats(&amp;self) -&gt; (usize, usize) {
        (self.content_cache.len(), self.content_cache.capacity())
    }
}

impl EnhancedScoreComponents {
    /// Get a breakdown of score contributions
    pub fn score_breakdown(&amp;self) -&gt; HashMap&lt;String, f64&gt; {
        let mut breakdown = self.base_score.as_map();

        breakdown.insert(&quot;complexity_score&quot;.to_string(), self.complexity_score);
        breakdown.insert(
            &quot;maintainability_score&quot;.to_string(),
            self.maintainability_score,
        );
        breakdown.insert(&quot;cognitive_score&quot;.to_string(), self.cognitive_score);
        breakdown.insert(&quot;quality_score&quot;.to_string(), self.quality_score);
        breakdown.insert(
            &quot;enhanced_final_score&quot;.to_string(),
            self.enhanced_final_score,
        );

        breakdown
    }

    /// Get the dominant scoring factor
    pub fn dominant_factor(&amp;self) -&gt; (&amp;&#x27;static str, f64) {
        let factors = [
            (&quot;base_heuristics&quot;, self.base_score.final_score * 0.6),
            (
                &quot;complexity&quot;,
                self.complexity_score * self.adjusted_weights.complexity_weight * 0.4,
            ),
            (
                &quot;maintainability&quot;,
                self.maintainability_score * self.adjusted_weights.maintainability_weight * 0.4,
            ),
            (
                &quot;cognitive&quot;,
                self.cognitive_score * self.adjusted_weights.cognitive_weight * 0.4,
            ),
            (
                &quot;quality&quot;,
                self.quality_score * self.adjusted_weights.quality_weight * 0.4,
            ),
        ];

        factors
            .iter()
            .max_by(|a, b| a.1.partial_cmp(&amp;b.1).unwrap_or(std::cmp::Ordering::Equal))
            .map(|(name, score)| (*name, *score))
            .unwrap_or((&quot;none&quot;, 0.0))
    }

    /// Get a human-readable explanation of the score
    pub fn explanation(&amp;self) -&gt; String {
        let (dominant, _) = self.dominant_factor();
        let complexity_summary = if let Some(metrics) = &amp;self.complexity_metrics {
            metrics.summary()
        } else {
            &quot;No complexity metrics&quot;.to_string()
        };

        format!(
            &quot;Score: {:.3} (dominated by {}), Base: {:.3}, Quality: {:.3}, {}&quot;,
            self.enhanced_final_score,
            dominant,
            self.base_score.final_score,
            self.quality_score,
            complexity_summary
        )
    }
}

fn complex() {

        if i % 2 == 0 {
            while condition() {
                match value {
                    1 =&gt; { if nested() { deep(); } },
                    2 =&gt; { if more_nested() { deeper(); } },
                    _ =&gt; { if even_more() { deepest(); } },
                }
            }
        }
    }
}
&quot;#;

        let files = vec![file1.clone(), file2.clone()];

        let simple_score = scorer

        let mut new_chars = RepositoryCharacteristics::default();
        new_chars.total_files = 5000; // Much larger

        new_chars.age_months = 48; // Mature project

        scorer.update_repository_characteristics(new_chars);

        let new_factors = &amp;scorer.weights.adaptive_factors;

        assert_ne!(

//! Final score calculation and combination logic

use super::normalization::NormalizedScores;
use super::types::{HeuristicWeights, ScoreComponents};

/// Calculate the final weighted score from normalized components
pub fn calculate_final_score(
    normalized_scores: &amp;NormalizedScores,
    weights: &amp;HeuristicWeights,
    template_boost: f64,
    priority_boost: f64,
) -&gt; f64 {
    let weighted_sum = weights.doc_weight * normalized_scores.doc_score
        + weights.readme_weight * normalized_scores.readme_score
        + weights.import_weight * normalized_scores.import_score
        + weights.path_weight * normalized_scores.path_score
        + weights.test_link_weight * normalized_scores.test_link_score
        + weights.churn_weight * normalized_scores.churn_score
        + weights.centrality_weight * normalized_scores.centrality_score
        + weights.entrypoint_weight * normalized_scores.entrypoint_score
        + weights.examples_weight * normalized_scores.examples_score;

    weighted_sum + template_boost + priority_boost
}

impl ScoreComponents {
    /// Get the top contributing factors to this score
    pub fn top_factors(&amp;self, count: usize) -&gt; Vec&lt;(String, f64)&gt; {
        let mut factors = vec![
            (
                &quot;doc_score&quot;.to_string(),
                self.doc_score * self.weights.doc_weight,
            ),
            (
                &quot;readme_score&quot;.to_string(),
                self.readme_score * self.weights.readme_weight,
            ),
            (
                &quot;import_score&quot;.to_string(),
                self.import_score * self.weights.import_weight,
            ),
            (
                &quot;path_score&quot;.to_string(),
                self.path_score * self.weights.path_weight,
            ),
            (
                &quot;test_link_score&quot;.to_string(),
                self.test_link_score * self.weights.test_link_weight,
            ),
            (
                &quot;churn_score&quot;.to_string(),
                self.churn_score * self.weights.churn_weight,
            ),
            (
                &quot;centrality_score&quot;.to_string(),
                self.centrality_score * self.weights.centrality_weight,
            ),
            (
                &quot;entrypoint_score&quot;.to_string(),
                self.entrypoint_score * self.weights.entrypoint_weight,
            ),
            (
                &quot;examples_score&quot;.to_string(),
                self.examples_score * self.weights.examples_weight,
            ),
            (&quot;priority_boost&quot;.to_string(), self.priority_boost),
            (&quot;template_boost&quot;.to_string(), self.template_boost),
        ];

        factors.sort_by(|a, b| b.1.partial_cmp(&amp;a.1).unwrap_or(std::cmp::Ordering::Equal));
        factors.truncate(count);
        factors
    }

    /// Check if this score represents a high-confidence result
    pub fn is_high_confidence(&amp;self) -&gt; bool {
        let contributing_factors = self
            .top_factors(11)
            .iter()
            .filter(|(_, score)| *score &gt; 0.1)
            .count();

        // High confidence if multiple factors contribute significantly
        contributing_factors &gt;= 3 &amp;&amp; self.final_score &gt; 1.0
    }

    /// Get a human-readable explanation of the score
    pub fn explanation(&amp;self) -&gt; String {
        let top_factors = self.top_factors(3);
        let mut explanation = format!(&quot;Score: {:.2}&quot;, self.final_score);

        if !top_factors.is_empty() {
            explanation.push_str(&quot; (top factors: &quot;);
            let factor_strings: Vec&lt;String&gt; = top_factors
                .iter()
                .map(|(name, score)| format!(&quot;{}: {:.2}&quot;, name.replace(&quot;_score&quot;, &quot;&quot;), score))
                .collect();
            explanation.push_str(&amp;factor_strings.join(&quot;, &quot;));
            explanation.push(&#x27;)&#x27;);
        }

        explanation
    }

    /// Determine the primary reason for this file&#x27;s importance
    pub fn primary_importance_reason(&amp;self) -&gt; String {
        let top_factor = self.top_factors(1);
        if let Some((factor_name, score)) = top_factor.first() {
            match factor_name.as_str() {
                &quot;doc_score&quot; =&gt; format!(&quot;Documentation file (score: {:.2})&quot;, score),
                &quot;readme_score&quot; =&gt; format!(&quot;README file (score: {:.2})&quot;, score),
                &quot;import_score&quot; =&gt; format!(&quot;High import connectivity (score: {:.2})&quot;, score),
                &quot;entrypoint_score&quot; =&gt; format!(&quot;Application entrypoint (score: {:.2})&quot;, score),
                &quot;centrality_score&quot; =&gt; format!(&quot;Central to codebase (PageRank: {:.2})&quot;, score),
                &quot;examples_score&quot; =&gt; format!(&quot;Contains examples (score: {:.2})&quot;, score),
                &quot;churn_score&quot; =&gt; format!(&quot;Recently modified (score: {:.2})&quot;, score),
                &quot;test_link_score&quot; =&gt; format!(&quot;Test-related file (score: {:.2})&quot;, score),
                &quot;priority_boost&quot; =&gt; format!(&quot;Manually prioritized (boost: {:.2})&quot;, score),
                &quot;template_boost&quot; =&gt; format!(&quot;Template/config file (boost: {:.2})&quot;, score),
                _ =&gt; format!(&quot;Mixed factors (top: {:.2})&quot;, score),
            }
        } else {
            &quot;No significant factors&quot;.to_string()
        }
    }

    /// Calculate a confidence interval for the score
    pub fn confidence_interval(&amp;self) -&gt; (f64, f64) {
        // Simple confidence estimation based on number of contributing factors
        let top_factors = self.top_factors(11);
        let significant_factors = top_factors.iter().filter(|(_, score)| *score &gt; 0.1).count();

        let confidence_width = match significant_factors {
            0..=1 =&gt; 0.5, // Low confidence - wide interval
            2..=3 =&gt; 0.3, // Medium confidence
            4..=5 =&gt; 0.2, // High confidence
            _ =&gt; 0.1,     // Very high confidence - narrow interval
        };

        let lower = (self.final_score - confidence_width).max(0.0);
        let upper = self.final_score + confidence_width;

        (lower, upper)
    }
}

mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::heuristics::scoring::types::{RawScoreComponents, ScoringFeatures};

    #[test]
    fn test_final_score_calculation() {
        let normalized = NormalizedScores {
            doc_score: 1.0,
            readme_score: 0.5,
            import_score: 0.3,
            path_score: 0.7,
            test_link_score: 0.0,
            churn_score: 0.2,
            centrality_score: 0.8,
            entrypoint_score: 1.0,
            examples_score: 0.4,
        };

        let weights = HeuristicWeights::default();

        let final_score = calculate_final_score(&amp;normalized, &amp;weights, 0.5, 0.2);

        // Should be a positive weighted sum
        assert!(final_score &gt; 0.0);

        // Should include boosts
        let base_score = calculate_final_score(&amp;normalized, &amp;weights, 0.0, 0.0);
        assert!(final_score &gt; base_score);
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_score_explanation() {
        let score_components = ScoreComponents {
            final_score: 5.2,
            doc_score: 1.0,
            readme_score: 0.8,
            import_score: 0.5,
            path_score: 0.3,
            test_link_score: 0.0,
            churn_score: 0.1,
            centrality_score: 0.9,
            entrypoint_score: 1.0,
            examples_score: 0.4,
            priority_boost: 0.5,
            template_boost: 0.2,
            raw_scores: RawScoreComponents {
                doc_raw: 1.0,
                readme_raw: 0.8,
                import_degree_in: 5,
                import_degree_out: 3,
                path_depth: 2,
                test_links_found: 0,
                churn_commits: 2,
                centrality_raw: 0.9,
                is_entrypoint: true,
                examples_count: 3,
            },
            weights: HeuristicWeights::default(),
        };

        let explanation = score_components.explanation();
        assert!(explanation.contains(&quot;Score: 5.20&quot;));
        assert!(explanation.contains(&quot;top factors&quot;));

        let reason = score_components.primary_importance_reason();
        assert!(!reason.is_empty());

        let (lower, upper) = score_components.confidence_interval();
        assert!(lower &lt;= score_components.final_score);
        assert!(upper &gt;= score_components.final_score);
    }
}
