//! # Core Scoring Algorithms for Heuristic File Prioritization
//!
//! Implements the multi-dimensional scoring system from the Python FastPath heuristics:
//!
//! ## Scoring Formula
//! ```text
//! final_score = Σ(weight_i × normalized_score_i) + priority_boost + template_boost
//! ```
//!
//! Where component scores include:
//! - Documentation importance (doc_score)
//! - README prioritization (readme_score)
//! - Import graph centrality (import_score)
//! - Path depth penalty (path_score)
//! - Test-code relationships (test_link_score)
//! - Git churn recency (churn_score)
//! - PageRank centrality (centrality_score, V2)
//! - Entrypoint detection (entrypoint_score)
//! - Examples detection (examples_score)

use super::{import_analysis::ImportGraph, ScanResult};
use scribe_core::Result;
use std::collections::HashMap;

// Public modules
pub mod final_scoring;
pub mod normalization;
pub mod raw_scores;
pub mod types;

// Re-export main types
pub use normalization::{NormalizationStats, NormalizedScores};
pub use types::{HeuristicWeights, RawScoreComponents, ScoreComponents, ScoringFeatures};

/// Main heuristic scorer that coordinates all scoring components
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct HeuristicScorer {
    weights: HeuristicWeights,
    import_graph: Option&lt;ImportGraph&gt;,
    norm_stats: Option&lt;NormalizationStats&gt;,
}

impl HeuristicScorer {
    /// Create a new scorer with given weights
    pub fn new(weights: HeuristicWeights) -&gt; Self {
        Self {
            weights,
            import_graph: None,
            norm_stats: None,
        }
    }

    /// Create a scorer with default weights
    pub fn default() -&gt; Self {
        Self::new(HeuristicWeights::default())
    }

    /// Set the import graph for centrality calculations
    pub fn set_import_graph(&amp;mut self, graph: ImportGraph) {
        self.import_graph = Some(graph);
    }

    /// Score a single file within the context of all files
    pub fn score_file&lt;T&gt;(&amp;mut self, file: &amp;T, all_files: &amp;[T]) -&gt; Result&lt;ScoreComponents&gt;
    where
        T: ScanResult,
    {
        // Build normalization statistics if not cached
        if self.norm_stats.is_none() {
            self.norm_stats = Some(normalization::build_normalization_stats(all_files));
        }

        let norm_stats = self.norm_stats.as_ref().unwrap();
        let raw_scores =
            raw_scores::calculate_raw_scores(file, &amp;self.weights, self.import_graph.as_ref());
        let normalized_scores = normalization::normalize_scores(&amp;raw_scores, norm_stats);

        // Calculate template boost
        let template_boost = if self.weights.features.enable_template_boost {
            super::template_detection::get_template_score_boost(file.path()).unwrap_or(0.0)
        } else {
            0.0
        };

        // Apply weighted formula
        let final_score = final_scoring::calculate_final_score(
            &amp;normalized_scores,
            &amp;self.weights,
            template_boost,
            file.priority_boost(),
        );

        Ok(ScoreComponents {
            final_score,
            doc_score: normalized_scores.doc_score,
            readme_score: normalized_scores.readme_score,
            import_score: normalized_scores.import_score,
            path_score: normalized_scores.path_score,
            test_link_score: normalized_scores.test_link_score,
            churn_score: normalized_scores.churn_score,
            centrality_score: normalized_scores.centrality_score,
            entrypoint_score: normalized_scores.entrypoint_score,
            examples_score: normalized_scores.examples_score,
            priority_boost: file.priority_boost(),
            template_boost,
            raw_scores,
            weights: self.weights.clone(),
        })
    }

    /// Score all files and return ranked results
    pub fn score_all_files&lt;T&gt;(&amp;mut self, files: &amp;[T]) -&gt; Result&lt;Vec&lt;(usize, ScoreComponents)&gt;&gt;
    where
        T: ScanResult,
    {
        let mut scored_files = Vec::new();

        for (idx, file) in files.iter().enumerate() {
            let score = self.score_file(file, files)?;
            scored_files.push((idx, score));
        }

        // Sort by final score (descending)
        scored_files.sort_by(|a, b| {
            b.1.final_score
                .partial_cmp(&amp;a.1.final_score)
                .unwrap_or(std::cmp::Ordering::Equal)
        });

        Ok(scored_files)
    }

    /// Score files with custom weights for specific use cases
    pub fn score_with_preset&lt;T&gt;(
        &amp;mut self,
        files: &amp;[T],
        preset: WeightPreset,
    ) -&gt; Result&lt;Vec&lt;(usize, ScoreComponents)&gt;&gt;
    where
        T: ScanResult,
    {
        // Temporarily change weights
        let original_weights = self.weights.clone();
        self.weights = match preset {
            WeightPreset::Documentation =&gt; HeuristicWeights::for_documentation(),
            WeightPreset::CoreCode =&gt; HeuristicWeights::for_core_code(),
            WeightPreset::Tests =&gt; HeuristicWeights::for_tests(),
            WeightPreset::Balanced =&gt; HeuristicWeights::balanced(),
        };

        // Clear cached normalization stats since weights changed
        self.norm_stats = None;

        let result = self.score_all_files(files);

        // Restore original weights
        self.weights = original_weights;
        self.norm_stats = None;

        result
    }

    /// Get current weights
    pub fn weights(&amp;self) -&gt; &amp;HeuristicWeights {
        &amp;self.weights
    }

    /// Update weights
    pub fn set_weights(&amp;mut self, weights: HeuristicWeights) {
        self.weights = weights;
        self.norm_stats = None; // Clear cache
    }
}

/// Preset weight configurations for common use cases
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
pub enum WeightPreset {
    Documentation,
    CoreCode,
    Tests,
    Balanced,
}

impl Default for HeuristicScorer {
    fn default() -&gt; Self {
        Self::new(HeuristicWeights::default())
    }
}

//! # Import Graph Analysis and Centrality Calculation
//!
//! Implements dependency graph construction and PageRank centrality calculation
//! for the heuristic scoring system. This module provides:
//!
//! - AST-based import statement parsing and normalization
//! - Dependency graph construction with intelligent matching
//! - PageRank centrality computation
//! - Import-to-file path matching heuristics
//!
//! The centrality scores help identify important files that are heavily depended upon.
//! Uses tree-sitter AST parsing instead of regex patterns for accurate import extraction.

use super::ScanResult;
use crate::ast_import_parser::{ImportLanguage, SimpleAstParser, SimpleImport};
use scribe_core::Result;
use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::path::Path;

/// Dependency graph for centrality calculation
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct ImportGraph {
    /// Node index to file path mapping
    nodes: Vec&lt;String&gt;,
    /// File path to node index mapping
    path_to_index: HashMap&lt;String, usize&gt;,
    /// Adjacency list: node -&gt; list of nodes it depends on
    dependencies: Vec&lt;Vec&lt;usize&gt;&gt;,
    /// Reverse adjacency list: node -&gt; list of nodes that depend on it
    dependents: Vec&lt;Vec&lt;usize&gt;&gt;,
    /// Cached PageRank scores
    pagerank_scores: Option&lt;Vec&lt;f64&gt;&gt;,
}

/// Fast import resolution keymap (O(1) lookups instead of O(F) scans)
#[derive(Debug)]
struct ImportKeyMap {
    /// Exact path matches: normalized_path -&gt; file_index
    exact: HashMap&lt;String, usize&gt;,
    /// Suffix matches: stem/base -&gt; file_index  
    suffix: HashMap&lt;String, usize&gt;,
}

impl ImportKeyMap {
    fn new&lt;T&gt;(files: &amp;[T]) -&gt; Self
    where
        T: ScanResult,
    {
        let mut exact = HashMap::with_capacity(files.len());
        let mut suffix = HashMap::with_capacity(files.len() * 2);

        for (i, file) in files.iter().enumerate() {
            let path = file.path();

            // Add exact normalized keys
            for key in Self::normalized_keys(path) {
                exact.insert(key, i);
            }

            // Add suffix keys
            for key in Self::suffix_keys(path) {
                suffix.insert(key, i);
            }
        }

        Self { exact, suffix }
    }

    fn resolve_import(&amp;self, normalized_import: &amp;str) -&gt; Option&lt;usize&gt; {
        // Try exact match first
        if let Some(&amp;idx) = self.exact.get(normalized_import) {
            return Some(idx);
        }

        // Try suffix match
        self.suffix.get(normalized_import).copied()
    }

    fn normalized_keys(path: &amp;str) -&gt; Vec&lt;String&gt; {
        let mut keys = Vec::new();

        // Add the path as-is
        keys.push(path.to_string());

        // Add without leading ./
        if path.starts_with(&quot;./&quot;) {
            keys.push(path[2..].to_string());
        }

        // Add path with common extensions removed
        if let Some(stem) = Path::new(path).file_stem().and_then(|s| s.to_str()) {
            if let Some(parent) = Path::new(path).parent().and_then(|p| p.to_str()) {
                if parent != &quot;&quot; {
                    keys.push(format!(&quot;{}/{}&quot;, parent, stem));
                } else {
                    keys.push(stem.to_string());
                }
            }
        }

        keys
    }

    fn suffix_keys(path: &amp;str) -&gt; Vec&lt;String&gt; {
        let mut keys = Vec::new();

        // Add filename without extension
        if let Some(stem) = Path::new(path).file_stem().and_then(|s| s.to_str()) {
            keys.push(stem.to_string());
        }

        // Add directory/filename patterns
        if let Some(filename) = Path::new(path).file_name().and_then(|s| s.to_str()) {
            keys.push(filename.to_string());
        }

        keys
    }
}

/// Builder for constructing import graphs from scan results
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct ImportGraphBuilder {
    /// Import path normalization cache
    normalization_cache: HashMap&lt;String, String&gt;,
    /// AST parser for extracting imports
    ast_parser: SimpleAstParser,
}

/// Centrality calculator implementing PageRank algorithm
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct CentralityCalculator {
    /// PageRank damping factor (typically 0.85)
    damping_factor: f64,
    /// Maximum iterations for convergence
    max_iterations: usize,
    /// Convergence tolerance
    tolerance: f64,
}

impl Default for ImportGraphBuilder {
    fn default() -&gt; Self {
        Self::new().expect(&quot;Failed to create ImportGraphBuilder&quot;)
    }
}

impl ImportGraphBuilder {
    /// Create a new import graph builder
    pub fn new() -&gt; Result&lt;Self&gt; {
        Ok(Self {
            normalization_cache: HashMap::new(),
            ast_parser: SimpleAstParser::new()?,
        })
    }

    /// Build import graph from scan results (OPTIMIZED: O(1) lookups instead of O(F×I))
    pub fn build_graph&lt;T&gt;(&amp;mut self, files: &amp;[T]) -&gt; Result&lt;ImportGraph&gt;
    where
        T: ScanResult,
    {
        let mut graph = ImportGraph::new();

        // Add all files as nodes
        for file in files {
            graph.add_node(file.path().to_string());
        }

        // Build keymap for O(1) import resolution (MAJOR PERFORMANCE FIX!)
        let keymap = ImportKeyMap::new(files);

        // Build edges based on import relationships
        for (file_idx, file) in files.iter().enumerate() {
            if let Some(imports) = file.imports() {
                for import_path in imports {
                    let normalized_import = self.normalize_import_path(import_path);
                    if let Some(target_idx) = keymap.resolve_import(&amp;normalized_import) {
                        graph.add_edge(file_idx, target_idx);
                    }
                }
            }
        }

        Ok(graph)
    }

    // Note: find_matching_file method removed - replaced with O(1) ImportKeyMap lookup

    /// Normalize import path for matching
    fn normalize_import_path(&amp;mut self, import_path: &amp;str) -&gt; String {
        // Check cache first
        if let Some(cached) = self.normalization_cache.get(import_path) {
            return cached.clone();
        }

        let normalized = self.perform_normalization(import_path);
        self.normalization_cache
            .insert(import_path.to_string(), normalized.clone());
        normalized
    }

    /// Perform actual import path normalization
    fn perform_normalization(&amp;self, import_path: &amp;str) -&gt; String {
        let mut normalized = import_path.to_string();

        // Remove quotes and whitespace
        normalized = normalized
            .trim_matches(|c| c == &#x27;&quot;&#x27; || c == &#x27;\&#x27;&#x27; || c == &#x27; &#x27;)
            .to_string();

        // Normalize path separators
        normalized = normalized.replace(&#x27;\\&#x27;, &quot;/&quot;);

        // Remove file extensions for language-agnostic matching
        if let Some(dot_pos) = normalized.rfind(&#x27;.&#x27;) {
            // Keep extension only for specific cases
            let extension = &amp;normalized[dot_pos..];
            match extension {
                &quot;.json&quot; | &quot;.xml&quot; | &quot;.yaml&quot; | &quot;.toml&quot; | &quot;.css&quot; | &quot;.scss&quot; =&gt; {
                    // Keep these extensions as they&#x27;re often imported directly
                }
                _ =&gt; {
                    // Remove programming language extensions
                    normalized.truncate(dot_pos);
                }
            }
        }

        // Handle relative imports
        if normalized.starts_with(&quot;./&quot;) || normalized.starts_with(&quot;../&quot;) {
            // Keep relative structure but normalize
            normalized = self.normalize_relative_path(&amp;normalized);
        }

        // Convert module-style imports to file paths
        normalized = normalized.replace(&quot;::&quot;, &quot;/&quot;).replace(&#x27;.&#x27;, &quot;/&quot;);

        // Handle common import aliases
        normalized = self.resolve_import_aliases(&amp;normalized);

        normalized
    }

    /// Normalize relative path imports
    fn normalize_relative_path(&amp;self, path: &amp;str) -&gt; String {
        // Simple path normalization - in practice, this would be more sophisticated
        let components: Vec&lt;&amp;str&gt; = path.split(&#x27;/&#x27;).collect();
        let mut normalized = Vec::new();

        for component in components {
            match component {
                &quot;&quot; | &quot;.&quot; =&gt; continue,
                &quot;..&quot; =&gt; {
                    normalized.pop();
                }
                _ =&gt; normalized.push(component),
            }
        }

        normalized.join(&quot;/&quot;)
    }

    /// Resolve common import aliases and patterns
    fn resolve_import_aliases(&amp;self, import_path: &amp;str) -&gt; String {
        // Handle common aliases
        match import_path {
            // Node.js built-ins
            &quot;fs&quot; | &quot;path&quot; | &quot;http&quot; | &quot;https&quot; | &quot;url&quot; | &quot;crypto&quot; | &quot;os&quot; =&gt; {
                return import_path.to_string(); // Keep as-is for built-ins
            }
            // Package imports (usually not files in the repo)
            path if !path.contains(&#x27;/&#x27;) &amp;&amp; !path.starts_with(&#x27;.&#x27;) =&gt; {
                return import_path.to_string(); // Likely external package
            }
            _ =&gt; {}
        }

        let mut resolved = import_path.to_string();

        // Common alias patterns
        if resolved.starts_with(&quot;@/&quot;) {
            resolved = resolved.replacen(&quot;@/&quot;, &quot;src/&quot;, 1);
        }

        if resolved.starts_with(&quot;~&quot;) {
            resolved = resolved.replacen(&quot;~&quot;, &quot;src&quot;, 1);
        }

        resolved
    }

    /// Detect language from file extension for AST parsing
    fn detect_language_from_path(&amp;self, file_path: &amp;str) -&gt; Option&lt;ImportLanguage&gt; {
        let extension = Path::new(file_path)
            .extension()
            .and_then(|ext| ext.to_str())
            .unwrap_or(&quot;&quot;);

        ImportLanguage::from_extension(extension)
    }

    /// Extract imports from file content using AST parsing
    pub fn extract_imports(&amp;self, content: &amp;str, file_path: &amp;str) -&gt; Vec&lt;String&gt; {
        // Detect language from file path
        let language = match self.detect_language_from_path(file_path) {
            Some(lang) =&gt; lang,
            None =&gt; return Vec::new(),
        };

        // Use AST parser to extract imports
        match self.ast_parser.extract_imports(content, language) {
            Ok(simple_imports) =&gt; simple_imports
                .into_iter()
                .map(|import| import.module)
                .collect(),
            Err(_) =&gt; {
                // Fall back to empty list if parsing fails
                Vec::new()
            }
        }
    }
}

impl ImportGraph {
    /// Create a new empty import graph
    pub fn new() -&gt; Self {
        Self {
            nodes: Vec::new(),
            path_to_index: HashMap::new(),
            dependencies: Vec::new(),
            dependents: Vec::new(),
            pagerank_scores: None,
        }
    }

    /// Add a node to the graph
    pub fn add_node(&amp;mut self, path: String) -&gt; usize {
        if let Some(&amp;existing_idx) = self.path_to_index.get(&amp;path) {
            return existing_idx;
        }

        let index = self.nodes.len();
        self.nodes.push(path.clone());
        self.path_to_index.insert(path, index);
        self.dependencies.push(Vec::new());
        self.dependents.push(Vec::new());

        // Invalidate cached PageRank scores
        self.pagerank_scores = None;

        index
    }

    /// Add an edge from source to target (source depends on target)
    pub fn add_edge(&amp;mut self, source: usize, target: usize) {
        if source &lt; self.dependencies.len() &amp;&amp; target &lt; self.dependents.len() &amp;&amp; source != target {
            // Avoid duplicate edges
            if !self.dependencies[source].contains(&amp;target) {
                self.dependencies[source].push(target);
                self.dependents[target].push(source);

                // Invalidate cached PageRank scores
                self.pagerank_scores = None;
            }
        }
    }

    /// Get node degrees (in-degree, out-degree)
    pub fn get_node_degrees(&amp;self, path: &amp;str) -&gt; Option&lt;(usize, usize)&gt; {
        let index = *self.path_to_index.get(path)?;
        let in_degree = self.dependents[index].len();
        let out_degree = self.dependencies[index].len();
        Some((in_degree, out_degree))
    }

    /// Get PageRank scores for all nodes
    pub fn get_pagerank_scores(&amp;mut self) -&gt; Result&lt;&amp;[f64]&gt; {
        if self.pagerank_scores.is_none() {
            let calculator = CentralityCalculator::default();
            let scores = calculator.calculate_pagerank(self)?;
            self.pagerank_scores = Some(scores);
        }

        Ok(self.pagerank_scores.as_ref().unwrap())
    }

    /// Get PageRank score for a specific file
    pub fn get_pagerank_score(&amp;mut self, path: &amp;str) -&gt; Result&lt;f64&gt; {
        let index = *self.path_to_index.get(path).unwrap_or(&amp;0);
        let scores = self.get_pagerank_scores()?;
        Ok(*scores.get(index).unwrap_or(&amp;0.0))
    }

    /// Get graph statistics
    pub fn stats(&amp;self) -&gt; GraphStats {
        let node_count = self.nodes.len();
        let edge_count: usize = self.dependencies.iter().map(|deps| deps.len()).sum();

        let in_degrees: Vec&lt;usize&gt; = self.dependents.iter().map(|deps| deps.len()).collect();
        let out_degrees: Vec&lt;usize&gt; = self.dependencies.iter().map(|deps| deps.len()).collect();

        let avg_in_degree = if node_count &gt; 0 {
            in_degrees.iter().sum::&lt;usize&gt;() as f64 / node_count as f64
        } else {
            0.0
        };

        let avg_out_degree = if node_count &gt; 0 {
            out_degrees.iter().sum::&lt;usize&gt;() as f64 / node_count as f64
        } else {
            0.0
        };

        let max_in_degree = in_degrees.iter().max().cloned().unwrap_or(0);
        let max_out_degree = out_degrees.iter().max().cloned().unwrap_or(0);

        let density = if node_count &gt; 1 {
            edge_count as f64 / (node_count * (node_count - 1)) as f64
        } else {
            0.0
        };

        GraphStats {
            node_count,
            edge_count,
            avg_in_degree,
            avg_out_degree,
            max_in_degree,
            max_out_degree,
            density,
        }
    }
}

impl Default for ImportGraph {
    fn default() -&gt; Self {
        Self::new()
    }
}

impl CentralityCalculator {
    /// Create a new centrality calculator with default parameters
    pub fn new() -&gt; Self {
        Self {
            damping_factor: 0.85,
            max_iterations: 100,
            tolerance: 1e-6,
        }
    }

    /// Create with custom parameters
    pub fn with_params(damping_factor: f64, max_iterations: usize, tolerance: f64) -&gt; Self {
        Self {
            damping_factor,
            max_iterations,
            tolerance,
        }
    }

    /// Calculate PageRank scores for the graph
    pub fn calculate_pagerank(&amp;self, graph: &amp;ImportGraph) -&gt; Result&lt;Vec&lt;f64&gt;&gt; {
        let n = graph.nodes.len();
        if n == 0 {
            return Ok(Vec::new());
        }

        // Initialize scores uniformly
        let mut scores = vec![1.0 / n as f64; n];
        let mut new_scores = vec![0.0; n];

        for _iteration in 0..self.max_iterations {
            // Calculate new scores
            for (i, new_score) in new_scores.iter_mut().enumerate() {
                let mut rank_sum = 0.0;

                // Sum contributions from nodes pointing to this one
                for &amp;source in &amp;graph.dependents[i] {
                    let out_degree = graph.dependencies[source].len();
                    if out_degree &gt; 0 {
                        rank_sum += scores[source] / out_degree as f64;
                    }
                }

                // Apply PageRank formula
                *new_score =
                    (1.0 - self.damping_factor) / n as f64 + self.damping_factor * rank_sum;
            }

            // Check for convergence
            let mut max_diff = 0.0;
            for i in 0..n {
                let diff = (new_scores[i] - scores[i]).abs();
                if diff &gt; max_diff {
                    max_diff = diff;
                }
            }

            // Swap score vectors
            std::mem::swap(&amp;mut scores, &amp;mut new_scores);

            if max_diff &lt; self.tolerance {
                break;
            }
        }

        Ok(scores)
    }
}

impl Default for CentralityCalculator {
    fn default() -&gt; Self {
        Self::new()
    }
}

/// Graph statistics for analysis
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct GraphStats {
    pub node_count: usize,
    pub edge_count: usize,
    pub avg_in_degree: f64,
    pub avg_out_degree: f64,
    pub max_in_degree: usize,
    pub max_out_degree: usize,
    pub density: f64,
}

/// Check if an import statement matches a file path
pub fn import_matches_file(import_path: &amp;str, file_path: &amp;str) -&gt; bool {
    // Normalize both paths for comparison
    let normalized_import = normalize_for_matching(import_path);
    let normalized_file = normalize_for_matching(file_path);

    // Direct match
    if normalized_import == normalized_file {
        return true;
    }

    // Check if import is a substring of file path (for module imports)
    if normalized_file.contains(&amp;normalized_import) {
        return true;
    }

    // Check if file path ends with import (common for relative imports)
    if normalized_file.ends_with(&amp;normalized_import) {
        return true;
    }

    // Check module-style imports (convert :: to /)
    let module_import = normalized_import.replace(&quot;::&quot;, &quot;/&quot;);
    if normalized_file.contains(&amp;module_import) || module_import.contains(&amp;normalized_file) {
        return true;
    }

    // Special handling for std library and common patterns
    if normalized_import.starts_with(&quot;std::&quot;) {
        let std_path = normalized_import.replace(&quot;::&quot;, &quot;/&quot;);
        if normalized_file
            .replace(&quot;_&quot;, &quot;&quot;)
            .contains(&amp;std_path.replace(&quot;_&quot;, &quot;&quot;))
        {
            return true;
        }
    }

    // Handle index files
    if is_index_file(file_path) {
        let directory = std::path::Path::new(file_path)
            .parent()
            .and_then(|p| p.to_str())
            .unwrap_or(&quot;&quot;);
        let normalized_dir = normalize_for_matching(directory);
        if normalized_import == normalized_dir {
            return true;
        }
    }

    false
}

/// Normalize paths for matching comparison
fn normalize_for_matching(path: &amp;str) -&gt; String {
    let mut normalized = path.to_lowercase();

    // Remove common prefixes
    if normalized.starts_with(&quot;./&quot;) {
        normalized = normalized[2..].to_string();
    }

    if normalized.starts_with(&quot;src/&quot;) {
        normalized = normalized[4..].to_string();
    }

    // Remove file extensions
    if let Some(dot_pos) = normalized.rfind(&#x27;.&#x27;) {
        normalized.truncate(dot_pos);
    }

    // Normalize separators
    normalized = normalized.replace(&#x27;\\&#x27;, &quot;/&quot;);

    // Remove trailing slashes
    normalized.trim_end_matches(&#x27;/&#x27;).to_string()
}

/// Check if a file is an index file (index.js, __init__.py, mod.rs, etc.)
fn is_index_file(file_path: &amp;str) -&gt; bool {
    let file_name = std::path::Path::new(file_path)
        .file_stem()
        .and_then(|stem| stem.to_str())
        .unwrap_or(&quot;&quot;);

    matches!(file_name, &quot;index&quot; | &quot;__init__&quot; | &quot;mod&quot; | &quot;main&quot;)
}

        let idx_c = graph.add_node(&quot;C&quot;.to_string());

        graph.add_edge(idx_a, idx_b);
        graph.add_edge(idx_b, idx_c);
        graph.add_edge(idx_a, idx_c);

        let scores = graph.get_pagerank_scores();
        assert!(scores.is_ok());

        assert_eq!(scores.len(), 3);

//! # Heuristic Scoring System for File Prioritization
//!
//! Implements a sophisticated multi-dimensional scoring system for ranking file importance
//! within a codebase. This module ports and enhances the Python FastPath heuristic system
//! with advanced features:
//!
//! ## Core Scoring Formula
//! ```text
//! score = w_doc*doc + w_readme*readme + w_imp*imp_deg + w_path*path_depth^-1 +
//!         w_test*test_link + w_churn*churn + w_centrality*centrality +
//!         w_entrypoint*entrypoint + w_examples*examples + priority_boost
//! ```
//!
//! ## Key Features
//! - **Template Detection**: Advanced template engine detection using multiple methods
//! - **Import Graph Analysis**: Dependency centrality and PageRank calculations
//! - **Documentation Intelligence**: README prioritization and document structure analysis
//! - **Test-Code Relationships**: Heuristic test file linkage detection
//! - **Git Churn Integration**: Change recency and frequency signals
//! - **Configurable Weighting**: V1/V2 feature flags with dynamic weight adjustment
//! - **Performance Optimized**: Caching and lazy evaluation for large codebases

pub mod enhanced_scoring;
pub mod import_analysis;
pub mod scoring;
pub mod template_detection;

pub use scoring::{
    HeuristicScorer, HeuristicWeights, RawScoreComponents, ScoreComponents, ScoringFeatures,
    WeightPreset,
};

pub use template_detection::{
    get_template_score_boost, is_template_file, TemplateDetectionMethod, TemplateDetector,
    TemplateEngine,
};

pub use import_analysis::{
    import_matches_file, CentralityCalculator, ImportGraph, ImportGraphBuilder,
};

pub use enhanced_scoring::{
    AdaptiveFactors, EnhancedHeuristicScorer, EnhancedScoreComponents, EnhancedWeights,
    ProjectType, RepositoryCharacteristics,
};

use scribe_core::Result;
use std::collections::HashMap;

/// Main entry point for the heuristic scoring system
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct HeuristicSystem {
    /// Core file scorer
    scorer: HeuristicScorer,
    /// Template detection engine
    template_detector: TemplateDetector,
    /// Import graph builder
    import_builder: ImportGraphBuilder,
}

impl HeuristicSystem {
    /// Create a new heuristic system with default configuration
    pub fn new() -&gt; Result&lt;Self&gt; {
        Ok(Self {
            scorer: HeuristicScorer::new(HeuristicWeights::default()),
            template_detector: TemplateDetector::new()?,
            import_builder: ImportGraphBuilder::new()?,
        })
    }

    /// Create with custom weights
    pub fn with_weights(weights: HeuristicWeights) -&gt; Result&lt;Self&gt; {
        Ok(Self {
            scorer: HeuristicScorer::new(weights),
            template_detector: TemplateDetector::new()?,
            import_builder: ImportGraphBuilder::new()?,
        })
    }

    /// Create with V2 features enabled
    pub fn with_v2_features() -&gt; Result&lt;Self&gt; {
        Ok(Self {
            scorer: HeuristicScorer::new(HeuristicWeights::with_v2_features()),
            template_detector: TemplateDetector::new()?,
            import_builder: ImportGraphBuilder::new()?,
        })
    }

    /// Score a single file within the context of all scanned files
    pub fn score_file&lt;T&gt;(&amp;mut self, file: &amp;T, all_files: &amp;[T]) -&gt; Result&lt;ScoreComponents&gt;
    where
        T: ScanResult,
    {
        self.scorer.score_file(file, all_files)
    }

    /// Score all files and return ranked results
    pub fn score_all_files&lt;T&gt;(&amp;mut self, files: &amp;[T]) -&gt; Result&lt;Vec&lt;(usize, ScoreComponents)&gt;&gt;
    where
        T: ScanResult,
    {
        self.scorer.score_all_files(files)
    }

    /// Get top-K files by heuristic score
    pub fn get_top_files&lt;T&gt;(
        &amp;mut self,
        files: &amp;[T],
        top_k: usize,
    ) -&gt; Result&lt;Vec&lt;(usize, ScoreComponents)&gt;&gt;
    where
        T: ScanResult,
    {
        Ok(self
            .score_all_files(files)?
            .into_iter()
            .take(top_k)
            .collect())
    }

    /// Get template score boost for a file path
    pub fn get_template_boost(&amp;self, file_path: &amp;str) -&gt; Result&lt;f64&gt; {
        self.template_detector.get_score_boost(file_path)
    }

    /// Check if two imports match (for import graph construction)
    pub fn import_matches(&amp;self, import_name: &amp;str, file_path: &amp;str) -&gt; bool {
        import_analysis::import_matches_file(import_name, file_path)
    }
}

impl Default for HeuristicSystem {
    fn default() -&gt; Self {
        Self::new().expect(&quot;Failed to create HeuristicSystem&quot;)
    }
}

/// Trait that scan results must implement for heuristic scoring
pub trait ScanResult {
    /// Get the file path
    fn path(&amp;self) -&gt; &amp;str;

    /// Get the relative path from repository root
    fn relative_path(&amp;self) -&gt; &amp;str;

    /// Get file depth (directory nesting level)
    fn depth(&amp;self) -&gt; usize;

    /// Check if this is a documentation file
    fn is_docs(&amp;self) -&gt; bool;

    /// Check if this is a README file
    fn is_readme(&amp;self) -&gt; bool;

    /// Check if this is a test file
    fn is_test(&amp;self) -&gt; bool;

    /// Check if this is an entrypoint file (main, index, etc.)
    fn is_entrypoint(&amp;self) -&gt; bool;

    /// Check if this file contains examples
    fn has_examples(&amp;self) -&gt; bool;

    /// Get the priority boost value (from scanner)
    fn priority_boost(&amp;self) -&gt; f64;

    /// Get the churn score (git activity)
    fn churn_score(&amp;self) -&gt; f64;

    /// Get centrality in score (PageRank)
    fn centrality_in(&amp;self) -&gt; f64;

    /// Get list of import statements
    fn imports(&amp;self) -&gt; Option&lt;&amp;[String]&gt;;

    /// Get document analysis results (if available)
    fn doc_analysis(&amp;self) -&gt; Option&lt;&amp;DocumentAnalysis&gt;;
}

/// Document analysis results for scoring
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct DocumentAnalysis {
    /// Number of headings in the document
    pub heading_count: usize,
    /// Number of table-of-contents indicators
    pub toc_indicators: usize,
    /// Number of links in the document
    pub link_count: usize,
    /// Number of code blocks
    pub code_block_count: usize,
    /// Whether the document appears well-structured
    pub is_well_structured: bool,
}

impl DocumentAnalysis {
    pub fn new() -&gt; Self {
        Self {
            heading_count: 0,
            toc_indicators: 0,
            link_count: 0,
            code_block_count: 0,
            is_well_structured: false,
        }
    }

    /// Calculate structure score based on analysis
    pub fn structure_score(&amp;self) -&gt; f64 {
        let mut score = 0.0;

        // Heading structure bonus
        if self.heading_count &gt; 0 {
            score += (self.heading_count as f64 / 10.0).min(0.5);
        }

        // TOC indicates well-organized document
        if self.toc_indicators &gt; 0 {
            score += 0.3;
        }

        // Links indicate reference document
        if self.link_count &gt; 0 {
            score += (self.link_count as f64 / 20.0).min(0.3);
        }

        // Code blocks in docs indicate technical documentation
        if self.code_block_count &gt; 0 {
            score += (self.code_block_count as f64 / 10.0).min(0.2);
        }

        score
    }
}

impl Default for DocumentAnalysis {
    fn default() -&gt; Self {
        Self::new()
    }
}

/// Performance metrics for the heuristic system
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct HeuristicMetrics {
    /// Number of files processed
    pub files_processed: usize,
    /// Total processing time in milliseconds
    pub processing_time_ms: u64,
    /// Import graph construction time
    pub import_graph_time_ms: u64,
    /// Template detection time
    pub template_detection_time_ms: u64,
    /// Average time per file
    pub avg_time_per_file_ms: f64,
    /// Cache hit rates
    pub cache_hit_rates: HashMap&lt;String, f64&gt;,
}

impl HeuristicMetrics {
    pub fn new() -&gt; Self {
        Self {
            files_processed: 0,
            processing_time_ms: 0,
            import_graph_time_ms: 0,
            template_detection_time_ms: 0,
            avg_time_per_file_ms: 0.0,
            cache_hit_rates: HashMap::new(),
        }
    }

    pub fn finalize(&amp;mut self) {
        if self.files_processed &gt; 0 {
            self.avg_time_per_file_ms =
                self.processing_time_ms as f64 / self.files_processed as f64;
        }
    }
}

impl Default for HeuristicMetrics {
    fn default() -&gt; Self {
        Self::new()
    }
}

//! Score normalization logic for consistent heuristic scoring

use super::super::ScanResult;
use super::types::{HeuristicWeights, RawScoreComponents};

/// Normalized score components after statistical normalization
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct NormalizedScores {
    pub doc_score: f64,
    pub readme_score: f64,
    pub import_score: f64,
    pub path_score: f64,
    pub test_link_score: f64,
    pub churn_score: f64,
    pub centrality_score: f64,
    pub entrypoint_score: f64,
    pub examples_score: f64,
}

/// Statistics for normalization across all files
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct NormalizationStats {
    pub max_doc_raw: f64,
    pub max_readme_raw: f64,
    pub max_import_degree_in: usize,
    pub max_import_degree_out: usize,
    pub max_path_depth: usize,
    pub max_test_links: usize,
    pub max_churn_commits: usize,
    pub max_centrality_raw: f64,
    pub max_examples_count: usize,
}

/// Build normalization statistics from all files
pub fn build_normalization_stats&lt;T&gt;(files: &amp;[T]) -&gt; NormalizationStats
where
    T: ScanResult,
{
    let mut stats = NormalizationStats {
        max_doc_raw: 0.0,
        max_readme_raw: 0.0,
        max_import_degree_in: 0,
        max_import_degree_out: 0,
        max_path_depth: 0,
        max_test_links: 0,
        max_churn_commits: 0,
        max_centrality_raw: 0.0,
        max_examples_count: 0,
    };

    for file in files {
        // Documentation stats
        if file.is_docs() {
            stats.max_doc_raw = stats.max_doc_raw.max(1.0);
            if let Some(doc_analysis) = file.doc_analysis() {
                stats.max_doc_raw = stats.max_doc_raw.max(doc_analysis.structure_score());
            }
        }

        // README stats
        if file.is_readme() {
            let readme_score = if file.depth() &lt;= 1 { 1.5 } else { 1.0 };
            stats.max_readme_raw = stats.max_readme_raw.max(readme_score);
        }

        // Path depth
        stats.max_path_depth = stats.max_path_depth.max(file.depth());

        // Test links (use is_test as proxy)
        if file.is_test() {
            stats.max_test_links = stats.max_test_links.max(1);
        }

        // Git churn (use churn_score from trait)
        let churn_score = file.churn_score() as usize;
        stats.max_churn_commits = stats.max_churn_commits.max(churn_score);

        // Count examples
        let examples_count = count_examples_in_file(file);
        stats.max_examples_count = stats.max_examples_count.max(examples_count);
    }

    // Ensure minimums to avoid division by zero
    stats.max_doc_raw = stats.max_doc_raw.max(1.0);
    stats.max_readme_raw = stats.max_readme_raw.max(1.0);
    stats.max_import_degree_in = stats.max_import_degree_in.max(1);
    stats.max_import_degree_out = stats.max_import_degree_out.max(1);
    stats.max_path_depth = stats.max_path_depth.max(1);
    stats.max_test_links = stats.max_test_links.max(1);
    stats.max_churn_commits = stats.max_churn_commits.max(1);
    stats.max_centrality_raw = stats.max_centrality_raw.max(0.1);
    stats.max_examples_count = stats.max_examples_count.max(1);

    stats
}

/// Normalize raw scores using statistics
pub fn normalize_scores(
    raw_scores: &amp;RawScoreComponents,
    stats: &amp;NormalizationStats,
) -&gt; NormalizedScores {
    NormalizedScores {
        doc_score: raw_scores.doc_raw / stats.max_doc_raw,
        readme_score: raw_scores.readme_raw / stats.max_readme_raw,
        import_score: calculate_import_score(raw_scores, stats),
        path_score: calculate_path_score(raw_scores, stats),
        test_link_score: raw_scores.test_links_found as f64 / stats.max_test_links as f64,
        churn_score: raw_scores.churn_commits as f64 / stats.max_churn_commits as f64,
        centrality_score: raw_scores.centrality_raw / stats.max_centrality_raw,
        entrypoint_score: if raw_scores.is_entrypoint { 1.0 } else { 0.0 },
        examples_score: raw_scores.examples_count as f64 / stats.max_examples_count as f64,
    }
}

/// Calculate normalized import score combining in and out degree
fn calculate_import_score(raw_scores: &amp;RawScoreComponents, stats: &amp;NormalizationStats) -&gt; f64 {
    let in_score = raw_scores.import_degree_in as f64 / stats.max_import_degree_in as f64;
    let out_score = raw_scores.import_degree_out as f64 / stats.max_import_degree_out as f64;

    // Weight incoming imports higher (more important files are imported more)
    0.7 * in_score + 0.3 * out_score
}

/// Calculate normalized path score (inverted - deeper paths get lower scores)
fn calculate_path_score(raw_scores: &amp;RawScoreComponents, stats: &amp;NormalizationStats) -&gt; f64 {
    // Invert path depth (deeper = lower score)
    1.0 - (raw_scores.path_depth as f64 / stats.max_path_depth as f64)
}

/// Count examples or example-like content in a file
fn count_examples_in_file&lt;T: ScanResult&gt;(file: &amp;T) -&gt; usize {
    // Use the built-in method from ScanResult trait
    if file.has_examples() {
        1
    } else {
        0
    }
}

            max_readme_raw: 1.0,

            max_import_degree_out: 1,
            max_path_depth: 5, // Max depth is 5
            max_test_links: 1,
            max_churn_commits: 1,
            max_centrality_raw: 1.0,
            max_examples_count: 1,
        };

        let path_score = calculate_path_score(&amp;raw_scores, &amp;stats);
        // Path depth 3/5 = 0.6, so inverted score should be 1.0 - 0.6 = 0.4
        assert!((path_score - 0.4).abs() &lt; 0.01);

//! Raw score calculation for heuristic components before normalization

use super::super::{import_analysis::ImportGraph, ScanResult};
use super::types::{HeuristicWeights, RawScoreComponents};

/// Calculate raw score components for a file before normalization
pub fn calculate_raw_scores&lt;T&gt;(
    file: &amp;T,
    weights: &amp;HeuristicWeights,
    import_graph: Option&lt;&amp;ImportGraph&gt;,
) -&gt; RawScoreComponents
where
    T: ScanResult,
{
    // Documentation score
    let doc_raw = if file.is_docs() { 1.0 } else { 0.0 }
        + if let Some(doc_analysis) = file.doc_analysis() {
            doc_analysis.structure_score()
        } else {
            0.0
        };

    // README score
    let readme_raw = if file.is_readme() {
        // Root-level README gets higher score
        if file.depth() &lt;= 1 {
            1.5
        } else {
            1.0
        }
    } else {
        0.0
    };

    // Import degree (estimated from imports list)
    let import_degree_in = file.centrality_in() as usize;
    let import_degree_out = if let Some(imports) = file.imports() {
        imports.len()
    } else {
        0
    };

    // Path depth
    let path_depth = file.depth();

    // Test links (use is_test as proxy)
    let test_links_found = if weights.features.enable_test_linking {
        if file.is_test() {
            1
        } else {
            0
        }
    } else {
        0
    };

    // Churn analysis (use churn_score from trait)
    let churn_commits = if weights.features.enable_churn_analysis {
        file.churn_score() as usize
    } else {
        0
    };

    // Centrality (PageRank from trait)
    let centrality_raw = if weights.features.enable_centrality {
        file.centrality_in()
    } else {
        0.0
    };

    // Entrypoint detection
    let is_entrypoint = is_file_entrypoint(file);

    // Examples detection
    let examples_count = if weights.features.enable_examples_detection {
        count_examples_in_file(file)
    } else {
        0
    };

    RawScoreComponents {
        doc_raw,
        readme_raw,
        import_degree_in,
        import_degree_out,
        path_depth,
        test_links_found,
        churn_commits,
        centrality_raw,
        is_entrypoint,
        examples_count,
    }
}

/// Detect if a file is likely an entrypoint
fn is_file_entrypoint&lt;T: ScanResult&gt;(file: &amp;T) -&gt; bool {
    // Use the built-in method from ScanResult trait
    file.is_entrypoint()
}

/// Check if a file is likely executable based on its content or naming
fn is_likely_executable&lt;T: ScanResult&gt;(file: &amp;T) -&gt; bool {
    let path_str = file.path().to_lowercase();

    // Executable extensions
    let exec_extensions = [&quot;.py&quot;, &quot;.rs&quot;, &quot;.js&quot;, &quot;.ts&quot;, &quot;.sh&quot;, &quot;.bash&quot;, &quot;.zsh&quot;];
    if exec_extensions.iter().any(|ext| path_str.ends_with(ext)) {
        return true;
    }

    false
}

/// Count examples or example-like content in a file
fn count_examples_in_file&lt;T: ScanResult&gt;(file: &amp;T) -&gt; usize {
    // Use the built-in method from ScanResult trait
    if file.has_examples() {
        1
    } else {
        0
    }
}

//! # AST Language Support Definitions
//!
//! Defines comprehensive language support tiers and capabilities for 20+ programming languages.
//! Replaces the basic regex-based approach with proper AST analysis using tree-sitter.

use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use std::collections::HashMap;

/// Programming language support (focused on tree-sitter languages)
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum AstLanguage {
    // Currently supported with tree-sitter
    Python,
    JavaScript,
    TypeScript,
    Go,
    Rust,
    Html,

    // Future tree-sitter support (when dependencies added)
    Java,
    C,
    Cpp,
    Ruby,
    CSharp,
}

/// Language support tier indicating analysis depth
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum LanguageTier {
    /// Full AST parsing with tree-sitter
    FullAst,
    /// Syntax-aware parsing for markup languages
    SyntaxAware,
    /// Future support (not yet implemented)
    Future,
}

/// Language-specific features and capabilities
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct LanguageFeatures {
    /// Support tier
    pub tier: LanguageTier,
    /// Can extract functions/methods
    pub has_functions: bool,
    /// Can extract classes/types
    pub has_classes: bool,
    /// Has documentation conventions
    pub has_documentation: bool,
    /// Has import/dependency statements
    pub has_imports: bool,
    /// Language-specific complexity factors
    pub complexity_factors: Vec&lt;String&gt;,
    /// Common file extensions
    pub extensions: Vec&lt;String&gt;,
}

impl AstLanguage {
    /// Get the tree-sitter language for this language (Tier 1 and 2 only)
    #[cfg(feature = &quot;tree-sitter&quot;)]
    pub fn tree_sitter_language(&amp;self) -&gt; Option&lt;tree_sitter::Language&gt; {
        match self {
            // Tier 1: Full AST languages
            AstLanguage::Python =&gt; Some(tree_sitter_python::language()),
            AstLanguage::JavaScript =&gt; Some(tree_sitter_javascript::language()),
            AstLanguage::TypeScript =&gt; Some(tree_sitter_typescript::language_typescript()),
            AstLanguage::Go =&gt; Some(tree_sitter_go::language()),
            AstLanguage::Rust =&gt; Some(tree_sitter_rust::language()),
            AstLanguage::Html =&gt; Some(tree_sitter_html::language()),

            // Future tree-sitter languages (when dependencies are added)
            AstLanguage::Java =&gt; None, // tree_sitter_java::language() when added
            AstLanguage::CSharp =&gt; None, // tree_sitter_c_sharp::language() when added
            AstLanguage::C =&gt; None,    // tree_sitter_c::language() when added
            AstLanguage::Cpp =&gt; None,  // tree_sitter_cpp::language() when added
            AstLanguage::PHP =&gt; None,  // tree_sitter_php::language() when added
            AstLanguage::Ruby =&gt; None, // tree_sitter_ruby::language() when added
            AstLanguage::Swift =&gt; None, // tree_sitter_swift::language() when added
            AstLanguage::Kotlin =&gt; None, // tree_sitter_kotlin::language() when added

            // Tier 2: Syntax-aware languages
            AstLanguage::Css =&gt; None, // tree_sitter_css::language() when added
            AstLanguage::Json =&gt; None, // tree_sitter_json::language() when added
            AstLanguage::Yaml =&gt; None, // tree_sitter_yaml::language() when added
            AstLanguage::Xml =&gt; None, // tree_sitter_xml::language() when added
            AstLanguage::Markdown =&gt; None, // tree_sitter_markdown::language() when added
            AstLanguage::Sql =&gt; None, // tree_sitter_sql::language() when added
            AstLanguage::Bash =&gt; None, // tree_sitter_bash::language() when added
            AstLanguage::PowerShell =&gt; None, // tree_sitter_powershell::language() when added
            AstLanguage::Dockerfile =&gt; None, // tree_sitter_dockerfile::language() when added

            // Tier 3: Basic structure languages (no tree-sitter)
            _ =&gt; None,
        }
    }

    /// Detect language from file extension
    pub fn from_extension(ext: &amp;str) -&gt; Option&lt;Self&gt; {
        match ext.to_lowercase().as_str() {
            // Currently supported
            &quot;py&quot; | &quot;pyi&quot; | &quot;pyw&quot; =&gt; Some(AstLanguage::Python),
            &quot;js&quot; | &quot;mjs&quot; | &quot;cjs&quot; =&gt; Some(AstLanguage::JavaScript),
            &quot;ts&quot; | &quot;mts&quot; | &quot;cts&quot; | &quot;tsx&quot; =&gt; Some(AstLanguage::TypeScript),
            &quot;go&quot; =&gt; Some(AstLanguage::Go),
            &quot;rs&quot; =&gt; Some(AstLanguage::Rust),
            &quot;html&quot; | &quot;htm&quot; =&gt; Some(AstLanguage::Html),

            // Future support
            &quot;java&quot; =&gt; Some(AstLanguage::Java),
            &quot;c&quot; =&gt; Some(AstLanguage::C),
            &quot;cpp&quot; | &quot;cc&quot; | &quot;cxx&quot; | &quot;c++&quot; | &quot;hpp&quot; | &quot;h&quot; =&gt; Some(AstLanguage::Cpp),
            &quot;rb&quot; | &quot;ruby&quot; =&gt; Some(AstLanguage::Ruby),
            &quot;cs&quot; =&gt; Some(AstLanguage::CSharp),

            _ =&gt; None,
        }
    }

    /// Get language tier
    pub fn tier(&amp;self) -&gt; LanguageTier {
        match self {
            // Currently supported with tree-sitter
            AstLanguage::Python
            | AstLanguage::JavaScript
            | AstLanguage::TypeScript
            | AstLanguage::Go
            | AstLanguage::Rust =&gt; LanguageTier::FullAst,

            // Syntax-aware (markup)
            AstLanguage::Html =&gt; LanguageTier::SyntaxAware,

            // Future support
            AstLanguage::Java
            | AstLanguage::C
            | AstLanguage::Cpp
            | AstLanguage::Ruby
            | AstLanguage::CSharp =&gt; LanguageTier::Future,
        }
    }

    /// Get language features and capabilities
    pub fn features(&amp;self) -&gt; LanguageFeatures {
        match self {
            AstLanguage::Python =&gt; LanguageFeatures {
                tier: LanguageTier::FullAst,
                has_functions: true,
                has_classes: true,
                has_documentation: true,
                has_imports: true,
                complexity_factors: vec![
                    &quot;list_comprehensions&quot;.to_string(),
                    &quot;decorators&quot;.to_string(),
                    &quot;async_await&quot;.to_string(),
                    &quot;generators&quot;.to_string(),
                ],
                extensions: vec![&quot;py&quot;.to_string(), &quot;pyi&quot;.to_string(), &quot;pyw&quot;.to_string()],
            },

            AstLanguage::JavaScript =&gt; LanguageFeatures {
                tier: LanguageTier::FullAst,
                has_functions: true,
                has_classes: true,
                has_documentation: true,
                has_imports: true,
                complexity_factors: vec![
                    &quot;closures&quot;.to_string(),
                    &quot;promises&quot;.to_string(),
                    &quot;async_await&quot;.to_string(),
                    &quot;prototypal_inheritance&quot;.to_string(),
                ],
                extensions: vec![&quot;js&quot;.to_string(), &quot;mjs&quot;.to_string(), &quot;cjs&quot;.to_string()],
            },

            AstLanguage::TypeScript =&gt; LanguageFeatures {
                tier: LanguageTier::FullAst,
                has_functions: true,
                has_classes: true,
                has_documentation: true,
                has_imports: true,
                complexity_factors: vec![
                    &quot;generic_types&quot;.to_string(),
                    &quot;type_guards&quot;.to_string(),
                    &quot;conditional_types&quot;.to_string(),
                    &quot;mapped_types&quot;.to_string(),
                ],
                extensions: vec![&quot;ts&quot;.to_string(), &quot;tsx&quot;.to_string(), &quot;mts&quot;.to_string()],
            },

            AstLanguage::Rust =&gt; LanguageFeatures {
                tier: LanguageTier::FullAst,
                has_functions: true,
                has_classes: false, // Rust has structs/traits instead
                has_documentation: true,
                has_imports: true,
                complexity_factors: vec![
                    &quot;lifetimes&quot;.to_string(),
                    &quot;borrowing&quot;.to_string(),
                    &quot;pattern_matching&quot;.to_string(),
                    &quot;macros&quot;.to_string(),
                ],
                extensions: vec![&quot;rs&quot;.to_string()],
            },

            AstLanguage::Go =&gt; LanguageFeatures {
                tier: LanguageTier::FullAst,
                has_functions: true,
                has_classes: false, // Go has structs/interfaces instead
                has_documentation: true,
                has_imports: true,
                complexity_factors: vec![
                    &quot;goroutines&quot;.to_string(),
                    &quot;channels&quot;.to_string(),
                    &quot;interfaces&quot;.to_string(),
                    &quot;defer_statements&quot;.to_string(),
                ],
                extensions: vec![&quot;go&quot;.to_string()],
            },

            AstLanguage::Java =&gt; LanguageFeatures {
                tier: LanguageTier::FullAst,
                has_functions: true,
                has_classes: true,
                has_documentation: true,
                has_imports: true,
                complexity_factors: vec![
                    &quot;inheritance&quot;.to_string(),
                    &quot;generics&quot;.to_string(),
                    &quot;reflection&quot;.to_string(),
                    &quot;annotations&quot;.to_string(),
                ],
                extensions: vec![&quot;java&quot;.to_string()],
            },

            // Add more language features as needed...
            _ =&gt; LanguageFeatures {
                tier: self.tier(),
                has_functions: false,
                has_classes: false,
                has_documentation: false,
                has_imports: false,
                complexity_factors: vec![],
                extensions: vec![],
            },
        }
    }

    /// Get all supported languages
    pub fn all_supported() -&gt; Vec&lt;Self&gt; {
        vec![
            // Currently supported
            AstLanguage::Python,
            AstLanguage::JavaScript,
            AstLanguage::TypeScript,
            AstLanguage::Go,
            AstLanguage::Rust,
            AstLanguage::Html,
            // Future support
            AstLanguage::Java,
            AstLanguage::C,
            AstLanguage::Cpp,
            AstLanguage::Ruby,
            AstLanguage::CSharp,
        ]
    }

    /// Get language name as string
    pub fn name(&amp;self) -&gt; &amp;&#x27;static str {
        match self {
            AstLanguage::Python =&gt; &quot;Python&quot;,
            AstLanguage::JavaScript =&gt; &quot;JavaScript&quot;,
            AstLanguage::TypeScript =&gt; &quot;TypeScript&quot;,
            AstLanguage::Go =&gt; &quot;Go&quot;,
            AstLanguage::Rust =&gt; &quot;Rust&quot;,
            AstLanguage::Html =&gt; &quot;HTML&quot;,
            AstLanguage::Java =&gt; &quot;Java&quot;,
            AstLanguage::C =&gt; &quot;C&quot;,
            AstLanguage::Cpp =&gt; &quot;C++&quot;,
            AstLanguage::Ruby =&gt; &quot;Ruby&quot;,
            AstLanguage::CSharp =&gt; &quot;C#&quot;,
        }
    }
}

/// Language statistics for reporting
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct LanguageStats {
    /// Total supported languages
    pub total_languages: usize,
    /// Languages by tier
    pub by_tier: HashMap&lt;LanguageTier, usize&gt;,
    /// Languages with AST support
    pub ast_supported: usize,
    /// Languages with tree-sitter support
    pub tree_sitter_available: usize,
}

impl LanguageStats {
    /// Calculate statistics for current language support
    pub fn calculate() -&gt; Self {
        let all_languages = AstLanguage::all_supported();
        let total_languages = all_languages.len();

        let mut by_tier = HashMap::new();
        let mut ast_supported = 0;
        let mut tree_sitter_available = 0;

        for language in &amp;all_languages {
            let tier = language.tier();
            *by_tier.entry(tier).or_insert(0) += 1;

            if tier == LanguageTier::FullAst || tier == LanguageTier::SyntaxAware {
                ast_supported += 1;
            }

            #[cfg(feature = &quot;tree-sitter&quot;)]
            if language.tree_sitter_language().is_some() {
                tree_sitter_available += 1;
            }
        }

        Self {
            total_languages,
            by_tier,
            ast_supported,
            tree_sitter_available,
        }
    }
}

//! # Advanced Template Detection System
//!
//! Implements sophisticated template engine detection using multiple methods:
//! 1. Extension-based detection for known template file types
//! 2. AST-based content pattern analysis for template syntax detection
//! 3. Tree-sitter parsing for HTML/XML files that might be templates
//! 4. Directory context analysis for template-like structures
//!
//! This module uses tree-sitter AST parsing instead of regex patterns
//! for accurate template detection and better performance.

use once_cell::sync::Lazy;
use scribe_core::Result;
use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::fs;
use std::io::{BufRead, BufReader};
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
use tree_sitter::{Language as TsLanguage, Node, Parser, Tree};

/// Template engine classification
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
pub enum TemplateEngine {
    // JavaScript template engines
    Handlebars,
    Mustache,
    Ejs,
    Pug,
    Jade,

    // Python template engines
    Django,
    Jinja2,
    Mako,

    // PHP template engines
    Twig,
    Smarty,

    // Ruby template engines
    Erb,
    Haml,

    // Other template engines
    Liquid,
    Dust,
    Eta,

    // Frontend frameworks with templates
    Vue,
    Svelte,
    React, // JSX/TSX
    Angular,

    // Generic/Unknown template
    Generic,
}

impl TemplateEngine {
    /// Get the typical file extensions for this template engine
    pub fn extensions(&amp;self) -&gt; &amp;&#x27;static [&amp;&#x27;static str] {
        match self {
            TemplateEngine::Handlebars =&gt; &amp;[&quot;.hbs&quot;, &quot;.handlebars&quot;],
            TemplateEngine::Mustache =&gt; &amp;[&quot;.mustache&quot;],
            TemplateEngine::Ejs =&gt; &amp;[&quot;.ejs&quot;],
            TemplateEngine::Pug =&gt; &amp;[&quot;.pug&quot;],
            TemplateEngine::Jade =&gt; &amp;[&quot;.jade&quot;],
            TemplateEngine::Django =&gt; &amp;[&quot;.html&quot;, &quot;.htm&quot;], // Context dependent
            TemplateEngine::Jinja2 =&gt; &amp;[&quot;.j2&quot;, &quot;.jinja&quot;, &quot;.jinja2&quot;],
            TemplateEngine::Mako =&gt; &amp;[&quot;.mako&quot;],
            TemplateEngine::Twig =&gt; &amp;[&quot;.twig&quot;],
            TemplateEngine::Smarty =&gt; &amp;[&quot;.tpl&quot;],
            TemplateEngine::Erb =&gt; &amp;[&quot;.erb&quot;, &quot;.rhtml&quot;],
            TemplateEngine::Haml =&gt; &amp;[&quot;.haml&quot;],
            TemplateEngine::Liquid =&gt; &amp;[&quot;.liquid&quot;],
            TemplateEngine::Dust =&gt; &amp;[&quot;.dust&quot;],
            TemplateEngine::Eta =&gt; &amp;[&quot;.eta&quot;],
            TemplateEngine::Vue =&gt; &amp;[&quot;.vue&quot;],
            TemplateEngine::Svelte =&gt; &amp;[&quot;.svelte&quot;],
            TemplateEngine::React =&gt; &amp;[&quot;.jsx&quot;, &quot;.tsx&quot;],
            TemplateEngine::Angular =&gt; &amp;[&quot;.html&quot;], // Context dependent
            TemplateEngine::Generic =&gt; &amp;[],
        }
    }

    /// Get score boost factor for this template engine
    pub fn score_boost(&amp;self) -&gt; f64 {
        match self {
            // High priority for dedicated template files
            TemplateEngine::Handlebars
            | TemplateEngine::Mustache
            | TemplateEngine::Jinja2
            | TemplateEngine::Twig
            | TemplateEngine::Liquid =&gt; 1.5,

            // Moderate priority for framework templates
            TemplateEngine::Vue | TemplateEngine::Svelte | TemplateEngine::React =&gt; 1.3,

            // Standard boost for other template engines
            TemplateEngine::Ejs
            | TemplateEngine::Pug
            | TemplateEngine::Erb
            | TemplateEngine::Haml =&gt; 1.2,

            // Lower boost for generic HTML templates
            TemplateEngine::Django | TemplateEngine::Angular =&gt; 1.0,

            // Minimal boost for unknown templates
            TemplateEngine::Generic =&gt; 0.8,

            _ =&gt; 1.0,
        }
    }
}

/// Method used for template detection
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum TemplateDetectionMethod {
    /// Detected by file extension
    Extension,
    /// Detected by content pattern analysis
    ContentPattern,
    /// Detected by directory context
    DirectoryContext,
    /// Detected by language heuristics
    LanguageHeuristic,
}

/// Result of template detection
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct TemplateDetectionResult {
    /// Whether the file is detected as a template
    pub is_template: bool,
    /// The detected template engine (if any)
    pub engine: Option&lt;TemplateEngine&gt;,
    /// Method used for detection
    pub detection_method: TemplateDetectionMethod,
    /// Confidence score (0.0 to 1.0)
    pub confidence: f64,
    /// Score boost to apply
    pub score_boost: f64,
}

impl TemplateDetectionResult {
    pub fn not_template() -&gt; Self {
        Self {
            is_template: false,
            engine: None,
            detection_method: TemplateDetectionMethod::Extension,
            confidence: 0.0,
            score_boost: 0.0,
        }
    }

    pub fn template(
        engine: TemplateEngine,
        method: TemplateDetectionMethod,
        confidence: f64,
    ) -&gt; Self {
        let score_boost = engine.score_boost();
        Self {
            is_template: true,
            engine: Some(engine),
            detection_method: method,
            confidence,
            score_boost,
        }
    }
}

/// Template pattern definition for content analysis
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct TemplatePattern {
    pub open_tag: String,
    pub close_tag: String,
    pub engine: TemplateEngine,
    pub min_occurrences: usize,
}

impl TemplatePattern {
    pub fn new(open: &amp;str, close: &amp;str, engine: TemplateEngine, min_occurrences: usize) -&gt; Self {
        Self {
            open_tag: open.to_string(),
            close_tag: close.to_string(),
            engine,
            min_occurrences,
        }
    }
}

/// Static template patterns for content analysis
static TEMPLATE_PATTERNS: Lazy&lt;Vec&lt;TemplatePattern&gt;&gt; = Lazy::new(|| {

        TemplatePattern::new(&quot;{{{&quot;, &quot;}}}&quot;, TemplateEngine::Handlebars, 1),
        // Jinja2, Django, Liquid patterns
        TemplatePattern::new(&quot;{%&quot;, &quot;%}&quot;, TemplateEngine::Jinja2, 2),
        TemplatePattern::new(&quot;{{&quot;, &quot;}}&quot;, TemplateEngine::Jinja2, 1), // Also Handlebars
        // EJS, ERB patterns
        TemplatePattern::new(&quot;&lt;%&quot;, &quot;%&gt;&quot;, TemplateEngine::Ejs, 2),
        TemplatePattern::new(&quot;&lt;%=&quot;, &quot;%&gt;&quot;, TemplateEngine::Ejs, 1),
        TemplatePattern::new(&quot;&lt;%#&quot;, &quot;%&gt;&quot;, TemplateEngine::Ejs, 1),
        // FreeMarker patterns
        TemplatePattern::new(&quot;&lt;#&quot;, &quot;#&gt;&quot;, TemplateEngine::Generic, 2),
        // Template literals and other patterns
        TemplatePattern::new(&quot;${&quot;, &quot;}&quot;, TemplateEngine::Generic, 3),
        TemplatePattern::new(&quot;@{&quot;, &quot;}&quot;, TemplateEngine::Generic, 2),
        TemplatePattern::new(&quot;[[&quot;, &quot;]]&quot;, TemplateEngine::Generic, 2),
    ]
});
