/// Single-pattern indicators for template detection
static SINGLE_PATTERNS: &amp;[&amp;str] = &amp;[
    &quot;ng-&quot;,        // Angular directives
    &quot;v-&quot;,         // Vue directives
    &quot;:&quot;,          // Vue shorthand or other template syntax
    &quot;data-bind&quot;,  // Knockout.js
    &quot;handlebars&quot;, // Handlebars comments
    &quot;jinja&quot;,      // Jinja comments
    &quot;mustache&quot;,   // Mustache comments
    &quot;twig&quot;,       // Twig comments
    &quot;liquid&quot;,     // Liquid comments
];

/// Template directory indicators
static TEMPLATE_DIRECTORIES: &amp;[&amp;str] = &amp;[
    &quot;template&quot;,
    &quot;templates&quot;,
    &quot;_includes&quot;,
    &quot;_layouts&quot;,
    &quot;layout&quot;,
    &quot;layouts&quot;,
    &quot;view&quot;,
    &quot;views&quot;,
    &quot;component&quot;,
    &quot;components&quot;,
    &quot;partial&quot;,
    &quot;partials&quot;,
];

/// Advanced template detection engine
pub struct TemplateDetector {
    /// AST parsers for different languages
    parsers: HashMap&lt;String, Parser&gt;,
    /// File content cache (for performance)
    content_cache: HashMap&lt;PathBuf, String&gt;,
    /// Cache size limit
    max_cache_size: usize,
}

impl std::fmt::Debug for TemplateDetector {
    fn fmt(&amp;self, f: &amp;mut std::fmt::Formatter&lt;&#x27;_&gt;) -&gt; std::fmt::Result {
        f.debug_struct(&quot;TemplateDetector&quot;)
            .field(&quot;parsers&quot;, &amp;format!(&quot;[{} parsers]&quot;, self.parsers.len()))
            .field(
                &quot;content_cache&quot;,
                &amp;format!(&quot;[{} cached items]&quot;, self.content_cache.len()),
            )
            .field(&quot;max_cache_size&quot;, &amp;self.max_cache_size)
            .finish()
    }
}

impl TemplateDetector {
    /// Create a new template detector
    pub fn new() -&gt; Result&lt;Self&gt; {
        let mut parsers = HashMap::new();

        // Initialize HTML parser for template detection
        let mut html_parser = Parser::new();
        html_parser
            .set_language(tree_sitter_html::language())
            .map_err(|e| {
                scribe_core::ScribeError::parse(format!(&quot;Failed to set HTML language: {}&quot;, e))
            })?;
        parsers.insert(&quot;html&quot;.to_string(), html_parser);

        Ok(Self {
            parsers,
            content_cache: HashMap::new(),
            max_cache_size: 100, // Cache up to 100 files
        })
    }

    /// Detect if a file is a template and get appropriate score boost
    pub fn detect_template(&amp;mut self, file_path: &amp;str) -&gt; Result&lt;TemplateDetectionResult&gt; {
        let path = Path::new(file_path);

        // Method 1: Extension-based detection (fastest)
        if let Some(result) = self.detect_by_extension(path) {
            return Ok(result);
        }

        // Method 2: Directory context analysis
        if let Some(result) = self.detect_by_directory_context(path) {
            return Ok(result);
        }

        // Method 3: Content pattern analysis (slower, for ambiguous files)
        if self.should_analyze_content(path) {
            if let Some(result) = self.detect_by_content_patterns(path)? {
                return Ok(result);
            }
        }

        // Method 4: Language-specific heuristics
        if let Some(result) = self.detect_by_language_heuristics(path) {
            return Ok(result);
        }

        Ok(TemplateDetectionResult::not_template())
    }

    /// Get template score boost for a file path
    pub fn get_score_boost(&amp;self, file_path: &amp;str) -&gt; Result&lt;f64&gt; {
        // Use a simplified version that doesn&#x27;t require mutable self
        let path = Path::new(file_path);

        // Extension-based detection
        if let Some(engine) = self.detect_engine_by_extension(path) {
            return Ok(engine.score_boost());
        }

        // Directory context check
        if self.is_in_template_directory(path) {
            return Ok(1.2); // Moderate boost for template directories
        }

        Ok(0.0)
    }

    /// Detect template engine by file extension
    fn detect_by_extension(&amp;self, path: &amp;Path) -&gt; Option&lt;TemplateDetectionResult&gt; {
        if let Some(engine) = self.detect_engine_by_extension(path) {
            return Some(TemplateDetectionResult::template(
                engine,
                TemplateDetectionMethod::Extension,
                0.95, // High confidence for extension-based detection
            ));
        }
        None
    }

    fn detect_engine_by_extension(&amp;self, path: &amp;Path) -&gt; Option&lt;TemplateEngine&gt; {
        let extension = path.extension()?.to_str()?.to_lowercase();
        let ext_with_dot = format!(&quot;.{}&quot;, extension);

        EXTENSION_MAP.get(ext_with_dot.as_str()).cloned()
    }

    /// Detect by directory context
    fn detect_by_directory_context(&amp;self, path: &amp;Path) -&gt; Option&lt;TemplateDetectionResult&gt; {
        if self.is_in_template_directory(path) {
            // Check if it&#x27;s HTML/XML in a template directory
            if let Some(ext) = path.extension() {
                let ext_str = ext.to_str()?.to_lowercase();
                if matches!(ext_str.as_str(), &quot;html&quot; | &quot;htm&quot; | &quot;xml&quot;) {
                    return Some(TemplateDetectionResult::template(
                        TemplateEngine::Generic,
                        TemplateDetectionMethod::DirectoryContext,
                        0.7, // Moderate confidence for directory context
                    ));
                }
            }
        }
        None
    }

    fn is_in_template_directory(&amp;self, path: &amp;Path) -&gt; bool {
        let path_str = path.to_string_lossy().to_lowercase();
        TEMPLATE_DIRECTORIES
            .iter()
            .any(|dir| path_str.contains(dir))
    }

    /// Check if file should be analyzed for content patterns
    fn should_analyze_content(&amp;self, path: &amp;Path) -&gt; bool {
        // Only analyze potentially ambiguous files
        if let Some(ext) = path.extension() {
            let ext_str = ext.to_str().unwrap_or(&quot;&quot;).to_lowercase();
            return matches!(ext_str.as_str(), &quot;html&quot; | &quot;htm&quot; | &quot;xml&quot; | &quot;js&quot; | &quot;ts&quot;);
        }
        false
    }

    /// Detect templates by AST-based content pattern analysis
    fn detect_by_content_patterns(
        &amp;mut self,
        path: &amp;Path,
    ) -&gt; Result&lt;Option&lt;TemplateDetectionResult&gt;&gt; {
        let content = self.read_file_content(path)?;

        // First check for simple template patterns (lightweight check)
        for pattern in TEMPLATE_PATTERNS.iter() {
            let occurrences =
                self.count_pattern_occurrences(&amp;content, &amp;pattern.open_tag, &amp;pattern.close_tag);

            if occurrences &gt;= pattern.min_occurrences {
                return Ok(Some(TemplateDetectionResult::template(
                    pattern.engine.clone(),
                    TemplateDetectionMethod::ContentPattern,
                    0.8, // Good confidence for pattern-based detection
                )));
            }
        }

        // If it&#x27;s HTML/XML content, try AST-based analysis
        if self.should_use_ast_analysis(path) {
            if let Some(result) = self.analyze_with_ast(path, &amp;content)? {
                return Ok(Some(result));
            }
        }

        // Check for single-pattern indicators as fallback
        let content_lower = content.to_lowercase();
        for &amp;pattern in SINGLE_PATTERNS {
            if content_lower.contains(pattern) {
                return Ok(Some(TemplateDetectionResult::template(
                    TemplateEngine::Generic,
                    TemplateDetectionMethod::ContentPattern,
                    0.6, // Lower confidence for single patterns
                )));
            }
        }

        Ok(None)
    }

    /// Detect by language-specific heuristics
    fn detect_by_language_heuristics(&amp;self, path: &amp;Path) -&gt; Option&lt;TemplateDetectionResult&gt; {
        // This is a placeholder for more sophisticated language analysis
        // In a full implementation, this might use tree-sitter or similar
        // for AST-based template detection

        if let Some(ext) = path.extension() {
            let ext_str = ext.to_str()?.to_lowercase();

            // JSX/TSX are React templates
            if matches!(ext_str.as_str(), &quot;jsx&quot; | &quot;tsx&quot;) {
                return Some(TemplateDetectionResult::template(
                    TemplateEngine::React,
                    TemplateDetectionMethod::LanguageHeuristic,
                    0.9,
                ));
            }
        }

        None
    }

    /// Read file content with caching
    fn read_file_content(&amp;mut self, path: &amp;Path) -&gt; Result&lt;String&gt; {
        // Check cache first
        if let Some(content) = self.content_cache.get(path) {
            return Ok(content.clone());
        }

        // Read file (limit to first 2KB for performance)
        let file = fs::File::open(path)?;
        let reader = BufReader::new(file);
        let mut content = String::new();
        let mut bytes_read = 0;
        const MAX_READ_SIZE: usize = 2048;

        for line in reader.lines() {
            let line = line?;
            if bytes_read + line.len() &gt; MAX_READ_SIZE {
                break;
            }
            content.push_str(&amp;line);
            content.push(&#x27;\n&#x27;);
            bytes_read += line.len() + 1;
        }

        // Cache the content (with size limit)
        if self.content_cache.len() &lt; self.max_cache_size {
            self.content_cache
                .insert(path.to_path_buf(), content.clone());
        }

        Ok(content)
    }

    /// Count occurrences of a pattern pair in content
    fn count_pattern_occurrences(&amp;self, content: &amp;str, open_tag: &amp;str, close_tag: &amp;str) -&gt; usize {
        let open_count = content.matches(open_tag).count();
        let close_count = content.matches(close_tag).count();

        // Return the minimum of open and close tags (pairs)
        open_count.min(close_count)
    }

    /// Check if file should use AST analysis
    fn should_use_ast_analysis(&amp;self, path: &amp;Path) -&gt; bool {
        if let Some(ext) = path.extension() {
            let ext_str = ext.to_str().unwrap_or(&quot;&quot;).to_lowercase();
            return matches!(ext_str.as_str(), &quot;html&quot; | &quot;htm&quot; | &quot;xml&quot; | &quot;vue&quot; | &quot;svelte&quot;);
        }
        false
    }

    /// Analyze content using AST parsing
    fn analyze_with_ast(
        &amp;mut self,
        path: &amp;Path,
        content: &amp;str,
    ) -&gt; Result&lt;Option&lt;TemplateDetectionResult&gt;&gt; {
        if let Some(parser) = self.parsers.get_mut(&quot;html&quot;) {
            if let Some(tree) = parser.parse(content, None) {
                let root_node = tree.root_node();

                // Check for template-specific patterns in AST
                if self.has_template_attributes(&amp;root_node) {
                    let engine = self.detect_template_engine_from_ast(&amp;root_node, path);
                    return Ok(Some(TemplateDetectionResult::template(
                        engine,
                        TemplateDetectionMethod::ContentPattern,
                        0.85, // High confidence for AST-based detection
                    )));
                }
            }
        }
        Ok(None)
    }

    /// Check for template-specific attributes in HTML AST
    fn has_template_attributes(&amp;self, node: &amp;Node) -&gt; bool {
        let template_indicators = [
            &quot;v-&quot;,     // Vue.js directives
            &quot;ng-&quot;,    // Angular directives
            &quot;*ng&quot;,    // Angular structural directives
            &quot;:bind&quot;,  // Vue binding
            &quot;@click&quot;, // Vue events
            &quot;{{{&quot;,    // Template expressions
            &quot;{{&quot;,     // Template expressions
            &quot;&lt;%&quot;,     // EJS, ERB
            &quot;{%&quot;,     // Jinja2, Liquid
        ];

        self.node_contains_patterns(node, &amp;template_indicators)
    }

    /// Recursively check if node or its children contain template patterns
    fn node_contains_patterns(&amp;self, node: &amp;Node, patterns: &amp;[&amp;str]) -&gt; bool {
        // Check current node kind
        if patterns
            .iter()
            .any(|&amp;pattern| node.kind().contains(pattern))
        {
            return true;
        }

        // Check node text content if it&#x27;s a text node
        if node.kind() == &quot;text&quot; || node.kind() == &quot;attribute_value&quot; {
            // For text nodes, we&#x27;d need the actual content, which requires the source text
            // This is a simplified check - in practice you&#x27;d get the node&#x27;s text from content
            return true; // Assume potential template content for now
        }

        // Recursively check children
        for i in 0..node.child_count() {
            if let Some(child) = node.child(i) {
                if self.node_contains_patterns(&amp;child, patterns) {
                    return true;
                }
            }
        }

        false
    }

    /// Detect specific template engine from AST patterns
    fn detect_template_engine_from_ast(&amp;self, node: &amp;Node, path: &amp;Path) -&gt; TemplateEngine {
        // Check file extension first
        if let Some(ext) = path.extension() {
            let ext_str = ext.to_str().unwrap_or(&quot;&quot;).to_lowercase();
            match ext_str.as_str() {
                &quot;vue&quot; =&gt; return TemplateEngine::Vue,
                &quot;svelte&quot; =&gt; return TemplateEngine::Svelte,
                _ =&gt; {}
            }
        }

        // Analyze AST structure for engine-specific patterns
        if self.has_vue_patterns(node) {
            TemplateEngine::Vue
        } else if self.has_angular_patterns(node) {
            TemplateEngine::Angular
        } else if self.has_react_patterns(node) {
            TemplateEngine::React
        } else {
            TemplateEngine::Generic
        }
    }

    /// Check for Vue.js specific patterns
    fn has_vue_patterns(&amp;self, node: &amp;Node) -&gt; bool {
        let vue_patterns = [&quot;v-if&quot;, &quot;v-for&quot;, &quot;v-model&quot;, &quot;v-bind&quot;, &quot;@click&quot;, &quot;:class&quot;];
        self.node_contains_patterns(node, &amp;vue_patterns)
    }

    /// Check for Angular specific patterns
    fn has_angular_patterns(&amp;self, node: &amp;Node) -&gt; bool {
        let angular_patterns = [&quot;*ngFor&quot;, &quot;*ngIf&quot;, &quot;(click)&quot;, &quot;[class]&quot;, &quot;[(ngModel)]&quot;];
        self.node_contains_patterns(node, &amp;angular_patterns)
    }

    /// Check for React JSX patterns (limited in HTML parser)
    fn has_react_patterns(&amp;self, node: &amp;Node) -&gt; bool {
        let react_patterns = [&quot;className&quot;, &quot;onClick&quot;, &quot;onChange&quot;];
        self.node_contains_patterns(node, &amp;react_patterns)
    }

    /// Clear content cache
    pub fn clear_cache(&amp;mut self) {
        self.content_cache.clear();
    }
}

impl Default for TemplateDetector {
    fn default() -&gt; Self {
        Self::new().expect(&quot;Failed to create TemplateDetector&quot;)
    }
}

/// Convenience function to check if a file is a template
pub fn is_template_file(file_path: &amp;str) -&gt; Result&lt;bool&gt; {
    let mut detector = TemplateDetector::new()?;
    let result = detector.detect_template(file_path)?;
    Ok(result.is_template)
}

/// Convenience function to get template score boost
pub fn get_template_score_boost(file_path: &amp;str) -&gt; Result&lt;f64&gt; {
    let detector = TemplateDetector::new()?;
    detector.get_score_boost(file_path)
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use std::fs;
    use std::io::Write;
    use tempfile::NamedTempFile;

    fn create_test_file(content: &amp;str, extension: &amp;str) -&gt; NamedTempFile {
        let mut file = NamedTempFile::new().unwrap();
        file.write_all(content.as_bytes()).unwrap();

        // Rename with proper extension (this is a bit hacky but works for tests)
        let path = file.path().with_extension(extension);
        std::fs::rename(file.path(), &amp;path).unwrap();

        file
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_extension_based_detection() {
        let detector = TemplateDetector::new().unwrap();

        // Test known template extensions
        assert_eq!(
            detector.detect_engine_by_extension(Path::new(&quot;template.hbs&quot;)),
            Some(TemplateEngine::Handlebars)
        );

        assert_eq!(
            detector.detect_engine_by_extension(Path::new(&quot;view.j2&quot;)),
            Some(TemplateEngine::Jinja2)
        );

        assert_eq!(
            detector.detect_engine_by_extension(Path::new(&quot;component.jsx&quot;)),
            Some(TemplateEngine::React)
        );

        // Test non-template extension
        assert_eq!(
            detector.detect_engine_by_extension(Path::new(&quot;script.js&quot;)),
            None
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_directory_context_detection() {
        let detector = TemplateDetector::new().unwrap();

        assert!(detector.is_in_template_directory(Path::new(&quot;templates/layout.html&quot;)));
        assert!(detector.is_in_template_directory(Path::new(&quot;src/components/header.html&quot;)));
        assert!(!detector.is_in_template_directory(Path::new(&quot;src/utils/helper.js&quot;)));
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_pattern_counting() {
        let detector = TemplateDetector::new().unwrap();
        let content = &quot;Hello {{ name }}! Welcome to {{ site }}.&quot;;

        assert_eq!(detector.count_pattern_occurrences(content, &quot;{{&quot;, &quot;}}&quot;), 2);
        assert_eq!(detector.count_pattern_occurrences(content, &quot;{%&quot;, &quot;%}&quot;), 0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_template_score_boost() {
        let detector = TemplateDetector::new().unwrap();

        // High boost for dedicated template files
        assert!(detector.get_score_boost(&quot;template.hbs&quot;).unwrap() &gt; 1.0);

        // No boost for regular files
        assert_eq!(detector.get_score_boost(&quot;script.js&quot;).unwrap(), 0.0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_engine_score_boost() {
        assert!(TemplateEngine::Handlebars.score_boost() &gt; 1.0);
        assert!(TemplateEngine::React.score_boost() &gt; 1.0);
        assert!(TemplateEngine::Generic.score_boost() &lt; 1.0);
    }

//! Core data types for the heuristic scoring system

/// Complete score breakdown for a file
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct ScoreComponents {
    /// Final weighted score
    pub final_score: f64,

    /// Individual component scores
    pub doc_score: f64,
    pub readme_score: f64,
    pub import_score: f64,
    pub path_score: f64,
    pub test_link_score: f64,
    pub churn_score: f64,
    pub centrality_score: f64,
    pub entrypoint_score: f64,
    pub examples_score: f64,

    /// Boost components
    pub priority_boost: f64,
    pub template_boost: f64,

    /// Raw component scores before normalization
    pub raw_scores: RawScoreComponents,

    /// Applied weights
    pub weights: HeuristicWeights,
}

impl ScoreComponents {
    /// Convert score components to a map for analysis
    pub fn as_map(&amp;self) -&gt; std::collections::HashMap&lt;String, f64&gt; {
        let mut map = std::collections::HashMap::new();
        map.insert(&quot;final_score&quot;.to_string(), self.final_score);
        map.insert(&quot;doc_score&quot;.to_string(), self.doc_score);
        map.insert(&quot;readme_score&quot;.to_string(), self.readme_score);
        map.insert(&quot;import_score&quot;.to_string(), self.import_score);
        map.insert(&quot;path_score&quot;.to_string(), self.path_score);
        map.insert(&quot;test_link_score&quot;.to_string(), self.test_link_score);
        map.insert(&quot;churn_score&quot;.to_string(), self.churn_score);
        map.insert(&quot;centrality_score&quot;.to_string(), self.centrality_score);
        map.insert(&quot;entrypoint_score&quot;.to_string(), self.entrypoint_score);
        map.insert(&quot;examples_score&quot;.to_string(), self.examples_score);
        map.insert(&quot;priority_boost&quot;.to_string(), self.priority_boost);
        map.insert(&quot;template_boost&quot;.to_string(), self.template_boost);
        map
    }
}

/// Raw score components before normalization
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct RawScoreComponents {
    pub doc_raw: f64,
    pub readme_raw: f64,
    pub import_degree_in: usize,
    pub import_degree_out: usize,
    pub path_depth: usize,
    pub test_links_found: usize,
    pub churn_commits: usize,
    pub centrality_raw: f64,
    pub is_entrypoint: bool,
    pub examples_count: usize,
}

/// Configurable weights for the scoring formula
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct HeuristicWeights {
    pub doc_weight: f64,
    pub readme_weight: f64,
    pub import_weight: f64,
    pub path_weight: f64,
    pub test_link_weight: f64,
    pub churn_weight: f64,
    pub centrality_weight: f64, // V2 feature
    pub entrypoint_weight: f64,
    pub examples_weight: f64,

    /// Feature flags for advanced capabilities
    pub features: ScoringFeatures,
}

/// Feature flags for scoring system capabilities
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct ScoringFeatures {
    /// Enable PageRank centrality calculation (V2)
    pub enable_centrality: bool,
    /// Enable template detection boost
    pub enable_template_boost: bool,
    /// Enable advanced document analysis
    pub enable_doc_analysis: bool,
    /// Enable test-code relationship detection
    pub enable_test_linking: bool,
    /// Enable git churn analysis
    pub enable_churn_analysis: bool,
    /// Enable examples detection
    pub enable_examples_detection: bool,
}

impl Default for HeuristicWeights {
    fn default() -&gt; Self {
        Self {
            doc_weight: 1.5,
            readme_weight: 2.0,
            import_weight: 1.2,
            path_weight: -0.3,
            test_link_weight: 0.8,
            churn_weight: 0.5,
            centrality_weight: 1.0,
            entrypoint_weight: 2.5,
            examples_weight: 1.8,
            features: ScoringFeatures::default(),
        }
    }
}

impl HeuristicWeights {
    /// Create weights optimized for documentation discovery
    pub fn for_documentation() -&gt; Self {
        Self {
            doc_weight: 3.0,
            readme_weight: 4.0,
            examples_weight: 2.5,
            ..Default::default()
        }
    }

    /// Create weights optimized for core code discovery
    pub fn for_core_code() -&gt; Self {
        Self {
            import_weight: 2.0,
            centrality_weight: 2.5,
            entrypoint_weight: 3.0,
            path_weight: -0.5,
            ..Default::default()
        }
    }

    /// Create weights optimized for test discovery
    pub fn for_tests() -&gt; Self {
        Self {
            test_link_weight: 3.0,
            path_weight: 0.0, // Don&#x27;t penalize deep test paths
            doc_weight: 0.5,
            ..Default::default()
        }
    }

    /// Create balanced weights for general analysis
    pub fn balanced() -&gt; Self {
        Self::default()
    }

    /// V2 weights with enhanced features enabled
    pub fn with_v2_features() -&gt; Self {
        Self {
            doc_weight: 0.8,
            readme_weight: 1.0,
            import_weight: 0.6,
            path_weight: 0.4,
            test_link_weight: 0.3,
            churn_weight: 0.4,
            centrality_weight: 0.7, // V2 enables centrality
            entrypoint_weight: 0.9,
            examples_weight: 0.5,
            features: ScoringFeatures {
                enable_centrality: true, // Key V2 feature
                enable_template_boost: true,
                enable_doc_analysis: true,
                enable_test_linking: true,
                enable_churn_analysis: true,
                enable_examples_detection: true,
            },
        }
    }

    /// Normalize all weights to sum to 1.0 for balanced scoring
    pub fn normalized(mut self) -&gt; Self {
        let total_weight = self.doc_weight
            + self.readme_weight
            + self.import_weight
            + self.test_link_weight
            + self.churn_weight
            + self.centrality_weight
            + self.entrypoint_weight
            + self.examples_weight;

        if total_weight &gt; 0.0 {
            self.doc_weight /= total_weight;
            self.readme_weight /= total_weight;
            self.import_weight /= total_weight;
            self.test_link_weight /= total_weight;
            self.churn_weight /= total_weight;
            self.centrality_weight /= total_weight;
            self.entrypoint_weight /= total_weight;
            self.examples_weight /= total_weight;
        }

        self
    }
}

impl Default for ScoringFeatures {
    fn default() -&gt; Self {
        Self {
            enable_centrality: true,
            enable_template_boost: true,
            enable_doc_analysis: true,
            enable_test_linking: true,
            enable_churn_analysis: true,
            enable_examples_detection: true,
        }
    }
}

impl ScoringFeatures {
    /// Enable all features (maximum analysis depth)
    pub fn all_enabled() -&gt; Self {
        Self {
            enable_centrality: true,
            enable_template_boost: true,
            enable_doc_analysis: true,
            enable_test_linking: true,
            enable_churn_analysis: true,
            enable_examples_detection: true,
        }
    }

    /// Minimal feature set for fast analysis
    pub fn minimal() -&gt; Self {
        Self {
            enable_centrality: false,
            enable_template_boost: false,
            enable_doc_analysis: true,
            enable_test_linking: false,
            enable_churn_analysis: false,
            enable_examples_detection: true,
        }

    /// Documentation-focused feature set

//! # Documentation Coverage Analysis
//!
//! Analyzes documentation coverage in source code files, including docstrings,
//! comments, and inline documentation patterns.

use super::ast_language::AstLanguage;
use scribe_core::Result;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};

/// Documentation coverage analysis results
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct DocumentationCoverage {
    /// Total number of functions/methods
    pub total_functions: usize,
    /// Number of documented functions
    pub documented_functions: usize,
    /// Total number of classes
    pub total_classes: usize,
    /// Number of documented classes
    pub documented_classes: usize,
    /// Documentation coverage percentage
    pub coverage_percentage: f64,
    /// Lines of documentation
    pub documentation_lines: usize,
    /// Total lines of code
    pub total_lines: usize,
}

/// Documentation analyzer for specific languages
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct DocumentationAnalyzer {
    language: AstLanguage,
}

impl DocumentationAnalyzer {
    /// Create a new documentation analyzer
    pub fn new(language: AstLanguage) -&gt; Result&lt;Self&gt; {
        Ok(Self { language })
    }

    /// Analyze documentation coverage in source code
    pub fn analyze_coverage(&amp;self, content: &amp;str) -&gt; Result&lt;DocumentationCoverage&gt; {
        // Basic implementation - can be enhanced with AST analysis
        let lines: Vec&lt;&amp;str&gt; = content.lines().collect();
        let total_lines = lines.len();
        let documentation_lines = self.count_documentation_lines(&amp;lines);

        let coverage_percentage = if total_lines &gt; 0 {
            (documentation_lines as f64 / total_lines as f64) * 100.0
        } else {
            0.0
        };

        Ok(DocumentationCoverage {
            total_functions: 0,      // TODO: Extract from AST
            documented_functions: 0, // TODO: Extract from AST
            total_classes: 0,        // TODO: Extract from AST
            documented_classes: 0,   // TODO: Extract from AST
            coverage_percentage,
            documentation_lines,
            total_lines,
        })
    }

    /// Count lines that contain documentation
    fn count_documentation_lines(&amp;self, lines: &amp;[&amp;str]) -&gt; usize {
        lines
            .iter()
            .filter(|line| self.is_documentation_line(line))
            .count()
    }

    /// Check if a line contains documentation
    fn is_documentation_line(&amp;self, line: &amp;str) -&gt; bool {
        let trimmed = line.trim();

        match self.language {
            AstLanguage::Python =&gt; {
                trimmed.starts_with(&#x27;#&#x27;)
                    || trimmed.starts_with(&quot;\&quot;\&quot;\&quot;&quot;)
                    || trimmed.starts_with(&quot;&#x27;&#x27;&#x27;&quot;)
            }
            AstLanguage::JavaScript | AstLanguage::TypeScript =&gt; {
                trimmed.starts_with(&quot;//&quot;)
                    || trimmed.starts_with(&quot;/*&quot;)
                    || trimmed.starts_with(&quot;*&quot;)
                    || trimmed.starts_with(&quot;/**&quot;)
            }
            AstLanguage::Rust =&gt; {
                trimmed.starts_with(&quot;//&quot;)
                    || trimmed.starts_with(&quot;///&quot;)
                    || trimmed.starts_with(&quot;//!&quot;)
            }
            AstLanguage::Go =&gt; trimmed.starts_with(&quot;//&quot;),
            _ =&gt; {
                // Generic comment detection
                trimmed.starts_with(&quot;//&quot;)
                    || trimmed.starts_with(&quot;#&quot;)
                    || trimmed.starts_with(&quot;/*&quot;)
                    || trimmed.starts_with(&quot;*&quot;)
            }
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn test_python_documentation_analysis() {
        let analyzer = DocumentationAnalyzer::new(AstLanguage::Python).unwrap();
        let python_code = r#&quot;
# This is a comment
def hello():
    &quot;&quot;&quot;This is a docstring.&quot;&quot;&quot;
    print(&quot;Hello&quot;)

def world():
    # Another comment
    print(&quot;World&quot;)
&quot;#;

        let coverage = analyzer.analyze_coverage(python_code).unwrap();
        assert!(coverage.documentation_lines &gt; 0);
        assert!(coverage.coverage_percentage &gt; 0.0);
    }
}

//! # Language-Specific Metrics
//!
//! Calculates language-specific complexity and quality metrics that are
//! tailored to each programming language&#x27;s characteristics.

use super::ast_language::AstLanguage;
use scribe_core::Result;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};

/// Language-specific complexity factors
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct LanguageSpecificComplexity {
    /// Base complexity score
    pub base_complexity: f64,
    /// Language-specific factors (e.g., async/await, generics)
    pub language_factors: f64,
    /// Idiomatic patterns bonus/penalty
    pub idiom_score: f64,
    /// Framework/library usage complexity
    pub framework_complexity: f64,
}

/// Comprehensive language metrics
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct LanguageMetrics {
    /// Programming language
    pub language: AstLanguage,
    /// Lines of code
    pub lines_of_code: usize,
    /// Number of functions
    pub function_count: usize,
    /// Number of classes
    pub class_count: usize,
    /// Language-specific complexity
    pub complexity: LanguageSpecificComplexity,
    /// Estimated maintainability score
    pub maintainability_score: f64,
}

impl LanguageMetrics {
    /// Calculate language metrics for source code
    pub fn calculate(content: &amp;str, language: AstLanguage) -&gt; Result&lt;Self&gt; {
        let lines: Vec&lt;&amp;str&gt; = content.lines().collect();
        let lines_of_code = lines.len();

        // Basic pattern counting - can be enhanced with AST analysis
        let function_count = Self::count_functions(content, language);
        let class_count = Self::count_classes(content, language);

        let complexity = Self::calculate_language_complexity(content, language);
        let maintainability_score = Self::calculate_maintainability(
            lines_of_code,
            function_count,
            class_count,
            &amp;complexity,
        );

        Ok(Self {
            language,
            lines_of_code,
            function_count,
            class_count,
            complexity,
            maintainability_score,
        })
    }

    /// Count functions using language-specific patterns
    fn count_functions(content: &amp;str, language: AstLanguage) -&gt; usize {
        match language {
            AstLanguage::Python =&gt; content
                .lines()
                .filter(|line| {
                    line.trim().starts_with(&quot;def &quot;) || line.trim().starts_with(&quot;async def &quot;)
                })
                .count(),
            AstLanguage::JavaScript | AstLanguage::TypeScript =&gt; content
                .lines()
                .filter(|line| {
                    let trimmed = line.trim();
                    trimmed.starts_with(&quot;function &quot;)
                        || trimmed.contains(&quot;=&gt; &quot;)
                        || trimmed.contains(&quot;function(&quot;)
                })
                .count(),
            AstLanguage::Rust =&gt; content
                .lines()
                .filter(|line| line.trim().starts_with(&quot;fn &quot;) || line.trim().starts_with(&quot;pub fn &quot;))
                .count(),
            AstLanguage::Go =&gt; content
                .lines()
                .filter(|line| line.trim().starts_with(&quot;func &quot;))
                .count(),
            _ =&gt; 0,
        }
    }

    /// Count classes using language-specific patterns
    fn count_classes(content: &amp;str, language: AstLanguage) -&gt; usize {
        match language {
            AstLanguage::Python =&gt; content
                .lines()
                .filter(|line| line.trim().starts_with(&quot;class &quot;))
                .count(),
            AstLanguage::JavaScript | AstLanguage::TypeScript =&gt; content
                .lines()
                .filter(|line| line.trim().starts_with(&quot;class &quot;))
                .count(),
            AstLanguage::Rust =&gt; content
                .lines()
                .filter(|line| {
                    let trimmed = line.trim();
                    trimmed.starts_with(&quot;struct &quot;)
                        || trimmed.starts_with(&quot;pub struct &quot;)
                        || trimmed.starts_with(&quot;enum &quot;)
                        || trimmed.starts_with(&quot;pub enum &quot;)
                })
                .count(),
            AstLanguage::Go =&gt; content
                .lines()
                .filter(|line| line.trim().starts_with(&quot;type &quot;) &amp;&amp; line.contains(&quot;struct&quot;))
                .count(),
            _ =&gt; 0,
        }
    }

    /// Calculate language-specific complexity factors
    fn calculate_language_complexity(
        content: &amp;str,
        language: AstLanguage,
    ) -&gt; LanguageSpecificComplexity {
        let mut language_factors = 0.0;
        let mut idiom_score = 0.0;
        let mut framework_complexity = 0.0;

        match language {
            AstLanguage::Python =&gt; {
                // Python-specific complexity factors
                if content.contains(&quot;async def&quot;) || content.contains(&quot;await &quot;) {
                    language_factors += 0.3; // Async complexity
                }
                if content.contains(&quot;@&quot;) {
                    language_factors += 0.2; // Decorators
                }
                if content.contains(&quot;[&quot;) &amp;&amp; content.contains(&quot;for &quot;) &amp;&amp; content.contains(&quot;in &quot;) {
                    language_factors += 0.1; // List comprehensions
                }

                // Framework detection
                if content.contains(&quot;import django&quot;) || content.contains(&quot;from django&quot;) {
                    framework_complexity += 0.2;
                }
                if content.contains(&quot;import flask&quot;) || content.contains(&quot;from flask&quot;) {
                    framework_complexity += 0.1;
                }
            }

            AstLanguage::Rust =&gt; {
                // Rust-specific complexity factors
                if content.contains(&quot;&#x27;&quot;) &amp;&amp; content.contains(&quot;&amp;&quot;) {
                    language_factors += 0.4; // Lifetimes and borrowing
                }
                if content.contains(&quot;match &quot;) || content.contains(&quot;if let &quot;) {
                    language_factors += 0.1; // Pattern matching
                }
                if content.contains(&quot;macro_rules!&quot;) || content.contains(&quot;!&quot;) {
                    language_factors += 0.3; // Macros
                }

                // Idiomatic Rust patterns
                if content.contains(&quot;Result&lt;&quot;) || content.contains(&quot;Option&lt;&quot;) {
                    idiom_score += 0.2; // Good error handling
                }
            }

            AstLanguage::JavaScript | AstLanguage::TypeScript =&gt; {
                // JS/TS complexity factors
                if content.contains(&quot;async &quot;) || content.contains(&quot;await &quot;) {
                    language_factors += 0.2; // Async/await
                }
                if content.contains(&quot;Promise&quot;) {
                    language_factors += 0.1; // Promises
                }
                if language == AstLanguage::TypeScript {
                    if content.contains(&quot;&lt;&quot;) &amp;&amp; content.contains(&quot;&gt;&quot;) {
                        language_factors += 0.2; // Generics
                    }
                }

                // Framework detection
                if content.contains(&quot;import React&quot;) || content.contains(&quot;from &#x27;react&#x27;&quot;) {
                    framework_complexity += 0.1;
                }
            }

            AstLanguage::Go =&gt; {
                // Go-specific complexity factors
                if content.contains(&quot;go &quot;) &amp;&amp; content.contains(&quot;()&quot;) {
                    language_factors += 0.2; // Goroutines
                }
                if content.contains(&quot;chan &quot;) || content.contains(&quot;&lt;-&quot;) {
                    language_factors += 0.3; // Channels
                }
                if content.contains(&quot;defer &quot;) {
                    language_factors += 0.1; // Defer statements
                }
            }

            _ =&gt; {
                // Generic complexity assessment
                language_factors = 0.1;
            }
        }

        let base_complexity = 1.0; // Base complexity

        LanguageSpecificComplexity {
            base_complexity,
            language_factors,
            idiom_score,
            framework_complexity,
        }
    }

    /// Calculate maintainability score
    fn calculate_maintainability(
        lines_of_code: usize,
        function_count: usize,
        class_count: usize,
        complexity: &amp;LanguageSpecificComplexity,
    ) -&gt; f64 {
        let mut score = 100.0;

        // Penalize large files
        if lines_of_code &gt; 500 {
            score -= (lines_of_code as f64 - 500.0) * 0.01;
        }

        // Reward modular code
        if function_count &gt; 0 {
            let avg_lines_per_function = lines_of_code as f64 / function_count as f64;
            if avg_lines_per_function &lt; 20.0 {
                score += 5.0; // Small functions are good
            } else if avg_lines_per_function &gt; 100.0 {
                score -= 10.0; // Large functions are bad
            }
        }

        // Adjust for language complexity
        score -= complexity.language_factors * 10.0;
        score += complexity.idiom_score * 5.0;
        score -= complexity.framework_complexity * 5.0;

        score.max(0.0).min(100.0)
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn test_python_metrics() {
        let python_code = r#&quot;
def hello():
    print(&quot;Hello&quot;)

async def async_hello():
    await some_async_function()

class Calculator:
    def add(self, a, b):
        return a + b
&quot;#;

        let metrics = LanguageMetrics::calculate(python_code, AstLanguage::Python).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(metrics.language, AstLanguage::Python);
        assert!(metrics.function_count &gt;= 2);
        assert_eq!(metrics.class_count, 1);
        assert!(metrics.complexity.language_factors &gt; 0.0); // Should detect async
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_rust_metrics() {
        let rust_code = r#&quot;
fn main() {
    println!(&quot;Hello, world!&quot;);
}

struct Calculator {
    value: f64,
}

impl Calculator {
    fn new() -&gt; Self {
        Calculator { value: 0.0 }
    }
}
&quot;#;

        let metrics = LanguageMetrics::calculate(rust_code, AstLanguage::Rust).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(metrics.language, AstLanguage::Rust);
        assert!(metrics.function_count &gt;= 1);
        assert!(metrics.class_count &gt;= 1); // struct counts as class
    }
}

//! # Function and Class Extraction from AST
//!
//! Extracts function definitions, class definitions, and methods from source code
//! using tree-sitter AST parsing for accurate analysis.

use super::ast_language::AstLanguage;
use scribe_core::{Result, ScribeError};
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use tree_sitter::{Language, Node, Parser, Query, QueryCursor, Tree};

/// Information about a function extracted from source code
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct FunctionInfo {
    /// Function name
    pub name: String,
    /// Line number where function starts
    pub start_line: usize,
    /// Line number where function ends
    pub end_line: usize,
    /// Function parameters
    pub parameters: Vec&lt;String&gt;,
    /// Return type (if available)
    pub return_type: Option&lt;String&gt;,
    /// Documentation/docstring
    pub documentation: Option&lt;String&gt;,
    /// Function visibility (public, private, etc.)
    pub visibility: Option&lt;String&gt;,
    /// Whether this is a method (inside a class)
    pub is_method: bool,
    /// Parent class name (if this is a method)
    pub parent_class: Option&lt;String&gt;,
}

/// Information about a class extracted from source code
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct ClassInfo {
    /// Class name
    pub name: String,
    /// Line number where class starts
    pub start_line: usize,
    /// Line number where class ends
    pub end_line: usize,
    /// Parent classes/interfaces
    pub parents: Vec&lt;String&gt;,
    /// Documentation/docstring
    pub documentation: Option&lt;String&gt;,
    /// Class visibility
    pub visibility: Option&lt;String&gt;,
    /// Methods in this class
    pub methods: Vec&lt;FunctionInfo&gt;,
}

/// Extracts functions and classes from source code using tree-sitter
pub struct FunctionExtractor {
    language: AstLanguage,
    parser: Parser,
    function_query: Option&lt;Query&gt;,
    class_query: Option&lt;Query&gt;,
}

impl FunctionExtractor {
    /// Create a new function extractor for the given language
    pub fn new(language: AstLanguage) -&gt; Result&lt;Self&gt; {
        let mut parser = Parser::new();

        // Set up tree-sitter language if available
        let (function_query, class_query) =
            if let Some(ts_language) = language.tree_sitter_language() {
                parser
                    .set_language(ts_language)
                    .map_err(|e| ScribeError::Analysis {
                        message: format!(&quot;Failed to set tree-sitter language: {}&quot;, e),
                        source: None,
                        file: std::path::PathBuf::from(&quot;&lt;unknown&gt;&quot;),
                    })?;

                let function_query = Self::create_function_query(language, ts_language)?;
                let class_query = Self::create_class_query(language, ts_language)?;
                (function_query, class_query)
            } else {
                (None, None)
            };

        Ok(Self {
            language,
            parser,
            function_query,
            class_query,
        })
    }

    /// Create tree-sitter query for finding functions
    fn create_function_query(
        language: AstLanguage,
        ts_language: Language,
    ) -&gt; Result&lt;Option&lt;Query&gt;&gt; {
        let query_string = match language {
            AstLanguage::Python =&gt; {
                r#&quot;
                (function_definition) @function.definition
            &quot;#
            }
            AstLanguage::JavaScript | AstLanguage::TypeScript =&gt; {
                r#&quot;
                (function_declaration) @function.definition
                (method_definition) @function.definition
            &quot;#
            }
            AstLanguage::Rust =&gt; {
                r#&quot;
                (function_item) @function.definition
            &quot;#
            }
            AstLanguage::Go =&gt; {
                r#&quot;
                (function_declaration) @function.definition
                (method_declaration) @function.definition
            &quot;#
            }
            // Future languages - placeholder queries
            AstLanguage::Java =&gt; {
                r#&quot;
                (method_declaration) @function.definition
            &quot;#
            }
            AstLanguage::C | AstLanguage::Cpp =&gt; {
                r#&quot;
                (function_definition) @function.definition
            &quot;#
            }
            AstLanguage::Ruby =&gt; {
                r#&quot;
                (method) @function.definition
            &quot;#
            }
            AstLanguage::CSharp =&gt; {
                r#&quot;
                (method_declaration) @function.definition
            &quot;#
            }
            _ =&gt; return Ok(None),
        };

        Query::new(ts_language, query_string)
            .map(Some)
            .map_err(|e| ScribeError::Analysis {
                message: format!(&quot;Failed to create function query: {}&quot;, e),
                source: None,
                file: std::path::PathBuf::from(&quot;&lt;unknown&gt;&quot;),
            })
    }

    /// Create tree-sitter query for finding classes
    fn create_class_query(language: AstLanguage, ts_language: Language) -&gt; Result&lt;Option&lt;Query&gt;&gt; {
        let query_string = match language {
            AstLanguage::Python =&gt; {
                r#&quot;
                (class_definition) @class.definition
            &quot;#
            }
            AstLanguage::JavaScript | AstLanguage::TypeScript =&gt; {
                r#&quot;
                (class_declaration) @class.definition
            &quot;#
            }
            AstLanguage::Rust =&gt; {
                r#&quot;
                (struct_item) @class.definition
            &quot;#
            }
            AstLanguage::Go =&gt; {
                r#&quot;
                (type_declaration) @class.definition
            &quot;#
            }
            // Future languages - placeholder queries
            AstLanguage::Java =&gt; {
                r#&quot;
                (class_declaration) @class.definition
            &quot;#
            }
            AstLanguage::Cpp =&gt; {
                r#&quot;
                (class_specifier) @class.definition
            &quot;#
            }
            AstLanguage::Ruby =&gt; {
                r#&quot;
                (class) @class.definition
            &quot;#
            }
            AstLanguage::CSharp =&gt; {
                r#&quot;
                (class_declaration) @class.definition
            &quot;#
            }
            _ =&gt; return Ok(None),
        };

        Query::new(ts_language, query_string)
            .map(Some)
            .map_err(|e| ScribeError::Analysis {
                message: format!(&quot;Failed to create class query: {}&quot;, e),
                source: None,
                file: std::path::PathBuf::from(&quot;&lt;unknown&gt;&quot;),
            })
    }

    /// Extract all functions from source code
    pub fn extract_functions(&amp;mut self, content: &amp;str) -&gt; Result&lt;Vec&lt;FunctionInfo&gt;&gt; {
        let tree = self
            .parser
            .parse(content, None)
            .ok_or_else(|| ScribeError::Analysis {
                message: &quot;Failed to parse source code&quot;.to_string(),
                source: None,
                file: std::path::PathBuf::from(&quot;&lt;unknown&gt;&quot;),
            })?;

        let mut functions = Vec::new();

        if let Some(query) = &amp;self.function_query {
            let mut query_cursor = QueryCursor::new();
            let matches = query_cursor.matches(query, tree.root_node(), content.as_bytes());

            for query_match in matches {
                if let Some(function_info) =
                    self.extract_function_from_match(&amp;query_match, content, &amp;tree)?
                {
                    functions.push(function_info);
                }
            }
        }

        Ok(functions)
    }

    /// Extract all classes from source code
    pub fn extract_classes(&amp;mut self, content: &amp;str) -&gt; Result&lt;Vec&lt;ClassInfo&gt;&gt; {
        let tree = self
            .parser
            .parse(content, None)
            .ok_or_else(|| ScribeError::Analysis {
                message: &quot;Failed to parse source code&quot;.to_string(),
                source: None,
                file: std::path::PathBuf::from(&quot;&lt;unknown&gt;&quot;),
            })?;

        let mut classes = Vec::new();

        if let Some(query) = &amp;self.class_query {
            let mut query_cursor = QueryCursor::new();
            let matches = query_cursor.matches(query, tree.root_node(), content.as_bytes());

            for query_match in matches {
                if let Some(class_info) =
                    self.extract_class_from_match(&amp;query_match, content, &amp;tree)?
                {
                    classes.push(class_info);
                }
            }
        }

        Ok(classes)
    }

    /// Extract function information from a query match
    fn extract_function_from_match(
        &amp;self,
        query_match: &amp;tree_sitter::QueryMatch,
        content: &amp;str,
        tree: &amp;Tree,
    ) -&gt; Result&lt;Option&lt;FunctionInfo&gt;&gt; {
        for capture in query_match.captures {
            let node = capture.node;
            let start_line = node.start_position().row + 1;
            let end_line = node.end_position().row + 1;

            // Extract function name from the AST node structure
            let name = self.extract_function_name(node, content);
            let parameters = self.extract_function_parameters(node, content);

            if let Some(function_name) = name {
                return Ok(Some(FunctionInfo {
                    name: function_name,
                    start_line,
                    end_line,
                    parameters,
                    return_type: None,   // TODO: Extract return type
                    documentation: None, // TODO: Extract documentation
                    visibility: None,    // TODO: Extract visibility
                    is_method: false,    // TODO: Determine if method
                    parent_class: None,  // TODO: Find parent class
                }));
            }
        }
        Ok(None)
    }

    /// Extract class information from a query match
    fn extract_class_from_match(
        &amp;self,
        query_match: &amp;tree_sitter::QueryMatch,
        content: &amp;str,
        tree: &amp;Tree,
    ) -&gt; Result&lt;Option&lt;ClassInfo&gt;&gt; {
        for capture in query_match.captures {
            let node = capture.node;
            let start_line = node.start_position().row + 1;
            let end_line = node.end_position().row + 1;

            // Extract class name from the AST node structure
            let name = self.extract_class_name(node, content);
            let parents = self.extract_class_parents(node, content);

            if let Some(class_name) = name {
                return Ok(Some(ClassInfo {
                    name: class_name,
                    start_line,
                    end_line,
                    parents,
                    documentation: None, // TODO: Extract documentation
                    visibility: None,    // TODO: Extract visibility
                    methods: Vec::new(), // TODO: Extract methods
                }));
            }
        }
        Ok(None)
    }

    /// Extract function name from AST node
    fn extract_function_name(&amp;self, node: Node, content: &amp;str) -&gt; Option&lt;String&gt; {
        // Look for identifier child nodes that represent the function name
        let mut cursor = node.walk();
        cursor.goto_first_child();

        loop {
            let child = cursor.node();
            match child.kind() {
                &quot;identifier&quot; =&gt; {
                    if let Ok(name) = child.utf8_text(content.as_bytes()) {
                        return Some(name.to_string());
                    }
                }
                _ =&gt; {}
            }

            if !cursor.goto_next_sibling() {
                break;
            }
        }
        None
    }

    /// Extract function parameters from AST node
    fn extract_function_parameters(&amp;self, node: Node, content: &amp;str) -&gt; Vec&lt;String&gt; {
        let mut parameters = Vec::new();
        let mut cursor = node.walk();
        cursor.goto_first_child();

        loop {
            let child = cursor.node();
            match child.kind() {
                &quot;parameters&quot; | &quot;parameter_list&quot; =&gt; {
                    // Extract parameter names from parameter list
                    let mut param_cursor = child.walk();
                    param_cursor.goto_first_child();

                    loop {
                        let param_node = param_cursor.node();
                        if param_node.kind() == &quot;identifier&quot; {
                            if let Ok(param_name) = param_node.utf8_text(content.as_bytes()) {
                                if param_name != &quot;self&quot; {
                                    parameters.push(param_name.to_string());
                                }
                            }
                        }

                        if !param_cursor.goto_next_sibling() {
                            break;
                        }
                    }
                    break;
                }
                _ =&gt; {}
            }

            if !cursor.goto_next_sibling() {
                break;
            }
        }
        parameters
    }

    /// Extract class name from AST node
    fn extract_class_name(&amp;self, node: Node, content: &amp;str) -&gt; Option&lt;String&gt; {
        // Look for identifier child nodes that represent the class name
        let mut cursor = node.walk();
        cursor.goto_first_child();

        loop {
            let child = cursor.node();
            match child.kind() {
                &quot;identifier&quot; | &quot;type_identifier&quot; =&gt; {
                    if let Ok(name) = child.utf8_text(content.as_bytes()) {
                        return Some(name.to_string());
                    }
                }
                _ =&gt; {}
            }

            if !cursor.goto_next_sibling() {
                break;
            }
        }
        None
    }

    /// Extract class parent classes from AST node
    fn extract_class_parents(&amp;self, node: Node, content: &amp;str) -&gt; Vec&lt;String&gt; {
        let mut parents = Vec::new();
        let mut cursor = node.walk();
        cursor.goto_first_child();

        loop {
            let child = cursor.node();
            match child.kind() {
                &quot;argument_list&quot; | &quot;superclass&quot; | &quot;inheritance&quot; =&gt; {
                    // Extract parent class names
                    let mut parent_cursor = child.walk();
                    parent_cursor.goto_first_child();

                    loop {
                        let parent_node = parent_cursor.node();
                        if parent_node.kind() == &quot;identifier&quot;
                            || parent_node.kind() == &quot;type_identifier&quot;
                        {
                            if let Ok(parent_name) = parent_node.utf8_text(content.as_bytes()) {
                                parents.push(parent_name.to_string());
                            }
                        }

                        if !parent_cursor.goto_next_sibling() {
                            break;
                        }
                    }
                }
                _ =&gt; {}
            }

            if !cursor.goto_next_sibling() {
                break;
            }
        }
        parents
    }

    /// Extract parameter names from parameter list text
    fn extract_parameters(&amp;self, params_text: &amp;str, _node: Node) -&gt; Vec&lt;String&gt; {
        // Simple parameter extraction - can be improved per language
        params_text
            .split(&#x27;,&#x27;)
            .filter_map(|param| {
                let param = param.trim();
                if param.is_empty() || param == &quot;self&quot; {
                    None
                } else {
                    // Extract just the parameter name (before type annotations)
                    let name = param.split(&#x27;:&#x27;).next().unwrap_or(param).trim();
                    if name.is_empty() {
                        None
                    } else {
                        Some(name.to_string())
                    }
                }
            })
            .collect()
    }

    /// Extract parent class names from inheritance clause
    fn extract_parent_classes(&amp;self, parents_text: &amp;str) -&gt; Vec&lt;String&gt; {
        // Simple parent class extraction - can be improved per language
        parents_text
            .split(&#x27;,&#x27;)
            .filter_map(|parent| {
                let parent = parent.trim();
                if parent.is_empty() {
                    None
                } else {
                    Some(parent.to_string())
                }
            })
            .collect()
    }
}

impl AstLanguage {
    /// Get tree-sitter language for supported languages
    pub fn tree_sitter_language(&amp;self) -&gt; Option&lt;tree_sitter::Language&gt; {
        match self {
            AstLanguage::Python =&gt; Some(tree_sitter_python::language()),
            AstLanguage::JavaScript =&gt; Some(tree_sitter_javascript::language()),
            AstLanguage::TypeScript =&gt; Some(tree_sitter_typescript::language_typescript()),
            AstLanguage::Go =&gt; Some(tree_sitter_go::language()),
            AstLanguage::Rust =&gt; Some(tree_sitter_rust::language()),
            AstLanguage::Html =&gt; Some(tree_sitter_html::language()),
            // TODO: Add when dependencies are available
            // AstLanguage::Java =&gt; Some(tree_sitter_java::language()),
            // AstLanguage::C =&gt; Some(tree_sitter_c::language()),
            // AstLanguage::Cpp =&gt; Some(tree_sitter_cpp::language()),
            // AstLanguage::Ruby =&gt; Some(tree_sitter_ruby::language()),
            // AstLanguage::CSharp =&gt; Some(tree_sitter_c_sharp::language()),
            _ =&gt; None,
        }
    }
}

    #[test]

def hello_world():
    &quot;&quot;&quot;A simple function.&quot;&quot;&quot;

def add_numbers(a, b):
    &quot;&quot;&quot;Add two numbers together.&quot;&quot;&quot;

class Calculator:

&quot;#;

//! # Multi-Language AST Analysis Support
//!
//! This module provides comprehensive language support for AST-based analysis,
//! significantly expanding beyond the basic regex-based parsing. Implements
//! proper tree-sitter AST parsing for 20+ programming languages.
//!
//! ## Supported Languages
//!
//! ### Tier 1: Full AST Support (Tree-sitter)
//! - Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, Go, Rust (existing)
//! - Java, C#, C, C++, PHP, Ruby, Swift, Kotlin (to be added)
//!
//! ### Tier 2: Syntax-Aware Support (Tree-sitter)
//! - HTML, CSS, JSON, YAML, XML, Markdown
//! - SQL, Bash, PowerShell, Dockerfile
//!
//! ### Tier 3: Basic Structure Analysis (Regex + Heuristics)
//! - Scala, Dart, Perl, R, Julia, Elixir, Lua, Haskell
//!
//! ## Key Features
//!
//! - **Function/Class Extraction**: Identify all functions, classes, and methods
//! - **Documentation Coverage**: Analyze docstrings, comments, and documentation
//! - **Language-Specific Complexity**: Tailored complexity metrics per language
//! - **Import/Dependency Analysis**: Accurate dependency graph construction
//! - **Symbol Resolution**: Variable, function, and class usage tracking

pub mod ast_language;
pub mod documentation_analysis;
pub mod function_extraction;
pub mod language_metrics;
pub mod symbol_analysis;

pub use ast_language::{AstLanguage, LanguageFeatures, LanguageTier};
pub use documentation_analysis::{DocumentationAnalyzer, DocumentationCoverage};
pub use function_extraction::{ClassInfo, FunctionExtractor, FunctionInfo};
pub use language_metrics::{LanguageMetrics, LanguageSpecificComplexity};
pub use symbol_analysis::{SymbolAnalyzer, SymbolType, SymbolUsage};

use scribe_core::Result;
use std::collections::HashMap;

/// Main language support coordinator
pub struct LanguageSupport {
    /// Function extractors by language
    function_extractors: HashMap&lt;AstLanguage, FunctionExtractor&gt;,
    /// Documentation analyzers by language
    doc_analyzers: HashMap&lt;AstLanguage, DocumentationAnalyzer&gt;,
    /// Symbol analyzers by language
    symbol_analyzers: HashMap&lt;AstLanguage, SymbolAnalyzer&gt;,
}

impl LanguageSupport {
    /// Create a new language support system
    pub fn new() -&gt; Result&lt;Self&gt; {
        let mut support = Self {
            function_extractors: HashMap::new(),
            doc_analyzers: HashMap::new(),
            symbol_analyzers: HashMap::new(),
        };

        // Initialize extractors for all supported languages
        support.initialize_extractors()?;

        Ok(support)
    }

    /// Initialize extractors for all supported languages
    fn initialize_extractors(&amp;mut self) -&gt; Result&lt;()&gt; {
        for language in AstLanguage::all_supported() {
            self.function_extractors
                .insert(language, FunctionExtractor::new(language)?);
            self.doc_analyzers
                .insert(language, DocumentationAnalyzer::new(language)?);
            self.symbol_analyzers
                .insert(language, SymbolAnalyzer::new(language)?);
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Get language features and capabilities
    pub fn get_language_features(&amp;self, language: AstLanguage) -&gt; LanguageFeatures {
        language.features()
    }

    /// Extract all functions and classes from source code
    pub fn extract_functions(
        &amp;mut self,
        content: &amp;str,
        language: AstLanguage,
    ) -&gt; Result&lt;Vec&lt;FunctionInfo&gt;&gt; {
        if let Some(extractor) = self.function_extractors.get_mut(&amp;language) {
            extractor.extract_functions(content)
        } else {
            Ok(Vec::new())
        }
    }

    /// Analyze documentation coverage
    pub fn analyze_documentation(
        &amp;self,
        content: &amp;str,
        language: AstLanguage,
    ) -&gt; Result&lt;DocumentationCoverage&gt; {
        if let Some(analyzer) = self.doc_analyzers.get(&amp;language) {
            analyzer.analyze_coverage(content)
        } else {
            Ok(DocumentationCoverage::default())
        }
    }

    /// Analyze symbol usage patterns
    pub fn analyze_symbols(
        &amp;self,
        content: &amp;str,
        language: AstLanguage,
    ) -&gt; Result&lt;Vec&lt;SymbolUsage&gt;&gt; {
        if let Some(analyzer) = self.symbol_analyzers.get(&amp;language) {
            analyzer.analyze_symbols(content)
        } else {
            Ok(Vec::new())
        }
    }

    /// Get language-specific complexity metrics
    pub fn calculate_language_metrics(
        &amp;self,
        content: &amp;str,
        language: AstLanguage,
    ) -&gt; Result&lt;LanguageMetrics&gt; {
        LanguageMetrics::calculate(content, language)
    }

    /// Check if a language is supported
    pub fn is_supported(&amp;self, language: AstLanguage) -&gt; bool {
        self.function_extractors.contains_key(&amp;language)
    }

    /// Get all supported languages
    pub fn supported_languages(&amp;self) -&gt; Vec&lt;AstLanguage&gt; {
        self.function_extractors.keys().copied().collect()
    }
}

impl Default for LanguageSupport {
    fn default() -&gt; Self {
        Self::new().expect(&quot;Failed to create LanguageSupport&quot;)
    }
}

/// Comprehensive analysis result for a source file
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct LanguageAnalysisResult {
    /// Detected programming language
    pub language: AstLanguage,
    /// Language tier and capabilities
    pub tier: LanguageTier,
    /// Extracted functions and classes
    pub functions: Vec&lt;FunctionInfo&gt;,
    /// Documentation coverage analysis
    pub documentation: DocumentationCoverage,
    /// Symbol usage patterns
    pub symbols: Vec&lt;SymbolUsage&gt;,
    /// Language-specific metrics
    pub metrics: LanguageMetrics,
}

/// Main entry point for language analysis
pub fn analyze_file_language(
    content: &amp;str,
    file_extension: &amp;str,
    language_support: &amp;mut LanguageSupport,
) -&gt; Result&lt;Option&lt;LanguageAnalysisResult&gt;&gt; {
    let language = match AstLanguage::from_extension(file_extension) {
        Some(lang) =&gt; lang,
        None =&gt; return Ok(None),
    };

    if !language_support.is_supported(language) {
        return Ok(None);
    }

    let functions = language_support.extract_functions(content, language)?;
    let documentation = language_support.analyze_documentation(content, language)?;
    let symbols = language_support.analyze_symbols(content, language)?;
    let metrics = language_support.calculate_language_metrics(content, language)?;

    Ok(Some(LanguageAnalysisResult {
        language,
        tier: language.tier(),
        functions,
        documentation,
        symbols,
        metrics,
    }))
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn test_language_support_creation() {
        let support = LanguageSupport::new();
        if let Err(e) = &amp;support {
            println!(&quot;Error creating LanguageSupport: {:?}&quot;, e);
        }
        assert!(support.is_ok());
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_supported_languages() {
        let support = LanguageSupport::new().unwrap();
        let languages = support.supported_languages();

        // Should have at least the core languages
        assert!(languages.contains(&amp;AstLanguage::Python));
        assert!(languages.contains(&amp;AstLanguage::JavaScript));
        assert!(languages.contains(&amp;AstLanguage::Rust));
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_python_function_extraction() {
        let mut support = LanguageSupport::new().unwrap();
        let python_code = r#&quot;
def hello_world():
    &quot;&quot;&quot;A simple function.&quot;&quot;&quot;
    print(&quot;Hello, World!&quot;)

class Calculator:
    &quot;&quot;&quot;A simple calculator class.&quot;&quot;&quot;
    
    def add(self, a, b):
        &quot;&quot;&quot;Add two numbers.&quot;&quot;&quot;
        return a + b
&quot;#;

        let functions = support.extract_functions(python_code, AstLanguage::Python);
        assert!(functions.is_ok());
        let functions = functions.unwrap();
        assert!(!functions.is_empty());
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_language_analysis() {
        let mut support = LanguageSupport::new().unwrap();
        let result = analyze_file_language(&quot;def test(): pass&quot;, &quot;py&quot;, &amp;mut support);

        assert!(result.is_ok());
        let result = result.unwrap();
        assert!(result.is_some());
        assert_eq!(result.unwrap().language, AstLanguage::Python);
    }
}

//! # Symbol Usage Analysis
//!
//! Analyzes symbol usage patterns, variable definitions, and cross-references
//! within source code files.

use super::ast_language::AstLanguage;
use scribe_core::Result;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};

/// Type of symbol
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum SymbolType {
    Variable,
    Function,
    Class,
    Module,
    Constant,
    Type,
}

/// Symbol usage information
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct SymbolUsage {
    /// Symbol name
    pub name: String,
    /// Symbol type
    pub symbol_type: SymbolType,
    /// Line where symbol is defined
    pub definition_line: Option&lt;usize&gt;,
    /// Lines where symbol is used
    pub usage_lines: Vec&lt;usize&gt;,
    /// Scope where symbol is defined
    pub scope: Option&lt;String&gt;,
}

/// Symbol analyzer for source code
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct SymbolAnalyzer {
    language: AstLanguage,
}

impl SymbolAnalyzer {
    /// Create a new symbol analyzer
    pub fn new(language: AstLanguage) -&gt; Result&lt;Self&gt; {
        Ok(Self { language })
    }
