//! # Code Parsing Infrastructure
//!
//! Placeholder module for language-specific parsers.

use crate::ast::AstNode;
use scribe_core::Result;

/// Simple character-based tokenizer without regex
struct SimpleTokenizer {
    input: Vec&lt;char&gt;,
    position: usize,
}

impl SimpleTokenizer {
    fn new(input: &amp;str) -&gt; Self {
        Self {
            input: input.chars().collect(),
            position: 0,
        }
    }

    fn is_at_end(&amp;self) -&gt; bool {
        self.position &gt;= self.input.len()
    }

    fn advance(&amp;mut self) {
        if !self.is_at_end() {
            self.position += 1;
        }
    }

    fn peek_char(&amp;self) -&gt; Option&lt;char&gt; {
        self.input.get(self.position).copied()
    }

    fn peek_ahead(&amp;self, offset: usize) -&gt; Option&lt;char&gt; {
        self.input.get(self.position + offset).copied()
    }

    fn current_char(&amp;self) -&gt; Option&lt;char&gt; {
        self.input.get(self.position).copied()
    }

    fn skip_whitespace(&amp;mut self) {
        while !self.is_at_end() {
            match self.current_char() {
                Some(&#x27; &#x27;) | Some(&#x27;\t&#x27;) | Some(&#x27;\r&#x27;) =&gt; self.advance(),
                _ =&gt; break,
            }
        }
    }

    fn skip_line(&amp;mut self) {
        while !self.is_at_end() {
            if self.current_char() == Some(&#x27;\n&#x27;) {
                self.advance();
                break;
            }
            self.advance();
        }
    }

    fn peek_word(&amp;self, word: &amp;str) -&gt; bool {
        let word_chars: Vec&lt;char&gt; = word.chars().collect();

        if self.position + word_chars.len() &gt; self.input.len() {
            return false;
        }

        // Check if characters match
        for (i, &amp;expected_char) in word_chars.iter().enumerate() {
            if let Some(actual_char) = self.input.get(self.position + i) {
                if *actual_char != expected_char {
                    return false;
                }
            } else {
                return false;
            }
        }

        // Check that it&#x27;s a complete word (not part of a larger identifier)
        if let Some(next_char) = self.input.get(self.position + word_chars.len()) {
            if next_char.is_alphanumeric() || *next_char == &#x27;_&#x27; {
                return false;
            }
        }

        true
    }

    fn consume_word(&amp;mut self, word: &amp;str) -&gt; Result&lt;()&gt; {
        if self.peek_word(word) {
            self.position += word.chars().count();
            Ok(())
        } else {
            Err(scribe_core::ScribeError::parse(&amp;format!(
                &quot;Expected &#x27;{}&#x27;&quot;,
                word
            )))
        }
    }

    fn next(&amp;mut self) -&gt; Option&lt;String&gt; {
        self.skip_whitespace();

        if self.is_at_end() {
            return None;
        }

        let mut token = String::new();

        // Collect alphanumeric characters and underscores
        while !self.is_at_end() {
            let ch = self.current_char().unwrap();
            if ch.is_alphanumeric() || ch == &#x27;_&#x27; {
                token.push(ch);
                self.advance();
            } else {
                break;
            }
        }

        if token.is_empty() {
            // Single character token
            if let Some(ch) = self.current_char() {
                token.push(ch);
                self.advance();
            }
        }

        if token.is_empty() {
            None
        } else {
            Some(token)
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct ParseResult {
    pub ast: AstNode,
    pub errors: Vec&lt;String&gt;,
}

impl ParseResult {
    pub fn new(ast: AstNode) -&gt; Self {
        Self {
            ast,
            errors: Vec::new(),
        }
    }

    pub fn with_errors(mut self, errors: Vec&lt;String&gt;) -&gt; Self {
        self.errors = errors;
        self
    }
}

pub struct Parser;

impl Parser {
    pub fn new() -&gt; Result&lt;Self&gt; {
        Ok(Self)
    }

    // Helper function to create nodes with children
    fn create_node_with_children(node_type: &amp;str, children: Vec&lt;AstNode&gt;) -&gt; AstNode {
        let mut node = AstNode::new(node_type.to_string());
        for child in children {
            node = node.add_child(child);
        }
        node
    }

    pub fn parse(&amp;self, code: &amp;str, language: &amp;str) -&gt; Result&lt;AstNode&gt; {
        let mut tokenizer = SimpleTokenizer::new(code);

        match language.to_lowercase().as_str() {
            &quot;rust&quot; | &quot;rs&quot; =&gt; self.parse_rust(&amp;mut tokenizer),
            &quot;python&quot; | &quot;py&quot; =&gt; self.parse_python(&amp;mut tokenizer),
            &quot;javascript&quot; | &quot;js&quot; | &quot;typescript&quot; | &quot;ts&quot; =&gt; self.parse_javascript(&amp;mut tokenizer),
            _ =&gt; self.parse_generic(&amp;mut tokenizer),
        }
    }

    fn parse_rust(&amp;self, tokenizer: &amp;mut SimpleTokenizer) -&gt; Result&lt;AstNode&gt; {
        let mut statements = Vec::new();

        while !tokenizer.is_at_end() {
            if let Some(stmt) = self.parse_statement(tokenizer)? {
                statements.push(stmt);
            }
        }

        Ok(Self::create_node_with_children(&quot;block&quot;, statements))
    }

    fn parse_python(&amp;self, tokenizer: &amp;mut SimpleTokenizer) -&gt; Result&lt;AstNode&gt; {
        // Simple Python parsing - detect basic structures
        let mut statements = Vec::new();

        while !tokenizer.is_at_end() {
            if let Some(stmt) = self.parse_python_statement(tokenizer)? {
                statements.push(stmt);
            }
        }

        Ok(Self::create_node_with_children(&quot;block&quot;, statements))
    }

    fn parse_javascript(&amp;self, tokenizer: &amp;mut SimpleTokenizer) -&gt; Result&lt;AstNode&gt; {
        // Simple JavaScript parsing
        let mut statements = Vec::new();

        while !tokenizer.is_at_end() {
            if let Some(stmt) = self.parse_js_statement(tokenizer)? {
                statements.push(stmt);
            }
        }

        Ok(Self::create_node_with_children(&quot;block&quot;, statements))
    }

    fn parse_generic(&amp;self, tokenizer: &amp;mut SimpleTokenizer) -&gt; Result&lt;AstNode&gt; {
        // Generic parsing - just count basic structures
        let mut statements = Vec::new();

        while !tokenizer.is_at_end() {
            if let Some(token) = tokenizer.next() {
                statements.push(AstNode::new(token));
            }
        }

        Ok(Self::create_node_with_children(&quot;block&quot;, statements))
    }

    fn parse_statement(&amp;self, tokenizer: &amp;mut SimpleTokenizer) -&gt; Result&lt;Option&lt;AstNode&gt;&gt; {
        tokenizer.skip_whitespace();

        if tokenizer.is_at_end() {
            return Ok(None);
        }

        // Look for common keywords
        if tokenizer.peek_word(&quot;if&quot;) {
            return Ok(Some(self.parse_if_statement(tokenizer)?));
        }

        if tokenizer.peek_word(&quot;while&quot;) {
            return Ok(Some(self.parse_while_statement(tokenizer)?));
        }

        if tokenizer.peek_word(&quot;for&quot;) {
            return Ok(Some(self.parse_for_statement(tokenizer)?));
        }

        if tokenizer.peek_word(&quot;match&quot;) {
            return Ok(Some(self.parse_match_statement(tokenizer)?));
        }

        // Skip to next line for other statements
        tokenizer.skip_line();
        Ok(Some(AstNode::new(&quot;statement&quot;.to_string())))
    }

    fn parse_python_statement(&amp;self, tokenizer: &amp;mut SimpleTokenizer) -&gt; Result&lt;Option&lt;AstNode&gt;&gt; {
        tokenizer.skip_whitespace();

        if tokenizer.is_at_end() {
            return Ok(None);
        }

        if tokenizer.peek_word(&quot;if&quot;) {
            return Ok(Some(self.parse_python_if(tokenizer)?));
        }

        if tokenizer.peek_word(&quot;while&quot;) {
            return Ok(Some(self.parse_python_while(tokenizer)?));
        }

        if tokenizer.peek_word(&quot;for&quot;) {
            return Ok(Some(self.parse_python_for(tokenizer)?));
        }

        tokenizer.skip_line();
        Ok(Some(AstNode::new(&quot;statement&quot;.to_string())))
    }

    fn parse_js_statement(&amp;self, tokenizer: &amp;mut SimpleTokenizer) -&gt; Result&lt;Option&lt;AstNode&gt;&gt; {
        tokenizer.skip_whitespace();

        if tokenizer.is_at_end() {
            return Ok(None);
        }

        if tokenizer.peek_word(&quot;if&quot;) {
            return Ok(Some(self.parse_js_if(tokenizer)?));
        }

        if tokenizer.peek_word(&quot;while&quot;) {
            return Ok(Some(self.parse_js_while(tokenizer)?));
        }

        if tokenizer.peek_word(&quot;for&quot;) {
            return Ok(Some(self.parse_js_for(tokenizer)?));
        }

        if tokenizer.peek_word(&quot;switch&quot;) {
            return Ok(Some(self.parse_js_switch(tokenizer)?));
        }

        tokenizer.skip_line();
        Ok(Some(AstNode::new(&quot;statement&quot;.to_string())))
    }

    fn parse_if_statement(&amp;self, tokenizer: &amp;mut SimpleTokenizer) -&gt; Result&lt;AstNode&gt; {
        tokenizer.consume_word(&quot;if&quot;)?;
        let _condition = self.parse_condition(tokenizer)?;
        let then_branch = self.parse_block(tokenizer)?;

        let mut children = vec![then_branch];

        if tokenizer.peek_word(&quot;else&quot;) {
            tokenizer.consume_word(&quot;else&quot;)?;
            let else_branch = self.parse_block(tokenizer)?;
            children.push(else_branch);
        }

        Ok(Self::create_node_with_children(&quot;if&quot;, children))
    }

    fn parse_while_statement(&amp;self, tokenizer: &amp;mut SimpleTokenizer) -&gt; Result&lt;AstNode&gt; {
        tokenizer.consume_word(&quot;while&quot;)?;
        let _condition = self.parse_condition(tokenizer)?;
        let body = self.parse_block(tokenizer)?;

        Ok(Self::create_node_with_children(&quot;while&quot;, vec![body]))
    }

    fn parse_for_statement(&amp;self, tokenizer: &amp;mut SimpleTokenizer) -&gt; Result&lt;AstNode&gt; {
        tokenizer.consume_word(&quot;for&quot;)?;

        // Simplified for loop parsing
        let _init = &quot;init&quot;.to_string();
        let _condition = &quot;condition&quot;.to_string();
        let _update = &quot;update&quot;.to_string();
        let body = self.parse_block(tokenizer)?;

        Ok(Self::create_node_with_children(&quot;for&quot;, vec![body]))
    }

    fn parse_match_statement(&amp;self, tokenizer: &amp;mut SimpleTokenizer) -&gt; Result&lt;AstNode&gt; {
        tokenizer.consume_word(&quot;match&quot;)?;
        let _condition = self.parse_condition(tokenizer)?;

        // Simplified match parsing - just count arms
        let mut cases = Vec::new();

        // Skip to opening brace and count patterns
        while !tokenizer.is_at_end() &amp;&amp; tokenizer.current_char() != Some(&#x27;}&#x27;) {
            if tokenizer.current_char() == Some(&#x27;=&#x27;) &amp;&amp; tokenizer.peek_ahead(1) == Some(&#x27;&gt;&#x27;) {
                cases.push(AstNode::new(&quot;match_arm&quot;.to_string()));
            }
            tokenizer.advance();
        }

        Ok(Self::create_node_with_children(&quot;match&quot;, cases))
    }

    fn parse_python_if(&amp;self, tokenizer: &amp;mut SimpleTokenizer) -&gt; Result&lt;AstNode&gt; {
        tokenizer.consume_word(&quot;if&quot;)?;
        let condition = self.parse_condition(tokenizer)?;
        let then_branch = Box::new(self.parse_python_block(tokenizer)?);

        let else_branch = if tokenizer.peek_word(&quot;else&quot;) {
            tokenizer.consume_word(&quot;else&quot;)?;
            Some(Box::new(self.parse_python_block(tokenizer)?))
        } else {
            None
        };

        Ok(Self::create_node_with_children(&quot;if&quot;, vec![*then_branch]))
    }

    fn parse_python_while(&amp;self, tokenizer: &amp;mut SimpleTokenizer) -&gt; Result&lt;AstNode&gt; {
        tokenizer.consume_word(&quot;while&quot;)?;
        let condition = self.parse_condition(tokenizer)?;
        let body = Box::new(self.parse_python_block(tokenizer)?);

        Ok(Self::create_node_with_children(&quot;while&quot;, vec![*body]))
    }

    fn parse_python_for(&amp;self, tokenizer: &amp;mut SimpleTokenizer) -&gt; Result&lt;AstNode&gt; {
        tokenizer.consume_word(&quot;for&quot;)?;

        let init = &quot;for_init&quot;.to_string();
        let condition = &quot;for_condition&quot;.to_string();
        let update = &quot;for_update&quot;.to_string();
        let body = Box::new(self.parse_python_block(tokenizer)?);

        Ok(Self::create_node_with_children(&quot;for&quot;, vec![*body]))
    }

    fn parse_js_if(&amp;self, tokenizer: &amp;mut SimpleTokenizer) -&gt; Result&lt;AstNode&gt; {
        tokenizer.consume_word(&quot;if&quot;)?;
        let condition = self.parse_condition(tokenizer)?;
        let then_branch = Box::new(self.parse_js_block(tokenizer)?);

        let else_branch = if tokenizer.peek_word(&quot;else&quot;) {
            tokenizer.consume_word(&quot;else&quot;)?;
            Some(Box::new(self.parse_js_block(tokenizer)?))
        } else {
            None
        };

        Ok(Self::create_node_with_children(&quot;if&quot;, vec![*then_branch]))
    }

    fn parse_js_while(&amp;self, tokenizer: &amp;mut SimpleTokenizer) -&gt; Result&lt;AstNode&gt; {
        tokenizer.consume_word(&quot;while&quot;)?;
        let condition = self.parse_condition(tokenizer)?;
        let body = Box::new(self.parse_js_block(tokenizer)?);

        Ok(Self::create_node_with_children(&quot;while&quot;, vec![*body]))
    }

    fn parse_js_for(&amp;self, tokenizer: &amp;mut SimpleTokenizer) -&gt; Result&lt;AstNode&gt; {
        tokenizer.consume_word(&quot;for&quot;)?;

        let init = &quot;for_init&quot;.to_string();
        let condition = &quot;for_condition&quot;.to_string();
        let update = &quot;for_update&quot;.to_string();
        let body = Box::new(self.parse_js_block(tokenizer)?);

        Ok(Self::create_node_with_children(&quot;for&quot;, vec![*body]))
    }

    fn parse_js_switch(&amp;self, tokenizer: &amp;mut SimpleTokenizer) -&gt; Result&lt;AstNode&gt; {
        tokenizer.consume_word(&quot;switch&quot;)?;
        let condition = self.parse_condition(tokenizer)?;

        let mut cases = Vec::new();

        // Count case statements
        while !tokenizer.is_at_end() {
            if tokenizer.peek_word(&quot;case&quot;) || tokenizer.peek_word(&quot;default&quot;) {
                cases.push(AstNode::new(&quot;case&quot;.to_string()));
            }
            tokenizer.advance();
        }

        Ok(Self::create_node_with_children(&quot;switch&quot;, cases))
    }

    fn parse_condition(&amp;self, tokenizer: &amp;mut SimpleTokenizer) -&gt; Result&lt;String&gt; {
        // Simple condition parsing - just collect until we hit a delimiter
        let mut condition = String::new();

        tokenizer.skip_whitespace();

        while !tokenizer.is_at_end() {
            let ch = tokenizer.peek_char().unwrap_or(&#x27; &#x27;);
            if ch == &#x27;{&#x27; || ch == &#x27;:&#x27; || ch == &#x27;\n&#x27; {
                break;
            }
            condition.push(ch);
            tokenizer.advance();
        }

        Ok(condition.trim().to_string())
    }

    fn parse_block(&amp;self, tokenizer: &amp;mut SimpleTokenizer) -&gt; Result&lt;AstNode&gt; {
        let mut statements = Vec::new();

        // Look for opening brace
        tokenizer.skip_whitespace();
        if tokenizer.peek_char() == Some(&#x27;{&#x27;) {
            tokenizer.advance(); // consume &#x27;{&#x27;

            let mut brace_count = 1;
            while !tokenizer.is_at_end() &amp;&amp; brace_count &gt; 0 {
                if tokenizer.peek_char() == Some(&#x27;{&#x27;) {
                    brace_count += 1;
                } else if tokenizer.peek_char() == Some(&#x27;}&#x27;) {
                    brace_count -= 1;
                }

                if brace_count &gt; 0 {
                    if let Some(stmt) = self.parse_statement(tokenizer)? {
                        statements.push(stmt);
                    }
                } else {
                    tokenizer.advance(); // consume &#x27;}&#x27;
                }
            }
        }

        Ok(Self::create_node_with_children(&quot;block&quot;, statements))
    }

    fn parse_python_block(&amp;self, tokenizer: &amp;mut SimpleTokenizer) -&gt; Result&lt;AstNode&gt; {
        let mut statements = Vec::new();

        // Python uses indentation
        tokenizer.skip_line(); // Skip to next line

        // For simplicity, just parse a few lines
        for _ in 0..5 {
            if tokenizer.is_at_end() {
                break;
            }
            if let Some(stmt) = self.parse_python_statement(tokenizer)? {
                statements.push(stmt);
            }
        }

        Ok(Self::create_node_with_children(&quot;block&quot;, statements))
    }

    fn parse_js_block(&amp;self, tokenizer: &amp;mut SimpleTokenizer) -&gt; Result&lt;AstNode&gt; {
        // JavaScript blocks are similar to Rust
        self.parse_block(tokenizer)
    }
}

impl Default for Parser {
    fn default() -&gt; Self {
        Self::new().expect(&quot;Failed to create Parser&quot;)
    }
}

use criterion::{black_box, criterion_group, criterion_main, Criterion};
use scribe_core::*;
use std::path::PathBuf;

fn benchmark_language_detection(c: &amp;mut Criterion) {
    let extensions = vec![&quot;rs&quot;, &quot;py&quot;, &quot;js&quot;, &quot;ts&quot;, &quot;go&quot;, &quot;java&quot;, &quot;cpp&quot;];

    c.bench_function(&quot;language_detection&quot;, |b| {
        b.iter(|| {
            for ext in &amp;extensions {
                black_box(Language::from_extension(ext));
            }
        })
    });
}

fn benchmark_path_normalization(c: &amp;mut Criterion) {
    let paths = vec![
        &quot;src/lib.rs&quot;,
        &quot;src\\windows\\path.rs&quot;,
        &quot;deeply/nested/directory/structure/file.rs&quot;,
        &quot;C:\\Windows\\System32\\file.exe&quot;,
    ];

    c.bench_function(&quot;path_normalization&quot;, |b| {
        b.iter(|| {
            for path in &amp;paths {
                black_box(normalize_path(path));
            }
        })
    });
}

fn benchmark_string_truncation(c: &amp;mut Criterion) {
    let strings = vec![
        &quot;short&quot;,
        &quot;this is a medium length string that might need truncation&quot;,
        &quot;this is a very long string that definitely needs to be truncated because it exceeds the maximum allowed length for display purposes in most contexts&quot;,
    ];

    c.bench_function(&quot;string_truncation&quot;, |b| {
        b.iter(|| {
            for s in &amp;strings {
                black_box(truncate(s, 50));
            }
        })
    });
}

pub const BINARY_EXTENSIONS: &amp;[&amp;str] = &amp;[
    // Images
    &quot;.png&quot;, &quot;.jpg&quot;, &quot;.jpeg&quot;, &quot;.gif&quot;, &quot;.webp&quot;, &quot;.bmp&quot;, &quot;.svg&quot;, &quot;.ico&quot;, &quot;.tiff&quot;,
    // Documents
    &quot;.pdf&quot;, &quot;.doc&quot;, &quot;.docx&quot;, &quot;.ppt&quot;, &quot;.pptx&quot;, &quot;.xls&quot;, &quot;.xlsx&quot;, // Archives
    &quot;.zip&quot;, &quot;.tar&quot;, &quot;.gz&quot;, &quot;.bz2&quot;, &quot;.xz&quot;, &quot;.7z&quot;, &quot;.rar&quot;, // Media
    &quot;.mp3&quot;, &quot;.mp4&quot;, &quot;.mov&quot;, &quot;.avi&quot;, &quot;.mkv&quot;, &quot;.wav&quot;, &quot;.ogg&quot;, &quot;.flac&quot;, // Fonts

/// Markdown file extensions
pub const MARKDOWN_EXTENSIONS: &amp;[&amp;str] = &amp;[&quot;.md&quot;, &quot;.markdown&quot;, &quot;.mdown&quot;, &quot;.mkd&quot;, &quot;.mkdn&quot;];

/// Decision about whether to include a file in analysis
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct RenderDecision {
    /// Whether to include the file in analysis
    pub include: bool,
    /// Human-readable reason for the decision
    pub reason: String,
    /// Optional additional context
    pub context: Option&lt;String&gt;,
}

impl RenderDecision {
    /// Create a decision to include the file
    pub fn include&lt;S: Into&lt;String&gt;&gt;(reason: S) -&gt; Self {
        Self {
            include: true,
            reason: reason.into(),
            context: None,
        }
    }

    /// Create a decision to exclude the file
    pub fn exclude&lt;S: Into&lt;String&gt;&gt;(reason: S) -&gt; Self {
        Self {
            include: false,
            reason: reason.into(),
            context: None,
        }
    }

    /// Add context to the decision
    pub fn with_context&lt;S: Into&lt;String&gt;&gt;(mut self, context: S) -&gt; Self {
        self.context = Some(context.into());
        self
    }

    /// Check if the file should be included
    pub fn should_include(&amp;self) -&gt; bool {
        self.include
    }

    /// Get the reason as a standard category
    pub fn reason_category(&amp;self) -&gt; RenderDecisionCategory {
        match self.reason.as_str() {
            &quot;ok&quot; =&gt; RenderDecisionCategory::Ok,
            &quot;binary&quot; =&gt; RenderDecisionCategory::Binary,
            &quot;too_large&quot; =&gt; RenderDecisionCategory::TooLarge,
            &quot;ignored&quot; =&gt; RenderDecisionCategory::Ignored,
            &quot;empty&quot; =&gt; RenderDecisionCategory::Empty,
            _ =&gt; RenderDecisionCategory::Other,
        }
    }
}

/// Standard categories for render decisions
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum RenderDecisionCategory {
    Ok,
    Binary,
    TooLarge,
    Ignored,
    Empty,
    Other,
}

/// Programming language classification

pub enum Language {

impl Language {
    /// Detect language from file extension
    pub fn from_extension(ext: &amp;str) -&gt; Self {
        match ext.to_lowercase().as_str() {
            &quot;rs&quot; =&gt; Language::Rust,
            &quot;c&quot; | &quot;h&quot; =&gt; Language::C,
            &quot;cpp&quot; | &quot;cxx&quot; | &quot;cc&quot; | &quot;hpp&quot; | &quot;hxx&quot; =&gt; Language::Cpp,
            &quot;go&quot; =&gt; Language::Go,

            &quot;fs&quot; | &quot;fsi&quot; | &quot;fsx&quot; =&gt; Language::FSharp,
            &quot;erl&quot; | &quot;hrl&quot; =&gt; Language::Erlang,
            &quot;ex&quot; | &quot;exs&quot; =&gt; Language::Elixir,
            &quot;clj&quot; | &quot;cljs&quot; | &quot;cljc&quot; =&gt; Language::Clojure,

            &quot;yaml&quot; | &quot;yml&quot; =&gt; Language::YAML,
            &quot;toml&quot; =&gt; Language::TOML,

            &quot;md&quot; | &quot;markdown&quot; | &quot;mdown&quot; | &quot;mkd&quot; | &quot;mkdn&quot; =&gt; Language::Markdown,
            &quot;sql&quot; =&gt; Language::SQL,
            &quot;sh&quot; | &quot;bash&quot; =&gt; Language::Bash,
            &quot;ps1&quot; | &quot;psm1&quot; | &quot;psd1&quot; =&gt; Language::PowerShell,

            // Handle ambiguous .m extension - could be Matlab or Objective-C
            // Default to Objective-C as it&#x27;s more common in modern development
            &quot;m&quot; | &quot;mm&quot; =&gt; Language::ObjectiveC,
            _ =&gt; Language::Unknown,
        }
    }

    /// Check if this language is typically used for documentation
    pub fn is_documentation(&amp;self) -&gt; bool {
        matches!(self, Language::Markdown | Language::HTML)
    }

    pub fn is_configuration(&amp;self) -&gt; bool {
        matches!(

/// File type classification for analysis purposes
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum FileType {
    /// Source code files
    Source { language: Language },
    /// Documentation files
    Documentation { format: DocumentationFormat },
    /// Configuration files
    Configuration { format: ConfigurationFormat },
    /// Test files
    Test { language: Language },
    /// Binary files that should be excluded
    Binary,
    /// Generated or built files
    Generated,
    /// Unknown or unclassified
    Unknown,
}

/// Documentation format classification
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum DocumentationFormat {
    Markdown,
    Html,
    PlainText,
    Rst,
    Asciidoc,
}

/// Configuration format classification
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum ConfigurationFormat {
    Json,
    Yaml,
    Toml,
    Xml,
    Ini,
    Dotenv,
}

/// Comprehensive file metadata structure
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct FileInfo {
    /// Absolute path to the file on disk
    pub path: PathBuf,

    /// Path relative to repository root (forward slash separated)
    pub relative_path: String,

    /// File size in bytes
    pub size: u64,

    /// File modification time
    pub modified: Option&lt;SystemTime&gt;,

    /// Analysis decision (include/exclude)
    pub decision: RenderDecision,

    /// Detected file type
    pub file_type: FileType,

    /// Detected programming language
    pub language: Language,

    /// File content (loaded on demand)
    pub content: Option&lt;String&gt;,

    /// Estimated token count for LLM processing
    pub token_estimate: Option&lt;usize&gt;,

    /// Line count (if text file)
    pub line_count: Option&lt;usize&gt;,

    /// Character count (if text file)
    pub char_count: Option&lt;usize&gt;,

    /// Whether the file is likely binary
    pub is_binary: bool,

    /// Git status information (if available)
    pub git_status: Option&lt;GitStatus&gt;,

    /// PageRank centrality score (0.0-1.0, higher means more important)
    pub centrality_score: Option&lt;f64&gt;,
}

/// Git status information for a file
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct GitStatus {
    /// Working tree status
    pub working_tree: GitFileStatus,
    /// Index/staging area status
    pub index: GitFileStatus,
}

/// Git file status
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum GitFileStatus {
    Unmodified,
    Modified,
    Added,
    Deleted,
    Renamed,
    Copied,
    Unmerged,
    Untracked,
    Ignored,
}

impl FileInfo {
    /// Create a new FileInfo from a path
    pub fn new&lt;P: AsRef&lt;Path&gt;&gt;(
        path: P,
        relative_path: String,
        decision: RenderDecision,
    ) -&gt; Result&lt;Self&gt; {
        let path = path.as_ref();
        let metadata = std::fs::metadata(path)
            .map_err(|e| ScribeError::path_with_source(&quot;Failed to read file metadata&quot;, path, e))?;

        let size = metadata.len();
        let modified = metadata.modified().ok();

        let extension = path.extension().and_then(|ext| ext.to_str()).unwrap_or(&quot;&quot;);

        let language = Language::from_extension(extension);
        let is_binary = Self::detect_binary_by_extension(extension);
        let file_type = Self::classify_file_type(&amp;relative_path, &amp;language, extension);

        Ok(Self {
            path: path.to_path_buf(),
            relative_path,
            size,
            modified,
            decision,
            file_type,
            language,
            content: None,
            token_estimate: None,
            line_count: None,
            char_count: None,
            is_binary,
            git_status: None,
            centrality_score: None,
        })
    }

    /// Load file content and compute statistics
    pub fn load_content(&amp;mut self) -&gt; Result&lt;()&gt; {
        if self.is_binary || !self.decision.should_include() {
            return Ok(());
        }

        let content = std::fs::read_to_string(&amp;self.path).map_err(|e| {
            ScribeError::analysis(format!(&quot;Failed to read file content: {}&quot;, e), &amp;self.path)
        })?;

        // Compute statistics
        let line_count = content.lines().count();
        let char_count = content.chars().count();
        let token_estimate = Self::estimate_tokens(&amp;content);

        self.content = Some(content);
        self.line_count = Some(line_count);
        self.char_count = Some(char_count);
        self.token_estimate = Some(token_estimate);

        Ok(())
    }

    /// Estimate token count for LLM processing using tiktoken
    ///
    /// This method uses the shared global TokenCounter instance for optimal performance.
    /// If tiktoken fails, it falls back to the legacy character-based estimation.
    pub fn estimate_tokens(content: &amp;str) -&gt; usize {
        use crate::tokenization::{utils, TokenCounter};

        // Use the shared global instance for optimal performance
        match TokenCounter::global().count_tokens(content) {
            Ok(tokens) =&gt; tokens,
            Err(_) =&gt; {
                // Fall back to legacy estimation if tiktoken fails
                utils::estimate_tokens_legacy(content)
            }
        }
    }

    /// Estimate token count for LLM processing with file context
    ///
    /// This method uses the file path to apply language-specific multipliers
    /// for more accurate token estimation.
    pub fn estimate_tokens_with_path(content: &amp;str, file_path: &amp;std::path::Path) -&gt; usize {
        use crate::tokenization::TokenCounter;

        // Use the shared global instance for optimal performance
        match TokenCounter::global().estimate_file_tokens(content, file_path) {
            Ok(tokens) =&gt; tokens,
            Err(_) =&gt; Self::estimate_tokens(content), // Fall back to basic estimation
        }
    }

    /// Check if file extension indicates binary content
    pub fn detect_binary_by_extension(extension: &amp;str) -&gt; bool {
        BINARY_EXTENSIONS.contains(&amp;format!(&quot;.{}&quot;, extension.to_lowercase()).as_str())
    }

    /// Classify file type based on path and language
    pub fn classify_file_type(path: &amp;str, language: &amp;Language, extension: &amp;str) -&gt; FileType {
        let path_lower = path.to_lowercase();

        // Test files
        if path_lower.contains(&quot;test&quot;) || path_lower.contains(&quot;spec&quot;) {
            return FileType::Test {
                language: language.clone(),
            };
        }

        // Documentation
        if language.is_documentation() {
            let format = match extension {
                &quot;md&quot; | &quot;markdown&quot; =&gt; DocumentationFormat::Markdown,
                &quot;html&quot; | &quot;htm&quot; =&gt; DocumentationFormat::Html,
                &quot;rst&quot; =&gt; DocumentationFormat::Rst,
                &quot;txt&quot; =&gt; DocumentationFormat::PlainText,
                _ =&gt; DocumentationFormat::Markdown,
            };
            return FileType::Documentation { format };
        }

        // Configuration
        if language.is_configuration() {
            let format = match extension {
                &quot;json&quot; =&gt; ConfigurationFormat::Json,
                &quot;yaml&quot; | &quot;yml&quot; =&gt; ConfigurationFormat::Yaml,
                &quot;toml&quot; =&gt; ConfigurationFormat::Toml,
                &quot;xml&quot; =&gt; ConfigurationFormat::Xml,
                &quot;ini&quot; =&gt; ConfigurationFormat::Ini,
                &quot;env&quot; =&gt; ConfigurationFormat::Dotenv,
                _ =&gt; ConfigurationFormat::Json,
            };
            return FileType::Configuration { format };
        }

        // Binary files
        if Self::detect_binary_by_extension(extension) {
            return FileType::Binary;
        }

        // Generated files (common patterns)
        if path_lower.contains(&quot;generated&quot;)
            || path_lower.contains(&quot;build&quot;)
            || path_lower.contains(&quot;dist&quot;)
            || path_lower.contains(&quot;target&quot;)
        {
            return FileType::Generated;
        }

        // Source code
        if language.is_programming() {
            return FileType::Source {
                language: language.clone(),
            };
        }

        FileType::Unknown
    }

    /// Get human-readable size
    pub fn human_size(&amp;self) -&gt; String {
        bytes_to_human(self.size)
    }

    /// Check if file should be included in analysis
    pub fn should_include(&amp;self) -&gt; bool {
        self.decision.should_include()
    }

    /// Get file name (last component of path)
    pub fn file_name(&amp;self) -&gt; Option&lt;&amp;str&gt; {
        self.path.file_name()?.to_str()
    }

    /// Get file stem (name without extension)
    pub fn file_stem(&amp;self) -&gt; Option&lt;&amp;str&gt; {
        self.path.file_stem()?.to_str()
    }

    /// Get file extension
    pub fn extension(&amp;self) -&gt; Option&lt;&amp;str&gt; {
        self.path.extension()?.to_str()
    }
}

/// Convert bytes to human-readable format
pub fn bytes_to_human(bytes: u64) -&gt; String {
    const UNITS: &amp;[&amp;str] = &amp;[&quot;B&quot;, &quot;KiB&quot;, &quot;MiB&quot;, &quot;GiB&quot;, &quot;TiB&quot;];
    const THRESHOLD: f64 = 1024.0;

    if bytes == 0 {
        return &quot;0 B&quot;.to_string();
    }

    let mut size = bytes as f64;
    let mut unit_idx = 0;

    while size &gt;= THRESHOLD &amp;&amp; unit_idx &lt; UNITS.len() - 1 {
        size /= THRESHOLD;
        unit_idx += 1;
    }

    if unit_idx == 0 {
        format!(&quot;{} {}&quot;, bytes, UNITS[unit_idx])
    } else {
        format!(&quot;{:.1} {}&quot;, size, UNITS[unit_idx])
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn test_language_detection() {
        assert_eq!(Language::from_extension(&quot;rs&quot;), Language::Rust);
        assert_eq!(Language::from_extension(&quot;py&quot;), Language::Python);
        assert_eq!(Language::from_extension(&quot;js&quot;), Language::JavaScript);
        assert_eq!(Language::from_extension(&quot;unknown&quot;), Language::Unknown);
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_binary_detection() {
        assert!(FileInfo::detect_binary_by_extension(&quot;png&quot;));
        assert!(FileInfo::detect_binary_by_extension(&quot;exe&quot;));

        assert!(!FileInfo::detect_binary_by_extension(&quot;py&quot;));
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_file_type_classification() {
        let rust_lang = Language::Rust;
        let py_lang = Language::Python;

        // Test Rust source files
        assert!(matches!(
            FileInfo::classify_file_type(&quot;src/lib.rs&quot;, &amp;rust_lang, &quot;rs&quot;),
            FileType::Source { .. }
        ));

        assert!(matches!(
            FileInfo::classify_file_type(&quot;scribe-rs/src/lib.rs&quot;, &amp;rust_lang, &quot;rs&quot;),
            FileType::Source { .. }
        ));

        // Test Python source files
        assert!(matches!(
            FileInfo::classify_file_type(&quot;script.py&quot;, &amp;py_lang, &quot;py&quot;),
            FileType::Source { .. }
        ));

        // Test that is_programming works correctly
        assert!(rust_lang.is_programming());
        assert!(py_lang.is_programming());
        assert!(!md_lang.is_programming());
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_integration_file_classification() {
        // Test the full pipeline: extension -&gt; language -&gt; file_type

        // Test Rust files
        let rust_lang = Language::from_extension(&quot;rs&quot;);
        assert_eq!(rust_lang, Language::Rust);
        assert!(rust_lang.is_programming());

        let rust_file_type = FileInfo::classify_file_type(&quot;src/lib.rs&quot;, &amp;rust_lang, &quot;rs&quot;);
        assert!(matches!(rust_file_type, FileType::Source { .. }));

        // Test Python files
        let py_lang = Language::from_extension(&quot;py&quot;);
        assert_eq!(py_lang, Language::Python);
        assert!(py_lang.is_programming());

        let py_file_type = FileInfo::classify_file_type(&quot;script.py&quot;, &amp;py_lang, &quot;py&quot;);
        assert!(matches!(py_file_type, FileType::Source { .. }));

        // Test that Unknown language doesn&#x27;t become Source
        let unknown_lang = Language::from_extension(&quot;xyz&quot;);
        assert_eq!(unknown_lang, Language::Unknown);
        assert!(!unknown_lang.is_programming());

        let unknown_file_type = FileInfo::classify_file_type(&quot;file.xyz&quot;, &amp;unknown_lang, &quot;xyz&quot;);
        assert!(matches!(unknown_file_type, FileType::Unknown));

        // Test Markdown files
        let md_lang = Language::from_extension(&quot;md&quot;);
        assert_eq!(md_lang, Language::Markdown);
        assert!(!md_lang.is_programming());

        let md_file_type = FileInfo::classify_file_type(&quot;README.md&quot;, &amp;md_lang, &quot;md&quot;);
        assert!(matches!(md_file_type, FileType::Documentation { .. }));
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_bytes_to_human() {
        assert_eq!(bytes_to_human(0), &quot;0 B&quot;);
        assert_eq!(bytes_to_human(512), &quot;512 B&quot;);
        assert_eq!(bytes_to_human(1024), &quot;1.0 KiB&quot;);
        assert_eq!(bytes_to_human(1536), &quot;1.5 KiB&quot;);
        assert_eq!(bytes_to_human(1048576), &quot;1.0 MiB&quot;);
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_token_estimation() {
        let content = &quot;Hello world, this is a test.&quot;;
        let tokens = FileInfo::estimate_tokens(content);
        assert!(tokens &gt; 0);
        assert!(tokens &lt; 20); // Should be reasonable estimate
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_render_decision() {
        let include = RenderDecision::include(&quot;valid file&quot;);
        assert!(include.should_include());
        assert_eq!(include.reason_category(), RenderDecisionCategory::Other);

        let exclude = RenderDecision::exclude(&quot;binary&quot;).with_context(&quot;detected by extension&quot;);
        assert!(!exclude.should_include());
        assert_eq!(exclude.reason_category(), RenderDecisionCategory::Binary);
        assert!(exclude.context.is_some());
    }
}

//! Configuration types and management for Scribe.
//!
//! Provides comprehensive configuration structures with validation,
//! serialization, and environment-based overrides.

use globset::{Glob, GlobSet, GlobSetBuilder};
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use std::collections::{HashMap, HashSet};
use std::hash::{Hash, Hasher};
use std::path::PathBuf;
use std::time::Duration;

use crate::error::{Result, ScribeError};
use crate::file::Language;
use crate::types::HeuristicWeights;

/// Main configuration structure for Scribe
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, Hash)]
pub struct Config {
    /// General settings
    pub general: GeneralConfig,

    /// File filtering configuration
    pub filtering: FilteringConfig,

    /// Analysis configuration
    pub analysis: AnalysisConfig,

    /// Scoring configuration
    pub scoring: ScoringConfig,

    /// Performance and resource limits
    pub performance: PerformanceConfig,

    /// Git integration settings
    pub git: GitConfig,

    /// Feature flags
    pub features: FeatureFlags,

    /// Output format configuration
    pub output: OutputConfig,
}

impl Default for Config {
    fn default() -&gt; Self {
        Self {
            general: GeneralConfig::default(),
            filtering: FilteringConfig::default(),
            analysis: AnalysisConfig::default(),
            scoring: ScoringConfig::default(),
            performance: PerformanceConfig::default(),
            git: GitConfig::default(),
            features: FeatureFlags::default(),
            output: OutputConfig::default(),
        }
    }
}

impl Config {
    /// Load configuration from a file
    pub fn load_from_file&lt;P: AsRef&lt;std::path::Path&gt;&gt;(path: P) -&gt; Result&lt;Self&gt; {
        let content = std::fs::read_to_string(path.as_ref()).map_err(|e| {
            ScribeError::path_with_source(&quot;Failed to read config file&quot;, path.as_ref(), e)
        })?;

        let config: Config = match path.as_ref().extension().and_then(|s| s.to_str()) {
            Some(&quot;json&quot;) =&gt; serde_json::from_str(&amp;content)?,
            Some(&quot;yaml&quot;) | Some(&quot;yml&quot;) =&gt; {
                return Err(ScribeError::config(&quot;YAML support not yet implemented&quot;));
            }
            Some(&quot;toml&quot;) =&gt; {
                return Err(ScribeError::config(&quot;TOML support not yet implemented&quot;));
            }
            _ =&gt; {
                return Err(ScribeError::config(
                    &quot;Unsupported config file format. Use .json, .yaml, or .toml&quot;,
                ));
            }
        };

        config.validate()?;
        Ok(config)
    }

    /// Save configuration to a file
    pub fn save_to_file&lt;P: AsRef&lt;std::path::Path&gt;&gt;(&amp;self, path: P) -&gt; Result&lt;()&gt; {
        let content = match path.as_ref().extension().and_then(|s| s.to_str()) {
            Some(&quot;json&quot;) =&gt; serde_json::to_string_pretty(self)?,
            Some(&quot;yaml&quot;) | Some(&quot;yml&quot;) =&gt; {
                return Err(ScribeError::config(&quot;YAML support not yet implemented&quot;));
            }
            Some(&quot;toml&quot;) =&gt; {
                return Err(ScribeError::config(&quot;TOML support not yet implemented&quot;));
            }
            _ =&gt; {
                return Err(ScribeError::config(
                    &quot;Unsupported config file format. Use .json, .yaml, or .toml&quot;,
                ));
            }
        };

        std::fs::write(path.as_ref(), content).map_err(|e| {
            ScribeError::path_with_source(&quot;Failed to write config file&quot;, path.as_ref(), e)
        })?;

        Ok(())
    }

    /// Validate the configuration
    pub fn validate(&amp;self) -&gt; Result&lt;()&gt; {
        self.general.validate()?;
        self.filtering.validate()?;
        self.analysis.validate()?;
        self.scoring.validate()?;
        self.performance.validate()?;
        self.git.validate()?;
        self.features.validate()?;
        self.output.validate()?;
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Merge with another configuration (other takes priority)
    pub fn merge_with(mut self, other: Config) -&gt; Self {
        // Note: This is a simplified merge - in practice you might want
        // more sophisticated merging logic
        self.general = other.general;
        self.filtering = other.filtering;
        self.analysis = other.analysis;
        self.scoring = other.scoring;
        self.performance = other.performance;
        self.git = other.git;
        self.features = other.features;
        self.output = other.output;
        self
    }

    /// Create a configuration hash for cache invalidation
    /// This is now highly optimized using direct hashing instead of JSON serialization
    pub fn compute_hash(&amp;self) -&gt; String {
        use std::collections::hash_map::DefaultHasher;

        let mut hasher = DefaultHasher::new();
        self.hash(&amp;mut hasher);
        format!(&quot;{:x}&quot;, hasher.finish())
    }
}

/// General application settings
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct GeneralConfig {
    /// Verbosity level (0-4)
    pub verbosity: u8,

    /// Enable progress reporting
    pub show_progress: bool,

    /// Enable colored output
    pub use_colors: bool,

    /// Maximum number of worker threads (0 = auto-detect)
    pub max_threads: usize,

    /// Working directory override
    pub working_dir: Option&lt;PathBuf&gt;,
}

// Custom Hash implementation for GeneralConfig to handle PathBuf properly
impl Hash for GeneralConfig {
    fn hash&lt;H: Hasher&gt;(&amp;self, state: &amp;mut H) {
        self.verbosity.hash(state);
        self.show_progress.hash(state);
        self.use_colors.hash(state);
        self.max_threads.hash(state);
        // Hash PathBuf as string for platform consistency
        if let Some(ref path) = self.working_dir {
            path.to_string_lossy().hash(state);
        } else {
            None::&lt;String&gt;.hash(state);
        }
    }
}

impl Default for GeneralConfig {
    fn default() -&gt; Self {
        Self {
            verbosity: 1,
            show_progress: true,
            use_colors: true,
            max_threads: 0, // Auto-detect
            working_dir: None,
        }
    }
}

impl GeneralConfig {
    fn validate(&amp;self) -&gt; Result&lt;()&gt; {
        if self.verbosity &gt; 4 {
            return Err(ScribeError::config_field(
                &quot;Verbosity must be between 0 and 4&quot;,
                &quot;verbosity&quot;,
            ));
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}

/// File filtering configuration
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct FilteringConfig {
    /// Include patterns (glob format)
    pub include_patterns: Vec&lt;String&gt;,

    /// Exclude patterns (glob format)
    pub exclude_patterns: Vec&lt;String&gt;,

    /// Maximum file size in bytes
    pub max_file_size: u64,

    /// Minimum file size in bytes
    pub min_file_size: u64,

    /// Languages to include (empty = all)
    pub include_languages: HashSet&lt;Language&gt;,

    /// Languages to exclude
    pub exclude_languages: HashSet&lt;Language&gt;,

    /// Whether to follow symbolic links
    pub follow_symlinks: bool,

    /// Whether to include hidden files (starting with .)
    pub include_hidden: bool,

    /// Whether to respect .gitignore files
    pub respect_gitignore: bool,

    /// Additional ignore files to respect
    pub ignore_files: Vec&lt;PathBuf&gt;,
}

// Custom Hash implementation for FilteringConfig to handle PathBuf properly
impl Hash for FilteringConfig {
    fn hash&lt;H: Hasher&gt;(&amp;self, state: &amp;mut H) {
        self.include_patterns.hash(state);
        self.exclude_patterns.hash(state);
        self.max_file_size.hash(state);
        self.min_file_size.hash(state);
        // Hash HashSet contents by iterating over sorted elements
        let mut include_langs: Vec&lt;_&gt; = self.include_languages.iter().collect();
        include_langs.sort();
        include_langs.hash(state);

        let mut exclude_langs: Vec&lt;_&gt; = self.exclude_languages.iter().collect();
        exclude_langs.sort();
        exclude_langs.hash(state);
        self.follow_symlinks.hash(state);
        self.include_hidden.hash(state);
        self.respect_gitignore.hash(state);
        // Hash PathBuf vector as string vector for platform consistency
        for path in &amp;self.ignore_files {
            path.to_string_lossy().hash(state);
        }
    }
}

impl Default for FilteringConfig {
    fn default() -&gt; Self {
        Self {
            include_patterns: vec![],
            exclude_patterns: vec![
                &quot;node_modules/**&quot;.to_string(),
                &quot;target/**&quot;.to_string(),
                &quot;.git/**&quot;.to_string(),
                &quot;build/**&quot;.to_string(),
                &quot;dist/**&quot;.to_string(),
                &quot;__pycache__/**&quot;.to_string(),
                &quot;*.pyc&quot;.to_string(),
                &quot;.DS_Store&quot;.to_string(),
            ],
            max_file_size: 10 * 1024 * 1024, // 10MB
            min_file_size: 0,
            include_languages: HashSet::new(), // Empty = all languages
            exclude_languages: HashSet::new(),
            follow_symlinks: false,
            include_hidden: false,
            respect_gitignore: true,
            ignore_files: vec![],
        }
    }
}

impl FilteringConfig {
    fn validate(&amp;self) -&gt; Result&lt;()&gt; {
        if self.max_file_size &lt; self.min_file_size {
            return Err(ScribeError::config(
                &quot;max_file_size must be &gt;= min_file_size&quot;,
            ));
        }

        // Validate glob patterns
        for pattern in &amp;self.include_patterns {
            Glob::new(pattern).map_err(|e| {
                ScribeError::pattern(format!(&quot;Invalid include pattern: {}&quot;, e), pattern)
            })?;
        }

        for pattern in &amp;self.exclude_patterns {
            Glob::new(pattern).map_err(|e| {
                ScribeError::pattern(format!(&quot;Invalid exclude pattern: {}&quot;, e), pattern)
            })?;
        }

        Ok(())
    }

    /// Build a GlobSet for include patterns
    pub fn build_include_set(&amp;self) -&gt; Result&lt;Option&lt;GlobSet&gt;&gt; {
        if self.include_patterns.is_empty() {
            return Ok(None);
        }

        let mut builder = GlobSetBuilder::new();
        for pattern in &amp;self.include_patterns {
            builder.add(Glob::new(pattern)?);
        }
        Ok(Some(builder.build()?))
    }

    /// Build a GlobSet for exclude patterns
    pub fn build_exclude_set(&amp;self) -&gt; Result&lt;GlobSet&gt; {
        let mut builder = GlobSetBuilder::new();
        for pattern in &amp;self.exclude_patterns {
            builder.add(Glob::new(pattern)?);
        }
        Ok(builder.build()?)
    }
}

/// Analysis configuration
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct AnalysisConfig {
    /// Whether to analyze file content (not just metadata)
    pub analyze_content: bool,

    /// Whether to compute token estimates
    pub compute_tokens: bool,

    /// Whether to count lines
    pub count_lines: bool,

    /// Whether to detect binary files by content (in addition to extension)
    pub detect_binary_content: bool,

    /// Languages that require special handling
    pub language_overrides: HashMap&lt;String, Language&gt;,

    /// Custom file type mappings (extension -&gt; language)
    pub custom_extensions: HashMap&lt;String, Language&gt;,

    /// Whether to cache analysis results
    pub enable_caching: bool,

    /// Cache directory (relative to project root or absolute)
    pub cache_dir: PathBuf,

    /// Cache TTL in seconds
    pub cache_ttl: u64,

    /// Token budget for intelligent file selection
    pub token_budget: Option&lt;usize&gt;,
}

// Custom Hash implementation for AnalysisConfig to handle PathBuf properly
impl Hash for AnalysisConfig {
    fn hash&lt;H: Hasher&gt;(&amp;self, state: &amp;mut H) {
        self.analyze_content.hash(state);
        self.compute_tokens.hash(state);
        self.count_lines.hash(state);
        self.detect_binary_content.hash(state);
        // Hash HashMap contents by iterating over sorted key-value pairs
        let mut lang_overrides: Vec&lt;_&gt; = self.language_overrides.iter().collect();
        lang_overrides.sort_by_key(|(k, _)| *k);
        lang_overrides.hash(state);

        let mut custom_exts: Vec&lt;_&gt; = self.custom_extensions.iter().collect();
        custom_exts.sort_by_key(|(k, _)| *k);
        custom_exts.hash(state);
        self.enable_caching.hash(state);
        // Hash PathBuf as string for platform consistency
        self.cache_dir.to_string_lossy().hash(state);
        self.cache_ttl.hash(state);
        self.token_budget.hash(state);
    }
}

impl Default for AnalysisConfig {
    fn default() -&gt; Self {
        Self {
            analyze_content: true,
            compute_tokens: true,
            count_lines: true,
            detect_binary_content: false,
            language_overrides: HashMap::new(),
            custom_extensions: HashMap::new(),
            enable_caching: false,
            cache_dir: PathBuf::from(&quot;.scribe-cache&quot;),
            cache_ttl: 3600, // 1 hour
            token_budget: None,
        }
    }
}

impl AnalysisConfig {
    fn validate(&amp;self) -&gt; Result&lt;()&gt; {
        if self.cache_ttl == 0 {
            return Err(ScribeError::config_field(
                &quot;cache_ttl must be &gt; 0&quot;,
                &quot;cache_ttl&quot;,
            ));
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}

/// Scoring system configuration
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct ScoringConfig {
    /// Heuristic weights
    pub weights: HeuristicWeights,

    /// Whether to enable advanced scoring features
    pub enable_advanced: bool,

    /// Custom scoring rules
    pub custom_rules: Vec&lt;CustomScoringRule&gt;,

    /// Minimum score threshold for inclusion
    pub min_score_threshold: f64,

    /// Maximum number of files to return (0 = unlimited)
    pub max_results: usize,

    /// Whether to normalize scores to 0-1 range
    pub normalize_scores: bool,
}

// Custom Hash implementation for ScoringConfig
impl Hash for ScoringConfig {
    fn hash&lt;H: Hasher&gt;(&amp;self, state: &amp;mut H) {
        self.weights.hash(state);
        self.enable_advanced.hash(state);
        self.custom_rules.hash(state);
        // Hash f64 as bits for consistent hashing
        self.min_score_threshold.to_bits().hash(state);
        self.max_results.hash(state);
        self.normalize_scores.hash(state);
    }
}

impl Default for ScoringConfig {
    fn default() -&gt; Self {
        Self {
            weights: HeuristicWeights::default(),
            enable_advanced: false,
            custom_rules: vec![],
            min_score_threshold: 0.0,
            max_results: 0, // Unlimited
            normalize_scores: true,
        }
    }
}

impl ScoringConfig {
    fn validate(&amp;self) -&gt; Result&lt;()&gt; {
        if self.min_score_threshold &lt; 0.0 || self.min_score_threshold &gt; 1.0 {
            return Err(ScribeError::config_field(
                &quot;min_score_threshold must be between 0.0 and 1.0&quot;,
                &quot;min_score_threshold&quot;,
            ));
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}

/// Custom scoring rule
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, Hash)]
pub struct CustomScoringRule {
    /// Rule name/description
    pub name: String,

    /// File pattern to match
    pub pattern: String,

    /// Score modifier type
    pub modifier: ScoreModifier,
}

/// Score modifier operations
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum ScoreModifier {
    /// Add a constant value
    Add(f64),
    /// Multiply by a factor
    Multiply(f64),
    /// Set to a specific value
    Set(f64),
    /// Add bonus based on condition
    ConditionalBonus { condition: String, bonus: f64 },
}

// Custom Hash implementation for ScoreModifier to handle f64 fields properly
impl Hash for ScoreModifier {
    fn hash&lt;H: Hasher&gt;(&amp;self, state: &amp;mut H) {
        match self {
            ScoreModifier::Add(value) =&gt; {
                0u8.hash(state); // discriminant
                value.to_bits().hash(state);
            }
            ScoreModifier::Multiply(value) =&gt; {
                1u8.hash(state); // discriminant
                value.to_bits().hash(state);
            }
            ScoreModifier::Set(value) =&gt; {
                2u8.hash(state); // discriminant
                value.to_bits().hash(state);
            }
            ScoreModifier::ConditionalBonus { condition, bonus } =&gt; {
                3u8.hash(state); // discriminant
                condition.hash(state);
                bonus.to_bits().hash(state);
            }
        }
    }
}

        }

        }

impl FeatureFlags {
    fn validate(&amp;self) -&gt; Result&lt;()&gt; {
        // Currently no validation needed
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Check if any V2 features are enabled
    pub fn has_v2_features(&amp;self) -&gt; bool {
        self.centrality_enabled || self.entrypoint_detection || self.examples_analysis
    }

    /// Get list of enabled feature names
    pub fn enabled_features(&amp;self) -&gt; Vec&lt;&amp;&#x27;static str&gt; {
        let mut features = Vec::new();

        if self.centrality_enabled {
            features.push(&quot;centrality&quot;);

        if self.entrypoint_detection {
            features.push(&quot;entrypoint_detection&quot;);

        if self.examples_analysis {
            features.push(&quot;examples_analysis&quot;);
        }
        if self.semantic_analysis {
            features.push(&quot;semantic_analysis&quot;);
        }
        if self.ml_features {
            features.push(&quot;ml_features&quot;);
        }
        if self.experimental_scoring {
            features.push(&quot;experimental_scoring&quot;);
        }
        if self.scaling_enabled {
            features.push(&quot;scaling&quot;);
        }

        features
    }
}

/// Output format configuration
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, Hash)]
pub struct OutputConfig {
    /// Output format
    pub format: OutputFormat,

    /// Whether to include file content in output
    pub include_content: bool,

    /// Whether to include detailed scores breakdown
    pub include_score_breakdown: bool,

    /// Whether to include repository statistics
    pub include_repo_stats: bool,

    /// Whether to sort results by score
    pub sort_by_score: bool,

    /// Pretty print JSON output
    pub pretty_json: bool,

    /// Custom output fields to include
    pub custom_fields: Vec&lt;String&gt;,
}

/// Output format options
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize, Hash)]
pub enum OutputFormat {
    Json,
    JsonLines,
    Csv,
    Table,
    Summary,
}

impl Default for OutputConfig {
    fn default() -&gt; Self {
        Self {
            format: OutputFormat::Json,
            include_content: false,
            include_score_breakdown: true,
            include_repo_stats: true,
            sort_by_score: true,
            pretty_json: true,
            custom_fields: vec![],
        }
    }
}

impl OutputConfig {
    fn validate(&amp;self) -&gt; Result&lt;()&gt; {
        // Currently no validation needed
        Ok(())
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use tempfile::NamedTempFile;

    #[test]
    fn test_config_defaults() {
        let config = Config::default();
        assert_eq!(config.general.verbosity, 1);
        assert!(config.filtering.respect_gitignore);
        assert!(config.git.enabled);
        assert!(!config.features.centrality_enabled);
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_config_validation() {
        let mut config = Config::default();
        assert!(config.validate().is_ok());

        // Test invalid verbosity
        config.general.verbosity = 10;
        assert!(config.validate().is_err());

        // Reset and test invalid file sizes
        config = Config::default();
        config.filtering.max_file_size = 100;
        config.filtering.min_file_size = 200;
        assert!(config.validate().is_err());
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_config_file_io() {
        let config = Config::default();
        let temp_file = NamedTempFile::new().unwrap();

        // Test JSON serialization
        let json_path = temp_file.path().with_extension(&quot;json&quot;);
        config.save_to_file(&amp;json_path).unwrap();
        let loaded_config = Config::load_from_file(&amp;json_path).unwrap();

        assert_eq!(config.general.verbosity, loaded_config.general.verbosity);
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_filtering_patterns() {
        let mut config = FilteringConfig::default();
        config.include_patterns.push(&quot;*.rs&quot;.to_string());
        config.exclude_patterns.push(&quot;target/**&quot;.to_string());

        assert!(config.validate().is_ok());

        let include_set = config.build_include_set().unwrap();
        assert!(include_set.is_some());

        let exclude_set = config.build_exclude_set().unwrap();
        assert!(exclude_set.is_match(&quot;target/debug/file.o&quot;));
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_feature_flags() {
        let mut flags = FeatureFlags::default();
        assert!(!flags.has_v2_features());
        assert!(flags.enabled_features().is_empty());

        flags.centrality_enabled = true;
        flags.entrypoint_detection = true;

        assert!(flags.has_v2_features());
        let enabled = flags.enabled_features();
        assert!(enabled.contains(&amp;&quot;centrality&quot;));
        assert!(enabled.contains(&amp;&quot;entrypoint_detection&quot;));
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_performance_config_timeouts() {
        let config = PerformanceConfig::default();
        assert_eq!(config.analysis_timeout_duration(), Duration::from_secs(30));
        assert_eq!(config.global_timeout_duration(), Duration::from_secs(300));
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_config_hash() {
        let config1 = Config::default();
        let config2 = Config::default();

        let hash1 = config1.compute_hash();
        let hash2 = config2.compute_hash();

        assert_eq!(hash1, hash2);

        let mut config3 = Config::default();
        config3.general.verbosity = 2;
        let hash3 = config3.compute_hash();

        assert_ne!(hash1, hash3);
    }
}

//! Core crate for Scribe

//! # Scribe Core
//!
//! Core types, utilities, and foundational components for the Scribe code analysis library.
//! This crate provides the fundamental data structures and traits used across all other
//! Scribe crates.
//!
//! ## Features
//!
//! - **Comprehensive Error Handling**: Rich error types with proper context and error chaining
//! - **File Analysis**: File metadata, language detection, and classification
//! - **Scoring System**: Heuristic scoring components and configurable weights
//! - **Configuration**: Flexible configuration with validation and serialization
//! - **Extensibility**: Traits for custom analyzers, scorers, and formatters
//! - **Utilities**: Common functions for path manipulation, string processing, and more
//!
//! ## Basic Usage
//!
//! ```rust
//! use scribe_core::{Config, FileInfo, ScoreComponents, Result};
//! use std::path::Path;
//!
//! # fn main() -&gt; Result&lt;()&gt; {
//! // Load configuration
//! let config = Config::default();
//!
//! // Analyze a file (this would typically be done by other crates)
//! // let file_info = analyze_file(Path::new(&quot;src/lib.rs&quot;), &amp;config)?;
//! # Ok(())
//! # }
//! ```

// Core modules

pub use traits::{

/// Current version of the Scribe library
pub const VERSION: &amp;str = env!(&quot;CARGO_PKG_VERSION&quot;);

/// Library metadata and build information
pub mod meta {
    /// Library name
    pub const NAME: &amp;str = env!(&quot;CARGO_PKG_NAME&quot;);

    /// Library version
    pub const VERSION: &amp;str = env!(&quot;CARGO_PKG_VERSION&quot;);

    /// Library description
    pub const DESCRIPTION: &amp;str = env!(&quot;CARGO_PKG_DESCRIPTION&quot;);

    /// Authors
    pub const AUTHORS: &amp;str = env!(&quot;CARGO_PKG_AUTHORS&quot;);

    /// Repository URL
    pub const REPOSITORY: &amp;str = env!(&quot;CARGO_PKG_REPOSITORY&quot;);

    /// License
    pub const LICENSE: &amp;str = env!(&quot;CARGO_PKG_LICENSE&quot;);

    /// Target triple (if available)
    pub const TARGET: Option&lt;&amp;str&gt; = option_env!(&quot;TARGET&quot;);

    /// Build timestamp (if available)
    pub const BUILD_TIMESTAMP: Option&lt;&amp;str&gt; = option_env!(&quot;BUILD_TIMESTAMP&quot;);

    /// Git commit hash (if available)
    pub const GIT_HASH: Option&lt;&amp;str&gt; = option_env!(&quot;GIT_HASH&quot;);

    /// Get library information as a formatted string
    pub fn info() -&gt; String {
        format!(&quot;{} v{} - {}&quot;, NAME, VERSION, DESCRIPTION)
    }

    /// Get detailed build information
    pub fn build_info() -&gt; String {
        let mut info = format!(&quot;{} v{}&quot;, NAME, VERSION);

        if let Some(target) = TARGET {
            info.push_str(&amp;format!(&quot; ({})&quot;, target));
        }

        if let Some(git_hash) = GIT_HASH {
            info.push_str(&amp;format!(&quot; [{}]&quot;, &amp;git_hash[..8]));
        }

        if let Some(timestamp) = BUILD_TIMESTAMP {
            info.push_str(&amp;format!(&quot; built on {}&quot;, timestamp));
        }

        info
    }
}

//! Error handling for the Scribe library.
//!
//! Provides comprehensive error types with proper context and error chaining
//! for all Scribe operations.

use std::io;
use std::path::PathBuf;
use thiserror::Error;

/// Type alias for Results using ScribeError
pub type Result&lt;T&gt; = std::result::Result&lt;T, ScribeError&gt;;

/// Comprehensive error type for all Scribe operations
#[derive(Error, Debug)]
pub enum ScribeError {
    /// I/O related errors (file system operations)
    #[error(&quot;I/O error: {message}&quot;)]
    Io {
        message: String,
        #[source]
        source: io::Error,
    },

    /// Path-related errors (invalid paths, path resolution issues)
    #[error(&quot;Path error: {message} (path: {path:?})&quot;)]
    Path {
        message: String,
        path: PathBuf,
        #[source]
        source: Option&lt;io::Error&gt;,
    },

    /// Git repository errors
    #[error(&quot;Git error: {message}&quot;)]
    Git {
        message: String,
        #[source]
        source: Option&lt;Box&lt;dyn std::error::Error + Send + Sync&gt;&gt;,
    },

    /// Configuration errors (invalid settings, missing required config)
    #[error(&quot;Configuration error: {message}&quot;)]
    Config {
        message: String,
        field: Option&lt;String&gt;,
    },

    /// File analysis errors (parsing, language detection, etc.)
    #[error(&quot;Analysis error: {message} (file: {file:?})&quot;)]
    Analysis {
        message: String,
        file: PathBuf,
        #[source]
        source: Option&lt;Box&lt;dyn std::error::Error + Send + Sync&gt;&gt;,
    },

    /// Scoring and heuristic computation errors
    #[error(&quot;Scoring error: {message}&quot;)]
    Scoring {
        message: String,
        context: Option&lt;String&gt;,
    },

    /// Graph computation errors (centrality, dependency analysis)
    #[error(&quot;Graph error: {message}&quot;)]
    Graph {
        message: String,
        details: Option&lt;String&gt;,
    },

    /// Pattern matching errors (glob patterns, regex, etc.)
    #[error(&quot;Pattern error: {message} (pattern: {pattern})&quot;)]
    Pattern {
        message: String,
        pattern: String,
        #[source]
        source: Option&lt;Box&lt;dyn std::error::Error + Send + Sync&gt;&gt;,
    },

    /// Serialization/deserialization errors
    #[error(&quot;Serialization error: {message}&quot;)]
    Serialization {
        message: String,
        #[source]
        source: Option&lt;Box&lt;dyn std::error::Error + Send + Sync&gt;&gt;,
    },

    /// Thread pool or concurrency errors
    #[error(&quot;Concurrency error: {message}&quot;)]
    Concurrency {
        message: String,
        #[source]
        source: Option&lt;Box&lt;dyn std::error::Error + Send + Sync&gt;&gt;,
    },

    /// Resource limit exceeded (memory, time, file size)
    #[error(&quot;Resource limit exceeded: {message} (limit: {limit}, actual: {actual})&quot;)]
    ResourceLimit {
        message: String,
        limit: u64,
        actual: u64,
    },

    /// Invalid input or operation
    #[error(&quot;Invalid operation: {message}&quot;)]
    InvalidOperation { message: String, operation: String },

    /// Parse errors (AST parsing, tree-sitter failures)
    #[error(&quot;Parse error: {message} (file: {file:?})&quot;)]
    Parse {
        message: String,
        file: Option&lt;PathBuf&gt;,
        #[source]
        source: Option&lt;Box&lt;dyn std::error::Error + Send + Sync&gt;&gt;,
    },

    /// Tokenization errors (tiktoken integration, encoding issues)
    #[error(&quot;Tokenization error: {message}&quot;)]
    Tokenization {
        message: String,
        #[source]
        source: Option&lt;Box&lt;dyn std::error::Error + Send + Sync&gt;&gt;,
    },

    /// Scaling optimization errors (when scaling feature is enabled)
    #[cfg(feature = &quot;scaling&quot;)]
    #[error(&quot;Scaling error: {message}&quot;)]
    Scaling {
        message: String,
        #[source]
        source: Option&lt;Box&lt;dyn std::error::Error + Send + Sync&gt;&gt;,
    },

    /// General internal errors (should not occur in normal operation)
    #[error(&quot;Internal error: {message}&quot;)]
    Internal {
        message: String,
        location: Option&lt;String&gt;,
    },
}

impl ScribeError {
    /// Create a new I/O error with context
    pub fn io&lt;S: Into&lt;String&gt;&gt;(message: S, source: io::Error) -&gt; Self {
        Self::Io {
            message: message.into(),
            source,
        }
    }

    /// Create a new path error with context
    pub fn path&lt;S: Into&lt;String&gt;, P: Into&lt;PathBuf&gt;&gt;(message: S, path: P) -&gt; Self {
        Self::Path {
            message: message.into(),
            path: path.into(),
            source: None,
        }
    }

    /// Create a new path error with source error
    pub fn path_with_source&lt;S: Into&lt;String&gt;, P: Into&lt;PathBuf&gt;&gt;(
        message: S,
        path: P,
        source: io::Error,
    ) -&gt; Self {
        Self::Path {
            message: message.into(),
            path: path.into(),
            source: Some(source),
        }
    }

    /// Create a new git error
    pub fn git&lt;S: Into&lt;String&gt;&gt;(message: S) -&gt; Self {
        Self::Git {
            message: message.into(),
            source: None,
        }
    }

    /// Create a new configuration error
    pub fn config&lt;S: Into&lt;String&gt;&gt;(message: S) -&gt; Self {
        Self::Config {
            message: message.into(),
            field: None,
        }
    }

    /// Create a new configuration error with field context
    pub fn config_field&lt;S: Into&lt;String&gt;, F: Into&lt;String&gt;&gt;(message: S, field: F) -&gt; Self {
        Self::Config {
            message: message.into(),
            field: Some(field.into()),
        }
    }

    /// Create a new analysis error
    pub fn analysis&lt;S: Into&lt;String&gt;, P: Into&lt;PathBuf&gt;&gt;(message: S, file: P) -&gt; Self {
        Self::Analysis {
            message: message.into(),
            file: file.into(),
            source: None,
        }
    }

    /// Create a new scoring error
    pub fn scoring&lt;S: Into&lt;String&gt;&gt;(message: S) -&gt; Self {
        Self::Scoring {
            message: message.into(),
            context: None,
        }
    }

    /// Create a new scoring error with context
    pub fn scoring_with_context&lt;S: Into&lt;String&gt;, C: Into&lt;String&gt;&gt;(message: S, context: C) -&gt; Self {
        Self::Scoring {
            message: message.into(),
            context: Some(context.into()),
        }
    }

    /// Create a new graph computation error
    pub fn graph&lt;S: Into&lt;String&gt;&gt;(message: S) -&gt; Self {
        Self::Graph {
            message: message.into(),
            details: None,
        }
    }

    /// Create a new pattern error
    pub fn pattern&lt;S: Into&lt;String&gt;, P: Into&lt;String&gt;&gt;(message: S, pattern: P) -&gt; Self {
        Self::Pattern {
            message: message.into(),
            pattern: pattern.into(),
            source: None,
        }
    }

    /// Create a new resource limit error
    pub fn resource_limit&lt;S: Into&lt;String&gt;&gt;(message: S, limit: u64, actual: u64) -&gt; Self {
        Self::ResourceLimit {
            message: message.into(),
            limit,
            actual,
        }
    }

    /// Create a new invalid operation error
    pub fn invalid_operation&lt;S: Into&lt;String&gt;, O: Into&lt;String&gt;&gt;(message: S, operation: O) -&gt; Self {
        Self::InvalidOperation {
            message: message.into(),
            operation: operation.into(),
        }
    }

    /// Create a new internal error
    pub fn internal&lt;S: Into&lt;String&gt;&gt;(message: S) -&gt; Self {
        Self::Internal {
            message: message.into(),
            location: None,
        }
    }

    /// Create a new parse error
    pub fn parse&lt;S: Into&lt;String&gt;&gt;(message: S) -&gt; Self {
        Self::Parse {
            message: message.into(),
            file: None,
            source: None,
        }
    }

    /// Create a new parse error with file context
    pub fn parse_file&lt;S: Into&lt;String&gt;, P: Into&lt;PathBuf&gt;&gt;(message: S, file: P) -&gt; Self {
        Self::Parse {
            message: message.into(),
            file: Some(file.into()),
            source: None,
        }
    }

    /// Create a new parse error with source error
    pub fn parse_with_source&lt;S: Into&lt;String&gt;&gt;(
        message: S,
        source: Box&lt;dyn std::error::Error + Send + Sync&gt;,
    ) -&gt; Self {
        Self::Parse {
            message: message.into(),
            file: None,
            source: Some(source),
        }
    }

    /// Create a new tokenization error
    pub fn tokenization&lt;S: Into&lt;String&gt;&gt;(message: S) -&gt; Self {
        Self::Tokenization {
            message: message.into(),
            source: None,
        }
    }

    /// Create a new tokenization error with source
    pub fn tokenization_with_source&lt;S: Into&lt;String&gt;&gt;(
        message: S,
        source: Box&lt;dyn std::error::Error + Send + Sync&gt;,
    ) -&gt; Self {
        Self::Tokenization {
            message: message.into(),
            source: Some(source),
        }
    }

    /// Create a new scaling error (when scaling feature is enabled)
    #[cfg(feature = &quot;scaling&quot;)]
    pub fn scaling&lt;S: Into&lt;String&gt;&gt;(message: S) -&gt; Self {
        Self::Scaling {
            message: message.into(),
            source: None,
        }
    }

    /// Create a new scaling error with source (when scaling feature is enabled)
    #[cfg(feature = &quot;scaling&quot;)]
    pub fn scaling_with_source&lt;S: Into&lt;String&gt;&gt;(
        message: S,
        source: Box&lt;dyn std::error::Error + Send + Sync&gt;,
    ) -&gt; Self {
        Self::Scaling {
            message: message.into(),
            source: Some(source),
        }
    }

    /// Create a new internal error with location
    pub fn internal_with_location&lt;S: Into&lt;String&gt;, L: Into&lt;String&gt;&gt;(
        message: S,
        location: L,
    ) -&gt; Self {
        Self::Internal {
            message: message.into(),
            location: Some(location.into()),
        }
    }
}

impl From&lt;io::Error&gt; for ScribeError {
    fn from(error: io::Error) -&gt; Self {
        Self::io(&quot;I/O operation failed&quot;, error)
    }
}

impl From&lt;serde_json::Error&gt; for ScribeError {
    fn from(error: serde_json::Error) -&gt; Self {
        Self::Serialization {
            message: &quot;JSON serialization failed&quot;.to_string(),
            source: Some(Box::new(error)),
        }
    }
}

impl From&lt;globset::Error&gt; for ScribeError {
    fn from(error: globset::Error) -&gt; Self {
        Self::Pattern {
            message: &quot;Glob pattern compilation failed&quot;.to_string(),
            pattern: &quot;unknown&quot;.to_string(),
            source: Some(Box::new(error)),
        }
    }
}

impl From&lt;ignore::Error&gt; for ScribeError {
    fn from(error: ignore::Error) -&gt; Self {
        Self::Pattern {
            message: &quot;Ignore pattern error&quot;.to_string(),
            pattern: &quot;unknown&quot;.to_string(),
            source: Some(Box::new(error)),
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use std::path::Path;

    #[test]
    fn test_error_creation() {
        let err = ScribeError::path(&quot;Test path error&quot;, Path::new(&quot;/test/path&quot;));
        assert!(err.to_string().contains(&quot;Test path error&quot;));
        assert!(err.to_string().contains(&quot;/test/path&quot;));
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_io_error_conversion() {
        let io_err = io::Error::new(io::ErrorKind::NotFound, &quot;File not found&quot;);
        let scribe_err = ScribeError::from(io_err);
        match scribe_err {
            ScribeError::Io { message, .. } =&gt; {
                assert_eq!(message, &quot;I/O operation failed&quot;);
            }
            _ =&gt; panic!(&quot;Expected Io error variant&quot;),
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_resource_limit_error() {
        let err = ScribeError::resource_limit(&quot;File too large&quot;, 1000, 2000);
        let msg = err.to_string();
        assert!(msg.contains(&quot;limit: 1000&quot;));
        assert!(msg.contains(&quot;actual: 2000&quot;));
    }
}
